examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: One who knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not treat the illusion as one thing and the aggregates as another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in total peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever here knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not make illusion one thing and the aggregates another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in perfect peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: मायोपमां य इह जानति पञ्च स्कन्धां न च माय अन्य न च स्कन्ध करोति अन्यान् । नानात्वसंज्ञविगतो उपशान्तचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, having heard that these phenomena are like emanations and illusions, Is without doubt and repeatedly practices the training, Know that such a person has long since entered the Mahayana, And has performed service to many tens of billions of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whoever, having heard that these dharmas are like emanations and illusions, Without doubt, trains and continuously applies themselves, That being should be known to have entered the Great Vehicle long ago, And to have served many tens of millions of billions of Buddhas.
examples.sa: चिरयानप्रस्थितु स वेदयितव्य सत्त्वो बहुबुद्धकोटिनयुतेहि कृताधिकारो । यो श्रुत्व धर्मि इमि निर्मितमायकल्पां न च काङ्क्षते अयु प्रयुज्यति शिक्षमाणः ॥

examples.dm: In the midst of a crowd, a conjured person does not think, "I must please these people," and yet they perform that very action; Although they are seen displaying various miraculous feats, They possess no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.gm: In the midst of people, an illusory person does not think, "I will please these people," yet still pleases them; Though seen to display various miracles, They have no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.sa: यथ मायकारपुरुषस्य न एव भोति ते शिष्य मां जनत सो च करोति कार्यम् । पश्यन्ति तं विविध कार्यु निदर्शयन्तं न च तस्य कायु न पि चित्त न नामधेयम् ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: When the leaves have emerged on the trees during the fine springtime, Before long, the branches will produce foliage, fruit, and flowers. Whoever receives this Perfection of Wisdom into their hands, Before long, will attain the awakening of the Guides.
examples.gm: In the excellent springtime, when trees shed their leaves, Before long, the branches will produce leaves, fruits, and flowers; Whoever attains this perfection of wisdom in their hands Will attain the enlightenment of the Leaders before long.
examples.sa: सुवसन्ति कालि पतिते तृणपत्रशाखा नचिरेण पत्रफलपुष्प समागमन्ति । प्रज्ञाय पारमित यस्यिमु हस्तप्राप्ता नचिरेण बोधिवर प्राप्स्यति नायकानाम् ॥

examples.dm: When this is explained, some will harbor doubts, thinking: "The Leader has not even mentioned my name here; He has not mentioned my family, my level, or my lineage." This is the work of Māra, causing them to reject it rather than listen.
examples.gm: When this is taught, some will harbor doubts, thinking, 'The Leader has not fully pronounced my name here, Nor fully pronounced my lineage, birthplace, or clan.' They will not listen and will abandon it; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: काङ्क्षा च केषचि भविष्यति भाषमाणे न ममात्र नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन । न च जाति भूमि परिकीर्तितु नापि गोत्रं न च सो श्रुणिष्यति क्षिपिष्यति मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Form is not wisdom, and wisdom is not found within form. Consciousness, perception, feeling, and intention— These are not wisdom, nor is wisdom present within them. This is identical to the element of space, without any distinction.
examples.gm: Form is not wisdom, in form there is no wisdom; Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—these Are not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in these; This is equal to the realm of space, without difference.
examples.sa: रुपे न प्रज्ञ इति रुपि न अस्ति प्रज्ञा विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च । न च एति प्रज्ञ इति तेष न अस्ति प्रज्ञा आकाशधातुसम तस्य न चास्ति भेदः ॥

examples.dm: The nature of all objective referents is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless. The nature of the expanse of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.gm: The nature of objects of apprehension is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless; The nature of the realm of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.sa: आरम्बणान प्रकृती स अ(न)न्तपारा सत्त्वान या च प्रकृती स अनन्तपारा । आकाशधातुप्रकृती स अनन्तपारा प्रज्ञा पि लोकविदुनां स अनन्तपारा ॥

examples.dm: Those who think, "May I become a disciple of the Sugata," And those who desire to become Pratyekabuddhas or likewise Kings of Dharma, Cannot achieve these without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot cross from this shore to the other without seeing the ferry.
examples.gm: Whoever thinks they will become a śrāvaka of the Sugata, Or a pratyekabuddha, and likewise wishes to become a Dharma King, Cannot attain it without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot see a crossing to go from this shore to the other.
examples.sa: यो इच्छती सुगतश्रावक हं भवेयं प्रत्येकबुद्ध भवियां तथ धर्मराजो । इमु क्षान्त्यनागमि न शक्यति प्रापुणेतुं यथ आरपारगमनाय अतीतदर्शी ॥

examples.dm: Whips, sticks, weapons, being killed, bound, or beaten, Decapitation, and the cutting off of ears, feet, hands, and nose— Thinking, "I shall endure whatever worldly sufferings there may be," The bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.gm: "Whips, sticks, weapons, killing, binding, and beating, Severing of the head, and cutting off ears, hands, feet, and nose— Whatever sufferings exist in the world, I will endure them!" Thinking this, the bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.sa: कशदण्डशस्त्रवधबन्धनताडनाश्च शिरछेदकर्णचरणाकरनासछेदाः । यावन्ति दुःख जगती अहु तत्सहामि क्षान्तीय पारमित तिष्ठति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: If they should hear others speaking ill or using harsh words, The wise bodhisattva rejoices, thinking, "This is my happiness." Who speaks, who hears, who [speaks] to whom, and for what reason? One who possesses this supreme perfection of patience is wise.
examples.gm: If one hears abusive and harsh words from others, Thinking, "I am happy," the wise bodhisattva rejoices; Who speaks, who hears, by what, what is it, and for what reason? The wise one is endowed with the supreme perfection of patience.
examples.sa: परुषं श्रुणित्व वचनं परतो दुरुक्तं परितोषयाति सुसुखं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । को भाषते क शृणुते कुतु कस्य केन सो युक्त क्षान्तिवरपारमिताय विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are throughout Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them were to generate the mind of supreme enlightenment, And were to practice generosity for many tens of millions of millennia, And were to dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the sake of all beings,
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are in Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them, having generated the mind toward supreme awakening, Were to give gifts for many tens of millions of thousands of years, And dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the benefit of beings;
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व निखिले इह जम्बुद्विपे ते सर्वि बोधिवरचित्त उपादयित्वा । दानं ददित्व बहुवर्षसहस्रकोटीः सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधौ ॥

examples.dm: If someone were to diligently apply themselves to the supreme perfection of wisdom, And practice in accordance with it for even a single day, The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this. Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without distraction.
examples.gm: Whoever visibly strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom, If they conform to it for even a single day, That aggregate of generosity cannot match a fraction of their merit; Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without wavering.
examples.sa: यश् चैव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताभियुक्तो दिवसं पि अन्तमश एकनुवर्तयेया । कलपुण्य सो न भवती इह दानस्कन्धो तदतन्द्रितेन सद ओसरितव्य प्रज्ञा ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: For the sake of other beings and persons, the bodhisattva of pure intention Applies themselves with diligent exertion to the perfection of perseverance. For example, just as a female slave carrying water is powerless and under the control of her master, So too do the heroic beings proceed under the control of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: For the sake of other sentient beings and persons, the perfectly pure bodhisattva Manifestly exerts themselves and acts in the perfection of diligence; For example, a servant woman drawing water has no power of her own, but is under the power of her master; Similarly, the heroes act under the power of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: परसत्त्वपुद्गलनिदान विशुद्धसत्त्वा विचरन्ति वीर्यबलपारमिताभियुक्ताः । यथ कुम्भदासि अवशावश भर्तिकस्य तथ सर्वसत्त्ववशतामुपयान्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: If one understands that these phenomena have ceased and are exhausted, And that which is dedicated is also exhausted, And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon, Then by knowing in such a way, it is a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If in this way one knows that this dharma has ceased and is exhausted, And that to which it is dedicated is also exhausted, And knows that a dharma is never dedicated to a dharma, Through knowing in that way, it is perfectly dedicated.
examples.sa: सचि एव जानति निरुध्यति क्षीणधर्मा तच्चैत क्षीण परिणामयिष्यन्ति यत्र । न च धर्म धर्मि परिणामयते कदाचित् परिणामितं भवति एव प्रजानमाने ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: If, while dedicating, the notion of a mind arises, Or the notion of enlightenment, or the notion of sentient beings, Then because of such notions, one dwells in views and the mind is attached to the three; Because there is an object of observation, it is not a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If, when dedicating, the notion of 'mind' arises, If there is the notion of awakening, the notion of dedicating, and the notion of sentient beings, Because of these notions, residing in views, the mind is attached to the three; Since there are apprehensions, it does not amount to dedication.
examples.sa: परिणामयन्तु यदि वर्तति चित्तसंज्ञा तथ बोधिसत्त्वपरिणामन सत्त्वसंज्ञा । संज्ञाय दृष्टिस्थितु चित्त त्रिसङ्गयुक्तो परिणामितं न भवती उपलभ्यमानम् ॥

examples.dm: If one dedicates merit to enlightenment in this way, One is "poison-free," does not forsake the Buddha, and speaks what the Victors have taught. The hero who dedicates in this way outshines All those bodhisattvas in the world who engage in conceptual apprehension.
examples.gm: If one perfectly dedicates merit to awakening in that way, It is without poison, one does not abandon the Buddha, and speaks what the Victor has spoken. Dedicating perfectly in that way, the hero outshines all Of however many bodhisattvas there are in the world who possess apprehension.
examples.sa: एवं च पुण्य परिणामयमान बोधौ न च सो हि बुद्ध क्षिपते जिन उक्तवादी । यावन्ति लोकि उपलम्भिकबोधिसत्त्वा अभिभोन्ति सर्वि परिणामयमान शूरो ॥

examples.dm: Whatever is called the perfection of the Victors, Those phenomena are also proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceptual arrogance Will not decline and will touch the supreme awakening of a Buddha.
examples.gm: Whatever is called the perfection of the victors, Those dharmas too are fully proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who fully dedicates without a conceited mind Will without decline touch the supreme awakening of a buddha.
examples.sa: ये चापि पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् एतेऽपि धर्म परिकीर्तित नाममात्राः । परिणामयाति न च मन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो न च हीयते स्पृशति उत्तमबुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: They teach the Dharma to beings without any regard for material gain. They take singular delight in the Dharma and always speak with gentle words. They possess constant alertness while moving, walking, sleeping, and sitting. They walk while looking only a yoke-length ahead, keeping the mind free from delusion.
examples.gm: Without material motives, they subsequently teach the dharma to beings. Singly rejoicing in the dharma, they are always endowed with gentle words. They are fully endowed with clear comprehension when going, walking, sleeping, and sitting. Looking ahead only the distance of a yoke, they walk without a wandering mind.
examples.sa: धर्मं निरामिषु जगस्यनुशासयन्ति एकान्तधर्मनियताः सद स्निग्धवाक्याः । स्थितिचंक्रमं शयनिषद्य सुसंप्रजाना युगमात्रप्रेक्षिण व्रजन्त्य् अभ्रान्तचिन्ता ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who abides in emptiness, Through aspirations based on the knowledge of sentient beings in the world, Manifests a great variety of diverse activities, Yet does not touch upon nirvana, nor do they remain in emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, Supported by aspirations knowing sentient beings among wanderers, Demonstrates many various kinds of activities, Does not touch nirvāṇa, and does not dwell in emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यतप्रतिष्ठितु एष सत्त्वो जगति क्रियां विविध दर्शयते विचित्राम् । सत्त्वान ज्ञानप्रणिधानअधिष्ठानमेव न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति शून्यत नास्ति स्थानम् ॥

examples.dm: When, having connected with beings through loving-kindness, He practices the meditative stabilizations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, It is impossible to designate that he has attained nirvana, Or to designate him as something conditioned; he does not abide anywhere.
examples.gm: Whenever, having bound themselves with love for wanderers, They practice the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Can it be designated that they will attain nirvāṇa, Or that they are conditioned? They have no abiding.
examples.sa: यं कालि मैत्रि जगती अनुबन्धयित्वा शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधी चरते समाधिम् । अस्थानमेव यदि निर्वृति प्रापुणेया अथवापि संस्कृत स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Dharma the Victor’s Śrāvakas may teach, Explain, or express through logical reasoning, And whatever attainment of supreme, noble bliss and its fruits they achieve, All of these are the power of the Tathāgata, the Great Being.
examples.gm: However much the śrāvakas of the Jina teach the Dharma, Explaining and expressing it logically, Creating supreme noble bliss and attaining its results, All of that is the power of the person of the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: यावन्ति धर्म जिनश्रावक देशयन्ति भाषन्ति युक्तिसहितांश् च उदीरयन्ति । परमार्थसौख्यक्रिय तत्फलप्राप्तिता च सर्वो अयं पुरुषकारु तथागतस्य ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who abides here in peace in this way, Has been prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceit of thinking, "I am in meditative equipoise," or "I have arisen," Why is that? Because the nature of phenomena is fully understood.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva dwells here thus in peace, Is prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceited thought, "I am in meditative equipoise" or "I have arisen." Why is this? Because they completely understand the nature of phenomena.
examples.sa: एवात्मशान्ति विहरन्निह बोधिसत्त्वो सो व्याकृतो पुरमकेहि तथागतेहि । न च मन्यते अहु समाधितु व्युत्थितो वा कस्मार्थ धर्मप्रकृतिं परिजानयित्वा ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no intention; Within those, there is not even an atom's worth of a station for consciousness. They do not dwell on any phenomena, but practice without a dwelling place; Without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no volition; Consciousness does not dwell in them even slightly. Not dwelling in all phenomena, they practice without dwelling, And without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतना च विज्ञान स्थानु अणुमात्र न भोन्ति तस्य । सो सर्वधर्म-अस्थितो अनिकेतचारी अपरीरिगृहीत लभते सुगतान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: One who does not dwell in form, does not dwell in feeling, One who does not dwell in perception, does not dwell in volition, And one who does not dwell in consciousness, dwells in the nature of reality; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling, Whoever does not abide in perception, does not abide in volition, And whoever does not abide in consciousness, abides in the nature of phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: रुपस्मि यो न स्थिहते न च वेदनायां संज्ञाय यो न स्थिहते न च चेतनायाम् । विज्ञानि यो न स्थिहते स्थितु धर्मतायां एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: When one whose conduct is completely pure does not engage with form, And does not engage with consciousness, perception, feeling, or intention, Practicing in that way, they completely abandon all attachments, And, liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: Whoever, with perfectly pure conduct, does not practice in form, And does not practice in consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition, Practicing like that, entirely abandoning all attachment, Liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: रूपस्मि यो न चरते परिशुद्धचारी विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायाम् । एवं चरन्तु परिवर्जयि सर्वसङ्गां सङ्गाद् विमुच्य चरते सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: If, while lacking such knowledge, one perceives form, And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if one conceptualizes that "these aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva Is still practicing with signs and lacks faith in the state of non-arising.
examples.gm: If, lacking understanding, one perceives form, And practices regarding the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if they think "these aggregates are empty," the bodhisattva Practices in signs, and does not have faith in the unborn state.
examples.sa: सचि रुप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान स्कन्ध चरती अप्रजानमानो । इमि स्कन्ध शून्य परिकल्पयि बोधिसत्त्वो चरती निमित्तअनुपादपदे असक्तो ॥

examples.dm: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, or intention, And does not practice in consciousness, practices without a fixed abode. Not apprehending the thought "I am practicing," such a one relies on wisdom; The unborn and intelligent touch the supreme peace of meditative stabilization.
examples.gm: Whoever does not practice regarding form, feeling, perception, or volition, And does not practice regarding consciousness, practices without dwelling. Not apprehending what is called "practicing," they rely on wisdom. Possessing the intelligence of the unborn, they contact the supreme, peaceful samādhi.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतनाया विज्ञानि यो न चरती अनिकेतचारी । चरतीति सो न उपगच्छति प्रज्ञधारी अनुपादधी स्पृशति शान्ति समाधि श्रेष्ठाम् ॥

examples.dm: When wise and learned bodhisattvas, contemplating non-arising, Practice in this way, Though they generate great compassion, they have no perception of sentient beings; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whenever a wise, understanding bodhisattva Reflects on non-arising and practices in this way, Generating great compassion without the perception of sentient beings, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो एवं चरन्तु अनुपादु विचिन्तयित्वा । महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, or intention, And does not practice in consciousness, practices without a fixed abode. Not apprehending the thought "I am practicing," such a one relies on wisdom; The unborn and intelligent touch the supreme peace of meditative stabilization.
examples.gm: Whoever does not practice regarding form, feeling, perception, or volition, And does not practice regarding consciousness, practices without dwelling. Not apprehending what is called "practicing," they rely on wisdom. Possessing the intelligence of the unborn, they contact the supreme, peaceful samādhi.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतनाया विज्ञानि यो न चरती अनिकेतचारी । चरतीति सो न उपगच्छति प्रज्ञधारी अनुपादधी स्पृशति शान्ति समाधि श्रेष्ठाम् ॥

examples.dm: Form is not wisdom, and wisdom is not found within form. Consciousness, perception, feeling, and intention— These are not wisdom, nor is wisdom present within them. This is identical to the element of space, without any distinction.
examples.gm: Form is not wisdom, in form there is no wisdom; Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—these Are not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in these; This is equal to the realm of space, without difference.
examples.sa: रुपे न प्रज्ञ इति रुपि न अस्ति प्रज्ञा विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च । न च एति प्रज्ञ इति तेष न अस्ति प्रज्ञा आकाशधातुसम तस्य न चास्ति भेदः ॥

examples.dm: In which form is not apprehended, nor feeling, nor perception, Nor consciousness, nor intention is apprehended, And all phenomena are thoroughly known to be unborn and empty— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Where form is not, feeling is not, and perception is not apprehended, Consciousness is not, and volition is not apprehended, And all dharmas are fully known in the manner of being unarisen and empty: This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न रूप अपि वेदन चापि संज्ञा विज्ञान नैव न पि चेतनयोपलब्धिः । अनुपादु शून्य न य जानति सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Form is not wisdom, and wisdom is not found within form. Consciousness, perception, feeling, and intention— These are not wisdom, nor is wisdom present within them. This is identical to the element of space, without any distinction.
examples.gm: Form is not wisdom, in form there is no wisdom; Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—these Are not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in these; This is equal to the realm of space, without difference.
examples.sa: रुपे न प्रज्ञ इति रुपि न अस्ति प्रज्ञा विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च । न च एति प्रज्ञ इति तेष न अस्ति प्रज्ञा आकाशधातुसम तस्य न चास्ति भेदः ॥

examples.dm: One should understand that the purity of form is the purity of the fruition; The purity of the fruition and the purity of form become the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruition, and the purity of form Are like the element of space—indivisible and inseparable.
examples.gm: The purity of form should be known as the purity of the fruit; The purity of the fruit and form becomes the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form Are equal to the realm of space, indivisible and unseverable.
examples.sa: रूपस्य शुद्धि फलशुद्धित वेदितव्या फलरूपशुद्धित सर्वज्ञतशुद्धिम् आहुः । सर्वज्ञताय फलशुद्धित रूपशुद्धी आकाशधातुसमताय अभिन्नछिन्नाः ॥

examples.dm: Wind relies upon space, and the mass of water relies upon that. This great earth relies upon that, and living beings rely upon it. Such is the causal basis for sentient beings' engagement in karma; Reflect on the meaning of this: upon what does space abide?
examples.gm: Wind is supported on space, on that is supported the mass of water, On that is supported this great earth, on that are supported living beings; Such is the cause of sentient beings engaging in karma; Think about this meaning of space being a pervasive foundation!
examples.sa: आकाशनिश्रित समीरण आपस्कन्धो त हि निश्रिता इह महापृथिवी जगच्च । सत्त्वान कर्म-उपभोगनिदानम् एव आकाशस्थानु कुतु चिन्तयि एतम् अर्थम् ॥

examples.dm: Those of great renown don the armor of difficult deeds, Which is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources. They are free from the concept of the three vehicles and have no grasping; They are irreversible, unwavering, and possess the quality of being imperturbable.
examples.gm: Those endowed with great renown don the armor that is difficult to do; It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. They are free from the perception of the three vehicles and have no grasping. They are irreversible, unwavering, and of unperturbed nature.
examples.sa: संनाहु दुष्करू महायशु संनहन्ती न च स्कन्धधातु न च आयतनैः सनद्धाः । त्रिभि यानसंज्ञविगता अपरिगृहीता अविवर्तिका अचलिताश्च अकोप्यधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: They have completely avoided the borderlands and the regions of barbarian peoples. They are never uncertain about their own stage, remaining as steadfast as Mount Meru. They would even sacrifice their lives for the sake of the Dharma and are devoted to the diligence of yoga. One should know that these are the signs of the state of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: They completely abandon the borderlands of uncivilized border-dwellers. Without self-doubt, they are always like Mount Sumeru. Giving up even their lives for the sake of the dharma, they vividly strive in yoga. One should know that these are the signs of an irreversible one.
examples.sa: प्रत्यन्तम्लेच्छजनवर्जित-अन्तदेशाः स्वकभूमि काङ्क्षविगताः सद मेरुकल्पाः । धर्मार्थ जीवित त्यजन्ति प्रयुक्तयोगा अविवर्तियान इमि लिङ्ग प्रजानितव्या ॥

examples.dm: The fifth chapter explains the clear realization of the pinnacle. One who does not desire the level of an Arhat, the wisdom of a Pratyekabuddha, Or the three realms, even in a dream, But sees the Buddhas and teaches the Dharma to beings— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: Chapter Five: Teaching the Clear Realization of the Peak. The stage of an arhat and the pristine wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, And the three realms, they do not desire even in dreams; Seeing the buddhas and teaching the dharma to wanderers, They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: अर्हन्तभूमिम् अपि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ त्रैधातुकं न स्पृशते सुपिनान्तरेऽपि । बुद्धांश् च पश्यति कथेति जनस्य धर्मं अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Whatever is called the perfection of the Victors, Those phenomena are also proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceptual arrogance Will not decline and will touch the supreme awakening of a Buddha.
examples.gm: Whatever is called the perfection of the victors, Those dharmas too are fully proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who fully dedicates without a conceited mind Will without decline touch the supreme awakening of a buddha.
examples.sa: ये चापि पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् एतेऽपि धर्म परिकीर्तित नाममात्राः । परिणामयाति न च मन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो न च हीयते स्पृशति उत्तमबुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: "And such will be the nature of your future ascetic discipline and yoga; Your former qualities were also like this," he declares. Any bodhisattva who, upon hearing such words, becomes conceited, Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
examples.gm: "Whatever ascetic practices, vows, and yogas you will possess, Your past qualities and conduct were also like this," he says. Whatever bodhisattva hears such words and becomes conceited, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
examples.sa: धुतवृत्त यादृशु स भेष्यति युक्तयोगी पूर्वं पि तुभ्य इमि आसि गुणोवरूपा । यो एव श्रुत्व अभिमन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्यु मारु पर्युत्थितु अल्पबुद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom
examples.gm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom

examples.dm: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: 'Phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!
examples.gm: In the language of India: Āryaprajñāpāramitāsañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the noble Mañjuśrī.
examples.sa: ओम् नमो भगवत्यै आर्यप्रज्ञापारमितारत्नगुणसंचयगाथायै । नमो आर्यमञ्जुश्रिये ।

examples.dm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom
examples.sa: रत्नगुणसंचयगाथा ।

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no intention; Within those, there is not even an atom's worth of a station for consciousness. They do not dwell on any phenomena, but practice without a dwelling place; Without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no volition; Consciousness does not dwell in them even slightly. Not dwelling in all phenomena, they practice without dwelling, And without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतना च विज्ञान स्थानु अणुमात्र न भोन्ति तस्य । सो सर्वधर्म-अस्थितो अनिकेतचारी अपरीरिगृहीत लभते सुगतान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.
examples.sa: रूपस्य दर्शनु अदर्शनु वेदनाये संज्ञाय दर्शनु अदर्शनु चेतनाये । विज्ञानचित्तमनुदर्शनु यत्र नास्ति अय धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्टु तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: If, while lacking such knowledge, one perceives form, And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if one conceptualizes that "these aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva Is still practicing with signs and lacks faith in the state of non-arising.
examples.gm: If, lacking understanding, one perceives form, And practices regarding the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if they think "these aggregates are empty," the bodhisattva Practices in signs, and does not have faith in the unborn state.
examples.sa: सचि रुप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान स्कन्ध चरती अप्रजानमानो । इमि स्कन्ध शून्य परिकल्पयि बोधिसत्त्वो चरती निमित्तअनुपादपदे असक्तो ॥

examples.dm: If, while lacking such knowledge, one perceives form, And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if one conceptualizes that "these aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva Is still practicing with signs and lacks faith in the state of non-arising.
examples.gm: If, lacking understanding, one perceives form, And practices regarding the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if they think "these aggregates are empty," the bodhisattva Practices in signs, and does not have faith in the unborn state.
examples.sa: सचि रुप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान स्कन्ध चरती अप्रजानमानो । इमि स्कन्ध शून्य परिकल्पयि बोधिसत्त्वो चरती निमित्तअनुपादपदे असक्तो ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: While practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, They do not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet do not engage in signs; For example, just as a skilled boatman goes back and forth, Without staying on either shore and without remaining in the ocean.
examples.gm: Practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Not touching nirvāṇa and not engaging in signs, Just as a skilled boatman going back and forth, Does not dwell on either shore, nor does he dwell in the ocean.
examples.sa: शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधिं चरमाणु धर्मा न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति नो च निमित्तचारी । यथ नाविको कुशल गच्छति आरपारम् उभयान्ति अस्थितु न तिष्ठति अर्णवेस्मिन् ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this one called a 'great being' (mahāsattva)?" Because they have become the foremost among the vast assembly of sentient beings, And because they sever the great thicket of views within the realm of sentient beings; For that reason, they are truly called a "great being."
examples.gm: Why are they called a "great being"? Because they become the supreme among great multitudes of sentient beings, and sever the great views of the realms of sentient beings; Therefore, they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महसत्त्व सोऽथ केनोच्यति कारणेन महताय अत्र अयु भेष्यति सत्त्वराशेः । दृष्टीगतां महति छिन्दति सत्त्वधातोः महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Thus the bodhisattvas practice the wisdom of the Victors; They know that these aggregates are empty and unborn from the very beginning. While not in meditative equipoise, they engage in compassion for the realm of sentient beings, And even during that interval, they never decline from the Buddha-dharma.
examples.gm: A bodhisattva engaging in the victors' perfection of wisdom, Knows these aggregates to be empty from the beginning and unarisen; Without resting in meditative equipoise, they enter into compassion for the realm of beings, And in the meantime, they never decline from the buddha dharmas.
examples.sa: पुन बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान प्रज्ञां अनुपाद स्कन्ध इमि जानति आदिशून्यान् । असमाहितो करुण प्रेक्षति सत्त्वधातुम् अत्रान्तरे न परिहायति बुद्धधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening?" It is because by mounting it, one delivers all sentient beings from suffering. This vehicle is a vast celestial palace, as immense as space; It is the supreme vehicle, the means for fully attaining joy, delight, and bliss.
examples.gm: Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Mounting it, all sentient beings pass beyond sorrow. This vehicle is a great immeasurable palace like space, The supreme vehicle, which brings about the attainment of joy, happiness, and bliss.
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधियानो यत्रारुहित्व स निर्वापयि सर्वसत्त्वान् । आकाशतुल्य अयु यान महाविमानो सुखसौख्यक्षेमभिप्रापणु यानश्रेष्ठो ॥

examples.dm: For those small-minded beings who have newly entered the vehicle, If they have not attained this rare and precious jewel, Mara will strive to create obstacles for them; The Buddhas of the ten directions apply themselves to protecting them.
examples.gm: Sentient beings of small intellect who have newly entered the vehicle, Who have not found this rare jewel— In order to create obstacles for them, Māra will become energetic; But the Buddhas of the ten directions will apply themselves to fully protecting them.
examples.sa: नवयानप्रस्थित स सत्त्व परीत्तबुद्धिः य इमं दुर्लाभु धर्मरतनं परापुणन्ति । मारोऽत्र उत्सुकु भविष्यति अन्तराये बुद्धा दशद्दिशि परिग्रहसंप्रयुक्ताः ॥

examples.dm: Whoever wishes to set forth in this Buddha vehicle Should train with an even mind toward all beings, the recognition of them as parents, A helpful attitude, and a loving heart, Being without harshness, remaining straightforward, and speaking gentle words.
examples.gm: Whoever desires to definitely emerge in this vehicle of the Buddha, With an even mind toward all beings, perceiving them as parents, Should act with an attitude of benefit and a mind of loving-kindness, Be free from rigidity, straightforward, and speak gentle words.
examples.sa: निर्यायनाय य इच्छति बुद्धज्ञाने समचित्त सर्वजगती पितृमातृसंज्ञा । हितचित्त मैत्रमन एव पराक्रमेय्या अखिलार्जवो मृदुगिराय पराक्रमेय्या ॥

examples.dm: The bodhisattva does not apprehend a prior limit, a later limit, Or a present; they are the purity of the three times. That which is such is unconditioned and free from conceptual elaboration; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas do not apprehend the past limit, the future limit, And the present occurrence; the three times are pure. They are unconditioned and free from conceptual proliferation; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: पूर्वान्ततो न उपलभ्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अपरान्ततोऽपि प्रतिउपन्न त्रियध्वशुद्धो । यो शुद्ध सो अनभिसंस्कृतु निष्प्रपञ्चो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: When wise and learned bodhisattvas, contemplating non-arising, Practice in this way, Though they generate great compassion, they have no perception of sentient beings; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whenever a wise, understanding bodhisattva Reflects on non-arising and practices in this way, Generating great compassion without the perception of sentient beings, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो एवं चरन्तु अनुपादु विचिन्तयित्वा । महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Whether the wise remain in the world or pass into nirvāṇa, This flawless true nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, remains. Bodhisattvas realize this suchness; And therefore, the Buddha is given the name "Tathāgata."
examples.gm: Whether the wise remain in the world or have passed into nirvāṇa, This flawless dharmatā, the emptiness of dharmas, remains; Bodhisattvas subsequently realize this suchness, Therefore, the Buddhas are given the name Tathāgata.
examples.sa: तिष्ठन्तु लोकविदुनां परिनिर्वृतानां स्थित एष धर्मतनियाम शून्यधर्मा । तां बोधिसत्त्व तथताम् अनुबुद्धयन्ति तस्मा हु बुद्ध कृत नाम तथागतेभिः ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, when seeking complete awakening, those who get to hear This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Will find relief and become fearless; This is not the level of an Arhat, nor the level of a Pratyekabuddha.
examples.gm: Likewise, when seeking enlightenment, whoever attains the hearing Of this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, They attain relief and become fearless— Not of the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमिता जिनानां शृणु तात यो लभति बोधि गवेषमाणः । आश्वासप्राप्त भवती न च तस्य त्रासो नार्हन्तभूमि न पि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमी ॥

examples.dm: When this is explained, some will harbor doubts, thinking: "The Leader has not even mentioned my name here; He has not mentioned my family, my level, or my lineage." This is the work of Māra, causing them to reject it rather than listen.
examples.gm: When this is taught, some will harbor doubts, thinking, 'The Leader has not fully pronounced my name here, Nor fully pronounced my lineage, birthplace, or clan.' They will not listen and will abandon it; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: काङ्क्षा च केषचि भविष्यति भाषमाणे न ममात्र नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन । न च जाति भूमि परिकीर्तितु नापि गोत्रं न च सो श्रुणिष्यति क्षिपिष्यति मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Form is not wisdom, and wisdom is not found within form. Consciousness, perception, feeling, and intention— These are not wisdom, nor is wisdom present within them. This is identical to the element of space, without any distinction.
examples.gm: Form is not wisdom, in form there is no wisdom; Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—these Are not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in these; This is equal to the realm of space, without difference.
examples.sa: रुपे न प्रज्ञ इति रुपि न अस्ति प्रज्ञा विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च । न च एति प्रज्ञ इति तेष न अस्ति प्रज्ञा आकाशधातुसम तस्य न चास्ति भेदः ॥

examples.dm: The nature of all objective referents is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless. The nature of the expanse of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.gm: The nature of objects of apprehension is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless; The nature of the realm of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.sa: आरम्बणान प्रकृती स अ(न)न्तपारा सत्त्वान या च प्रकृती स अनन्तपारा । आकाशधातुप्रकृती स अनन्तपारा प्रज्ञा पि लोकविदुनां स अनन्तपारा ॥

examples.dm: The element of space in the eastern direction and the southern direction, And likewise in the western direction and the northern direction, is infinite; It exists above, below, and in all the ten directions as far as they extend. It is without differentiation and without any distinctions.
examples.gm: The element of space in the eastern direction and the southern direction, And likewise in the western direction and the northern direction, is boundless; Above, below, and in as many of the ten directions as there are, it exists; There is no difference and there is no distinction.
examples.sa: आकाशधातु पुरिमादिशि दक्षिणायां तथ पश्चिमोत्तरदिशाय अनन्तपारा । उपराधराय दशद्दिशि यावदस्ति नानात्वता न भवते न विशेषप्राप्ता ॥

examples.dm: The Guide has proclaimed that perception is the near shore; By dismantling and abandoning perception, one goes to the far shore. Those who are free from perception have attained this subsequent state; Having crossed over, they abide by the Teacher’s command.
examples.gm: The Guide has proclaimed that perception is this shore; Destroying and abandoning perception, one goes to the other shore; Those who are free from perception, attaining this, Have reached the other shore and abide in the Teacher's word.
examples.sa: संज्ञेति नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन संज्ञां विभाविय प्रहाण व्रजन्ति पारम् । ये अत्र संज्ञविगमं अनुप्राप्नुवन्ति ते पारप्राप्त स्थित पारमिते हु भोन्ति ॥

examples.dm: All those who have passed, the current Protectors of the worlds of the ten directions, And those who will arise in the future, all emerge from her. She is the Mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental activities of other sentient beings.
examples.gm: Those protectors of the world in the past and in the ten directions, And those who will appear in future times, arise from this. She is the mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental conduct of other sentient beings.
examples.sa: येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत भविष्यन्त्य् अनागताश् च । लोकस्य दर्शिक जनेत्रि जिनान माता परसत्त्वचित्तचरितान निदर्शिता(का) च ॥

examples.dm: Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many eons As there are grains of sand in the Ganges and proclaim the word "sentient being," Since they are pure from the beginning, how could a sentient being ever be born? This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many Aeons as there are grains of sand, and proclaim the word "sentient being," Since they are pure from the very beginning, how could a sentient being arise? This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि गङ्गवालुकसमानि स्थिहित्व कल्पां सत्त्वेति शब्द परिकीर्तयि नायकोऽयम् । सत्त्वस्य्’ उपादु कुतु भेष्यति आदिशुद्धो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: When I spoke in accordance with this supreme perfection, At that time, the Supreme Being of the past prophesied, Saying, "In a future time, you will become a Buddha," Thus the Conqueror spoke, saying that I had been prophesied.
examples.gm: When I, with this supreme perfection of wisdom, Spoke in conformity, at that time the supreme being of the past, Saying, "In a future time you will become a buddha"— "I was prophesied," thus the Victorious One declared.
examples.sa: एवं जिनो भणति अप्रतिकूलभाणी यद् अहं इमाय वरपारमिताय आसी । तद व्याकृतोऽहु परापुरुषोत्तमेन बुद्धो भविष्यसि अनागत-अध्वनस्मिन् ॥

examples.dm: For all the Victors of the past, the future, and those residing in the ten directions, This perfection is the path; there is no other. This perfection is said to be the clarity, the lamp, the light, And the supreme guide for those who have entered upon supreme enlightenment.
examples.gm: The Victorious Ones of the past, future, and whoever abide in the ten directions, The path of all of them is this perfection, and no other. This perfection is, for those entered into supreme awakening, Explained as the supreme illumination, lamp, light, and teacher.
examples.sa: अतिक्रान्तनागत जिना स्थित ये दिशासु सर्वेषु मार्गु अयु पारमिता अनन्यो । ओभास उल्क वरबोधयि प्रस्थितानाम् आलोक शास्त्रि इमि पारमिता प्रदिष्टाः ॥

examples.dm: For those who have trained in the perfection of wisdom, All the perfections are gathered within this. Just as the sixty-two views are contained within the view of the transitory collection, So too, it is taught that all these perfections are contained within this one.
examples.gm: For those who have trained in the perfection of wisdom, All perfections come to be included herein. Just as the sixty-two views are included within the view of the transitory collection, Likewise, these perfections are taught to be included (herein).
examples.sa: प्रज्ञाय पारमित शिक्षित संस्कृतानां सर्वेष पारमित भोन्तिह संगृहीताः । सत्कायदृष्टि यथ षष्टि दुवे च दृष्टी अन्तर्गतास्तथमि पारमिता भवन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Suppose someone were to make offerings to the stūpas Of the Sugatas who have passed into parinirvāṇa, constructing them of the seven precious gems, And were to fill a thousand million buddha-fields With as many stūpas of the Sugatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
examples.gm: If someone, of the completely parinirvāṇized Sugata, Were to build stūpas from the seven precious things and make offerings, and with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the Ganges' Sands, were to fill thousands of millions of fields;
examples.sa: परिनिर्वृतस्य सुगतस्य करेय्य स्तूपां पूजेय सप्तरतनामयु कश्चिद् एव । तेहि प्रपूर्ण सिय क्षेत्रसहस्रकोट्यो यथ गङ्गवालिकसमैः सुगतस्य स्तूपैः ॥

examples.dm: If in infinite tens of millions of realms, All the sentient beings who dwell therein, Were to do nothing else but offer divine flowers, the finest incense, And ointments for three eons or even longer,
examples.gm: And if, in infinite millions of fully conceived fields, All of the sentient beings, however many reside there, Doing no other work, with divine flowers, supreme incense, and Ointments, were to make offerings for aeons of the three times or even more—
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व पुन तान्तक क्षेत्रकोट्यो ते सर्वि पूजन करेयुर् अनन्तकल्पान् । दिव्येहि पुष्पवरगन्धविलेपनेहि कल्पांस् त्रियध्वपरिकल्प ततोऽपि भूयः ॥

examples.dm: The Victor, having been asked a question by Śakra, replied: If there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would still take this very Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Victor fully asked Śakra a question, and he replied: "Even if there were buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनेन परिपृच्छितु प्रश्नमाहु सचि गङ्गवालिकसमा सिय बुद्धक्षेत्राः । जिनधातु सर्वि परिपूरित चूडिबद्धा इमम् एव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताहु गृह्णे ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Buddhas of the past, numbering tens of millions of billions, Who reside in infinitely many billions of fields, and those who have passed into parinirvāṇa, Those protectors of the world, Teach the precious Dharma for the sake of completely ending suffering.
examples.gm: Whatever tens of millions of hundreds of billions of buddhas of the past, And whoever resides in many infinite thousands of tens of millions of fields, And whatever protectors of the world who have passed into nirvāṇa, Demonstrate the precious dharma in order to exhaust suffering:
examples.sa: ये बुद्धकोटिनियुता पुरिमा व्यतीता ये वा अनन्तबहुक्षेत्रसहस्रकोटयः । तिष्ठन्ति येऽपि परिनिर्वृत लोकनाथा देशन्ति धर्मरतनं दुखसंक्षयाय ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, if you wish to attain the supreme primordial wisdom of a Buddha, Have faith in this Mother of the Victors. For example, it would be unfitting to be like a merchant who, Having traveled to an island of jewels, returns home with his goods exhausted.
examples.gm: Therefore, if the supreme pristine wisdom of a buddha One wishes to touch, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! For example, having gone to the island of jewels, a merchant Returning bereft of goods—it is not fitting to become like that.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु श्रद्दधत एव जिनान मातां यदि इच्छथा स्पृशितु उत्तमबुद्धज्ञानम् । सो वाणिजो यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं मूलातु छेदन करित्व पुन आगमेया ॥

examples.dm: However much the hosts of śrāvakas generate a mass of merit Through being endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, It cannot match even a fraction of a bodhisattva’s single thought of rejoicing; The mass of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Even if however many hosts of śrāvakas generate collections of merit, Fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, Compared to a single mind of rejoicing of a bodhisattva, The heap of merit of the hosts of śrāvakas cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति श्रावकगणाः प्रसवन्ति पुण्यं दानं च शीलमपि भावनसंप्रयुक्तम् । स हि बोधिसत्त्व अनुमोदन एकचित्ते न च सर्वश्रावकगणे सिय पुण्यस्कन्धो ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who meditates on the supreme perfection of wisdom, And having arisen from that, teaches the stainless Dharma, And dedicates that for the sake of beings as the cause of enlightenment— There is no virtue in the three worlds equal to that.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who meditates on the supreme wisdom, Arising from that, teaches the untainted dharma, And dedicates that as a cause for awakening for the sake of beings, There is no virtue equal to that in the three worlds.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व वरप्रज्ञ विभावयन्तो तत उत्थितो कथयि धर्म निरुपलेपम् । तं चापि नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधौ नास्ति त्रिलोक शुभ तेन समं भवेया ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.
examples.sa: रूपस्य दर्शनु अदर्शनु वेदनाये संज्ञाय दर्शनु अदर्शनु चेतनाये । विज्ञानचित्तमनुदर्शनु यत्र नास्ति अय धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्टु तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Supreme enlightenment is not reached by the initial mind, Yet without that initial mind, it cannot be reached. Peaceful enlightenment is not attained by the final mind, Yet without that, it is also impossible to attain it.
examples.gm: By the first mind, supreme awakening is not touched, Yet without it, one is not able to touch it. By the final mind, peaceful awakening is not attained, Yet without it, one is not able to attain it.
examples.sa: प्रथमेव चित्त स्पृशती न च अग्रबोधिम् असता न तस्य स्पृशता पुन शक्य भोन्ति । न च चित्त पश्चिम शिवाम् अनुप्रापुणाति असता न तस्य पुन प्रापणनाय शक्यम् ॥

examples.dm: From a seed, the sprout, flower, and fruit arise; Just as it is not the case that the tree does not exist because the seed has ceased, So too, the initial mind is the cause of awakening; It is not the case that awakening does not exist because that mind has ceased.
examples.gm: From a seed, a sprout, a flower, and a fruit arise, And when it ceases, the tree is not absent there—just as, Likewise, the first mind is also the cause of awakening, And when it ceases, it is not that awakening is absent.
examples.sa: बीजातु स्तम्ब फल पुष्प समागमन्ति सो वानिरुद्ध असतो न हि तस्य वृक्षो । एमेव चित्त प्रथमं तु निदान बोधेः सो वा निरुद्ध असतो न हि तस्य बोधिः ॥

examples.dm: Form, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness, Are profound, by nature signless, and utterly peaceful. Just as one might seek to reach the bottom of the ocean with an arrow, When analyzed with wisdom, the depth of the aggregates cannot be found.
examples.gm: Form, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness Are profound, naturally signless, and utterly peaceful; For example, like searching for the bottom of the ocean with an arrow, When examined with wisdom, the depth of the aggregates cannot be found.
examples.sa: गम्भीर रुप अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान संज्ञ प्रकृती अनिमित्तशान्ता । काण्डेन गाध यथ सागरि एषमाणो प्रज्ञाय स्कन्ध विमृषित्व अलब्धगाधा ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the bodhisattva who practices the supreme perfection of wisdom, Dwelling in emptiness and the signless, Having destroyed the dense darkness of views, outshines all worldly beings, Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, and the many bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Just so, the bodhisattva practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Practicing emptiness and signlessness, The wise one, having destroyed the dense thicket of views, outshines all beings, Arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and many bodhisattvas.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितां चरन्तो विधमित्व दृष्टिगहनं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । अभिभोन्ति सर्वजगती रहप्रत्ययांश्च शून्यानिमित्तचरितो पृथु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: This is a marvelous and wondrous accumulation of qualities: Abiding in meditative concentration and stabilization, they are without signs. If those who abide therein should have their bodies perish, They will be reborn in the desire realm exactly according to their intentions.
examples.gm: This is the marvelous wonder of accumulating qualities: Having abided in the samādhis of the dhyānas, they have no signs; If the bodies of those who abide in them were to fall apart, They are again born in the desire realm according to their intention.
examples.sa: आश्चर्यम् अद्भुतम् इदं गुणसंचयानां ध्याने समाधि विहरन्ति निमित्त नास्ति । तत्र स्थितान यदि भज्यति आत्मभावो पुन कामधातु उपपद्यति यथाभिप्राया ॥

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, if you wish to attain the supreme primordial wisdom of a Buddha, Have faith in this Mother of the Victors. For example, it would be unfitting to be like a merchant who, Having traveled to an island of jewels, returns home with his goods exhausted.
examples.gm: Therefore, if the supreme pristine wisdom of a buddha One wishes to touch, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! For example, having gone to the island of jewels, a merchant Returning bereft of goods—it is not fitting to become like that.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु श्रद्दधत एव जिनान मातां यदि इच्छथा स्पृशितु उत्तमबुद्धज्ञानम् । सो वाणिजो यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं मूलातु छेदन करित्व पुन आगमेया ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may possess great faith, If they lack wisdom, they will quickly deteriorate. When faith is fully embraced by wisdom, They will transcend the two levels and attain supreme awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may have much faith, If they are completely lacking in wisdom, they will quickly become unfit. If their faith is fully embraced by wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds, they will attain supreme enlightenment.
examples.sa: किंचापि श्रद्धबहुलो सिय बोधिसत्त्वो प्रज्ञाविहीन विलयं लघु प्रापुणाति । तं चैव श्रद्ध परिगृह्णयमान प्रज्ञा अतिक्रम्य बोधिद्वय प्राप्स्यति अग्रबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: The first chapter teaches omniscience of all aspects. Whatever rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and forests, All depend upon the Naga King, the Lord of Nagas, who dwells in Anavatapta; They are the power and glory of that Lord of Nagas.
examples.gm: Chapter One: The Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects. However many rivers flow in this Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests, All depend upon the nāga king, the lord of nāgas, dwelling in Anavatapta; It is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
examples.sa: यावन्ति नद्य प्रवहन्ति ह जम्बुद्वीपे फल पुष्प औषधाधि वनस्पति रोहयन्ति । भूजत गजेन्द्रनागपतिनिश्रयनोवतनस्य तस्यानुभावश्रिय साभु जगाधिपस्य ॥

examples.dm: For example, although there are billions of trees in the world of Jambudvīpa, In many various forms, with diverse colors and diverse shapes, Aside from speaking of them in terms of the number of things that cast a shadow, The shadows themselves are not diverse, nor is there any distinction between them.
examples.gm: For example, in Jambudvīpa there are thousands of tens of millions of trees, Of various kinds, numerous types, and many forms; Except when spoken of as a number of shadows, There are no various shadows, nor are there differences.
examples.sa: यथ जम्बुद्वीपि बहुवृक्षसहस्रकोटी नानाप्रकार विविधाश्च अनेकरूपाः । न वि छायनानतु भवेत विशेषतापि अन्यत्र छायगतसंख्य प्रभाषमाणा ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: That which does not exist is called "nonexistent." Foolish beings, having conceptualized it, treat it as either existing or non-existing. Existence and non-existence—these two are phenomena that do not exist. Any bodhisattva who understands this will definitely emerge.
examples.gm: Whatever does not exist is called "non-existent." Fools, examining this, conceive of existence and non-existence. Both existence and non-existence are non-existent phenomena; Whatever bodhisattva knows this will definitely emerge.
examples.sa: योऽसौ न विद्यति स एष अविद्यमानो तां बालु कल्पयि अविद्य करोति विद्याम् । विद्या अविद्य उभि एति असन्त धर्मा निर्याति यो इति प्रजानति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings, completely famished, desire food, And those with minds attached to cyclic existence wander perpetually. The two phenomena of "self" and "mine" are unreal and empty; Yet the foolish, by their own doing, tie knots in the sky.
examples.gm: Fully starving sentient beings desire food, and Those possessing a mind attached to saṃsāra constantly wander. Both self and the phenomena of self are unreal and empty; Childish beings themselves have cast a knot in space.
examples.sa: आहारकाम परिकल्पयमान सत्त्वाः संसारि युक्तमनसः सद संस्मरन्ति । अहु मह्य धर्म उभि एति अभूत शून्या आकाशगण्ठि अयु आत्मन बद्ध बाले ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like being stricken by poison through the mere perception of suspicion; Even if that poison has not entered the body, one will fall unconscious. Likewise, the childish who claim "I" and "mine," Have the notion of a self, and through unreal conceptualization, are born and die in impermanence.
examples.gm: For example, just as poison aroused by the perception of suspicion, Even if that poison has not gone inside, one will faint; Likewise, childish beings, accepting self and what belongs to self, Perceiving that self, which is not real, constantly are born and die.
examples.sa: यथ शङ्कितेन विषसंज्ञत अभ्युपैति नो चास्य कोष्ठगतु सो विषु पात्यते च । एमेव बालुपगतो अहु मह्य एषो अहसंज्ञि जायि म्रियते च सदा अभूतो ॥

examples.dm: Those who possess spiritual friends and possess special insight, Will never become afraid upon hearing the Mother of the Victors. Those who associate with negative friends and rely on others, Are like an unfired clay vessel that disintegrates when touched by water.
examples.gm: Possessing spiritual friends and possessing profound insight, Hearing the Mother of the Jinas, they will not be afraid. Whoever possesses bad friends and depends upon others, Is like an unfired clay vessel that collapses when it contacts water.
examples.sa: कल्याणमित्रसहितस्य विपश्यकस्य त्रासो न भेष्यति श्रुणित्व जिनान मात्राम् । यो पापमित्रसहितो च परप्रणेयो सो आमभाजन यथोदकस्पृष्ट भिन्नो ॥

examples.dm: These four types of persons are not afraid of that: The Child of the Victors skilled in the truths, the irreversible one, The Arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, the one who is fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
examples.gm: These four kinds of persons are not terrified by this: The children of the Victorious One who are wise in the truth, those who are irreversible, Arhats who have cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, those perfectly embraced by spiritual friends.
examples.sa: चत्वारि पुद्गल इमे न त्रसन्ति येऽस्मिन् जिनपुत्र सत्यकुशलो अविवर्तियश्च । अर्हं विधूतमलक्लेश प्रहीणकाङ्क्षो कल्याणमित्रपरिपाचित यश्चतुर्थः ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because the qualities of the wise arise from them; They provide instruction in the perfection of wisdom. "The Buddha-qualities depend upon the spiritual friend," So spoke the Victor, who possesses the excellence of all virtues.
examples.gm: If one asks why, it is because the qualities of the wise arise from them; They teach the perfection of wisdom. "The dharmas of a Buddha depend on spiritual friends"— So spoke the Victor, who possesses the supreme of all qualities.
