examples.sa: किं कारणं ततु गुणागमु पण्डितानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते अनुशासयन्ति । एवं जिनो भणति सर्वगुणाग्रधारी कल्याणमित्रमुपनिश्रित बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Know that all sentient beings are exactly as oneself is; Know that all phenomena are exactly as all sentient beings are; Not conceptualizing either non-arising or arising— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Knowing all sentient beings to be like oneself, Knowing all dharmas to be like all sentient beings, Not conceptualizing both non-arising and arising, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ आत्मनं तथ प्रजानति सर्वसत्त्वां यथ सर्वसत्त्व तथ प्रजानति सर्वधर्मान् । अनुपादुपादु उभये अविकल्पमानो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Know that all sentient beings are exactly as oneself is; Know that all phenomena are exactly as all sentient beings are; Not conceptualizing either non-arising or arising— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Knowing all sentient beings to be like oneself, Knowing all dharmas to be like all sentient beings, Not conceptualizing both non-arising and arising, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ आत्मनं तथ प्रजानति सर्वसत्त्वां यथ सर्वसत्त्व तथ प्रजानति सर्वधर्मान् । अनुपादुपादु उभये अविकल्पमानो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, while practicing wisdom, it never occurs to one to think, "Having realized awakening, I shall liberate all beings." Although they display various births and many activities, They practice without conceptualization, just like an illusion.
examples.gm: Likewise, those practicing wisdom never think thus: "Having realized awakening, I will completely liberate beings"; Though they demonstrate taking various births and having many activities, Like an illusion, they practice without conceptualizing.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञचरिते न कदाचि भोति बुद्धित्व बोधि जगती परिमोचयित्वा । आत्मोपपत्ति विविधां क्रियसंप्रयोगां दर्शेति मायसदृशो न विकल्पचारी ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, when seeking complete awakening, those who get to hear This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Will find relief and become fearless; This is not the level of an Arhat, nor the level of a Pratyekabuddha.
examples.gm: Likewise, when seeking enlightenment, whoever attains the hearing Of this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, They attain relief and become fearless— Not of the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमिता जिनानां शृणु तात यो लभति बोधि गवेषमाणः । आश्वासप्राप्त भवती न च तस्य त्रासो नार्हन्तभूमि न पि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमी ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like someone who has found food possessing a hundred flavors, Yet, having found the finest food, they search for poor food. Just so, having found this Perfection of the Bodhisattvas, They seek the enlightenment of the Arhat stage.
examples.gm: For example, just as someone who has found food with a hundred flavors, Having found supreme food, searches for inferior food; A bodhisattva who has found this perfection of wisdom But seeks enlightenment through the level of an arhat is just like that.
examples.sa: यथ भोजनं शतरसं लभियान कश्चित् मार्गेषु षष्टिकु लभित्व स भोजनाग्र्यम् । तथ बोधिसत्त्व इम पारमितां लभित्वा अर्हन्तभूमित गवेषयिष्यन्ति बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: When conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, as well as white and black dharmas, Have been thoroughly deconstructed by wisdom so that not even an atom is observed, That is accounted as the perfection of wisdom in the world; It is just like space, which does not abide in anything at all.
examples.gm: When conditioned, unconditioned, and white and black dharmas Are broken down by wisdom and not even a particle is apprehended, In the world it is reckoned as the perfection of wisdom; It is like space, which does not abide anywhere at all.
examples.sa: यद धर्म संस्कृत असंस्कृत कृष्णशुक्लो अणुमात्रु नो लभति प्रज्ञ विभावमानः । यद प्रज्ञपारमित गच्छति संख्य लोके आकाश यत्र न प्रतिष्ठितु किंचि तत्र ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Thus did the elder Subhūti request of the Protector of the World: "Please explain the signs of the ocean of qualities free from afflictions, And how those of great power do not turn back; O Victor, please grant a prophecy regarding even a mere portion of such qualities."
examples.gm: The elder Subhūti thoroughly requested the Protector of the World: "Ocean of Qualities, please teach the signs of those free from afflictions. How those of great power will not turn back again— Thus, may the Victor explain just a fraction of their qualities."
examples.sa: स्थविरो सुभूति परिपृच्छति लोकनाथं अरणाय लिङ्ग भणही गुणसागराणाम् । अविवर्तिया यथ भवन्ति महानुभावा तां व्याकुरुष्व जिनगुणान प्रदेशमात्रम् ॥

examples.dm: It is not for the sake of the increase, decrease, or grasping of form; Nor is it for the sake of grasping the various phenomena that one trains. While training, one also grasps omniscience itself; This very transcendence is the training of those who delight in excellence.
examples.gm: It is not for the sake of the increase, complete deterioration, or complete apprehension of form; Not training for the sake of completely apprehending various dharmas, Yet training and completely apprehending omniscience itself— Whatever definite emergence this is, this is the training that rejoices in qualities.
examples.sa: न च रुपवृद्धिपरिहाणिपरिग्रहाये न च शिक्षति विविधधर्मपरिग्रहाये । सर्वज्ञतां च परिगृह्णति शिक्षमाणो निर्यायती य इय शिक्ष गुणे रतानाम् ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, these five perfections of the Victors Also acquire the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When they are fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, known as "awakening."
examples.gm: Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also Will attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित नामतया भवन्ति । सर्वज्ञताय परिणामयमाण सर्वे षडपीह एकनयम् अर्छति बोधिनामा ॥

examples.dm: When this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Tathāgatas, is taught, Any bodhisattva who feels devotion and, with sincere resolve, Applies themselves with effort to its realization, Should be known as one who has entered into omniscience itself.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Tathāgatas, When it is taught, whichever bodhisattva aspires to it, And clearly exerts themselves to accomplish it with sincere intent, That noble one should be known to have entered into omniscience.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व अधिमुच्यति भाष्यमाणाम् इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात तथागतानाम् । प्रतिपत्तिया च अभियुज्यति आशयेन सर्वज्ञताय अभिप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Yet someone were to write down in a book this Mother of the Sugatas, From whom the Ten Powers of the Guides arise, And, bearing it, were to honor it with flowers and ointments, The merit of having worshiped stūpas would not approach even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding that from which the Guides of ten powers will arise, Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book, Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments, The merit of building stūpas and making offerings cannot match a fraction of that.
examples.sa: यश् चो इमां सुगतमात लिखित्व पुस्ते यत उत्पती दशबलान विनायकानाम् । धारेयि सत्करयि पुष्पविलेपनेहि कल पुण्य भोन्ति न स स्तूपि करित्व पूजाम् ॥

examples.dm: A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceit, thinking, "I will be prophesied by the Ten-Powered Ones and shall reach enlightenment." Thinking, "There is nothing at all here," they have no fear of enlightenment. To practice in such a manner is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceited mind thinking, "I Am prophesied by the Ten-Powered One and will touch awakening," Nor do they fear awakening, thinking, "There is nothing at all here"; Practicing in this way is practicing the wisdom of the sugatas.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु न च मन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अहु व्याकृतो दशबलेहि स्पृशेय बोधिम् । न च त्रासु बोधि भवते न इहास्ति किंचिद् एवं चरन्तु चरती सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Wisdom is the pleasure grove where they abide; It is the sphere of activity for the Guides who possess the ten powers. Although they completely deliver sentient beings from the sufferings of the three lower realms, They never entertain the notion of a "sentient being."
examples.gm: Relying on the perfection of wisdom as a pleasure grove, This is the domain of the guides with the ten powers; Even though they fully extract sentient beings from the suffering of the three lower realms, They never have the notion of "sentient beings".
examples.sa: अयु गोचरो दशबलान विनायकानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित रम्यवनाश्रितानाम् । दुखितांश्च सत्त्व त्रिअपाय समुद्धरन्ति न पि सत्त्वसंज्ञ अपि तेषु कदाचि भोति ॥

examples.dm: Yet someone were to write down in a book this Mother of the Sugatas, From whom the Ten Powers of the Guides arise, And, bearing it, were to honor it with flowers and ointments, The merit of having worshiped stūpas would not approach even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding that from which the Guides of ten powers will arise, Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book, Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments, The merit of building stūpas and making offerings cannot match a fraction of that.
examples.sa: यश् चो इमां सुगतमात लिखित्व पुस्ते यत उत्पती दशबलान विनायकानाम् । धारेयि सत्करयि पुष्पविलेपनेहि कल पुण्य भोन्ति न स स्तूपि करित्व पूजाम् ॥

examples.dm: When a mother falls ill, though she has many children, They all become distressed and perform healing rites for her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions Direct their intention toward this supreme Perfection of Wisdom, who is their mother.
examples.gm: When a mother becomes sick and has many sons, They all become unhappy and attend upon her. Likewise, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions also Keep in mind this holy wisdom, which is their mother.
examples.sa: मात्राय पुत्र बहु सन्ति गिलानि काये ते सर्वि दुर्मनस तत्र प्रयुज्ययेयुः । एमेव बुद्धपिं दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात्र समन्वाहरन्ति ॥

examples.dm: All those who have passed, the current Protectors of the worlds of the ten directions, And those who will arise in the future, all emerge from her. She is the Mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental activities of other sentient beings.
examples.gm: Those protectors of the world in the past and in the ten directions, And those who will appear in future times, arise from this. She is the mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental conduct of other sentient beings.
examples.sa: येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत भविष्यन्त्य् अनागताश् च । लोकस्य दर्शिक जनेत्रि जिनान माता परसत्त्वचित्तचरितान निदर्शिता(का) च ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: Thus the bodhisattvas practice the wisdom of the Victors; They know that these aggregates are empty and unborn from the very beginning. While not in meditative equipoise, they engage in compassion for the realm of sentient beings, And even during that interval, they never decline from the Buddha-dharma.
examples.gm: A bodhisattva engaging in the victors' perfection of wisdom, Knows these aggregates to be empty from the beginning and unarisen; Without resting in meditative equipoise, they enter into compassion for the realm of beings, And in the meantime, they never decline from the buddha dharmas.
examples.sa: पुन बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान प्रज्ञां अनुपाद स्कन्ध इमि जानति आदिशून्यान् । असमाहितो करुण प्रेक्षति सत्त्वधातुम् अत्रान्तरे न परिहायति बुद्धधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the skillful bodhisattva also, Generates great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, And having completely transcended the four Māras and even the two levels, Abides in supreme meditative absorption, yet does not touch upon awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, at that time, a skilled bodhisattva, Generating great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, Having utterly passed beyond the four māras and the two, Dwells in the supreme samādhi and does not touch awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव यस्मि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो महमैत्रि सर्वि उपबन्धति सत्त्वधातौ । चतुरो स मार अतिक्रम्य द्वये च भूमिम् अस्मिन् समाधि स्थितु नो च स्पृशाति बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: In which form is not apprehended, nor feeling, nor perception, Nor consciousness, nor intention is apprehended, And all phenomena are thoroughly known to be unborn and empty— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Where form is not, feeling is not, and perception is not apprehended, Consciousness is not, and volition is not apprehended, And all dharmas are fully known in the manner of being unarisen and empty: This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न रूप अपि वेदन चापि संज्ञा विज्ञान नैव न पि चेतनयोपलब्धिः । अनुपादु शून्य न य जानति सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: When conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, as well as white and black dharmas, Have been thoroughly deconstructed by wisdom so that not even an atom is observed, That is accounted as the perfection of wisdom in the world; It is just like space, which does not abide in anything at all.
examples.gm: When conditioned, unconditioned, and white and black dharmas Are broken down by wisdom and not even a particle is apprehended, In the world it is reckoned as the perfection of wisdom; It is like space, which does not abide anywhere at all.
examples.sa: यद धर्म संस्कृत असंस्कृत कृष्णशुक्लो अणुमात्रु नो लभति प्रज्ञ विभावमानः । यद प्रज्ञपारमित गच्छति संख्य लोके आकाश यत्र न प्रतिष्ठितु किंचि तत्र ॥

examples.dm: When a bodhisattva, through the perfection of wisdom, sees That all phenomena are naturally pure and utterly pristine, They do not perceive an agent, nor do they perceive any phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: All dharmas being naturally pure and entirely pure, If the bodhisattva views the perfection of wisdom, Not apprehending an agent and not apprehending all dharmas, This is practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: प्रकृतीय शुद्ध परिशुद्धिमि सर्वधर्मां प्रज्ञाय पारमित पश्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । न च पश्यकं लभति नापि च सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, those who have truly entered into supreme awakening should understand that by hearing This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Even if they have not received a direct prophecy from the Guide, "Before long, I shall touch the awakening of a Buddha."
examples.gm: Likewise, one who has fully entered supreme enlightenment Should be known as hearing this perfection of wisdom of the Victors; Even if they have not been directly prophesied by the Leaders, They think, 'Before long, I will touch the enlightenment of the Buddhas.'
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो श्रुणमाण प्रज्ञ इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् । यद्यापि संमुख न व्याकृतु नायकेनो तथपि स्पृशिष्यति नचिरेण हु बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Those qualities from which the virtues of certain awakening arise— This is the meaning of ethical discipline for those endowed with virtuous qualities. The complete degeneration of the awakening of those who perform beneficial dharmas— This is what the Guide has called "immoral conduct."
examples.gm: Whatever dharmas produce the qualities of definite awakening, This is the purpose of discipline for those endowed with virtuous dharmas. Whatever dharmas cause the awakening of benefactors to completely degenerate, This was taught by the Guide to be broken discipline.
examples.sa: यो धर्म बोधिगुणआगमु सूरतानां सो शीलअर्थु गुणधर्मसमन्वितानाम् । यो धर्म बोधिगुणहानि हितंकराणां दुःशीलता अयु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: If one dedicates merit to enlightenment in this way, One is "poison-free," does not forsake the Buddha, and speaks what the Victors have taught. The hero who dedicates in this way outshines All those bodhisattvas in the world who engage in conceptual apprehension.
examples.gm: If one perfectly dedicates merit to awakening in that way, It is without poison, one does not abandon the Buddha, and speaks what the Victor has spoken. Dedicating perfectly in that way, the hero outshines all Of however many bodhisattvas there are in the world who possess apprehension.
examples.sa: एवं च पुण्य परिणामयमान बोधौ न च सो हि बुद्ध क्षिपते जिन उक्तवादी । यावन्ति लोकि उपलम्भिकबोधिसत्त्वा अभिभोन्ति सर्वि परिणामयमान शूरो ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme Perfection of Wisdom, Do not see any increase or decrease in form. One who does not see phenomena, non-phenomena, or the sphere of phenomena, And does not touch nirvana, is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: When practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, the yogi Does not see the increase or complete decrease of form; Whoever does not see dharma, non-dharma, or the dharmadhātu, And does not touch nirvāṇa, they abide in wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी न च रूपवृद्धि न च पश्यति पारिहाणिम् । धर्मा अधर्म इमु पश्यति धर्मधातुं न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who fully understands that all phenomena are non-conceptual, Empty, signless, and free from conceptual proliferation, Does not seek awakening through a dualistic wisdom; That yogi strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva, non-conceptualizing, fully knows all dharmas As empty, signless, and free from elaboration, They do not seek awakening through dualistic wisdom; That yogin exerts themselves in the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व अविकल्पकु सर्वधर्मान् शून्यानिमित्त परिजानति निष्प्रपञ्चान् । न च प्रज्ञ बोधि परिएषति आशयेन सो युक्त प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who wishes to remain for a long time in cyclic existence, A yogi who perseveres in the welfare of sentient beings and the purification of the realm, If they do not give rise to even a speck of weariness, They possess the perfection of diligence and are never negligent.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva wishes to cycle in saṃsāra for a long time, A yogi exerting themselves for the benefit of sentient beings and purifying the realms, If they do not generate even an atom of a weary mind, They are endowed with the perfection of diligence and are free from idleness.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व चिरसंसरणाभिप्रायो सत्त्वार्थ क्षेत्रपरिशोधनयुक्तयोगी । न च खेदबुद्धि अणुमात्र उपादियाति सो वीर्यपारमितयुक्त अतन्द्रितश् च ॥

examples.dm: When writing down this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Various and diverse kinds of flashes of inspiration will arise; Yet if, without having benefited sentient beings, they vanish as swiftly as lightning, This complete deterioration is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: When copying this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Various differing modes of confidence will arise; Yet without accomplishing the benefit of beings, swiftly like lightning, They will completely fade away; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: प्रतिभान नेक विविधानि उपपद्यिष्यन्ति लिखमान प्रज्ञ इमु पारमिता जिनानाम् । युत शीघ्र विद्युत यथा परिहायिष्यन्ति अकरित्व अर्थ जगती इमु मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: At that time, these activities of Māra will occur. At that time, after many monks have been stirred to agitation, Many other various obstacles will also arise, Which prevent them from upholding this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: At that time, this work of Māra will arise: At that time, whoever disturbs many monks, They will not uphold this perfection of wisdom; And many other various obstacles will also arise.
examples.sa: इमि मारकर्म भविष्यन्ति य तस्मि काले अन्ये च नेक विविधा बहु अन्तराया । येही समाकुलिकृता बहु भिक्षु तत्र प्रज्ञाय पारमित एतु न धारयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: When this is explained, some will harbor doubts, thinking: "The Leader has not even mentioned my name here; He has not mentioned my family, my level, or my lineage." This is the work of Māra, causing them to reject it rather than listen.
examples.gm: When this is taught, some will harbor doubts, thinking, 'The Leader has not fully pronounced my name here, Nor fully pronounced my lineage, birthplace, or clan.' They will not listen and will abandon it; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: काङ्क्षा च केषचि भविष्यति भाषमाणे न ममात्र नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन । न च जाति भूमि परिकीर्तितु नापि गोत्रं न च सो श्रुणिष्यति क्षिपिष्यति मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: For example, in order to gain knowledge of the route, a merchant seeking profit Travels to whatever cities, towns, or villages lie along the way; He does not remain there, nor does he remain even on the Island of Jewels, And without staying at home, he becomes an expert on the path.
examples.gm: For example, an ambitious merchant, in order to know the routes, Goes to whatever intermediate cities, towns, and villages there are. He does not dwell there, nor does he dwell on the jewel island; The wise one does not dwell at home, but becomes skilled in the path.
examples.sa: अभ्यन्तरे य नगरे निगमे च ग्रामे कामार्थ वाणिजु यथा गमि जाननाय । नो चापि तत्र स्थिहती न च रत्नद्वीपे न च गेह मार्गि कुशलो पुन भोति विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all the knowledge and liberations Of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; He does not abide in those, nor does he abide in the primordial wisdom of a Buddha; He does not abide in the unconditioned; he is one who knows the nature of the path.
examples.gm: Likewise, a brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all The knowledges and liberations of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; They do not dwell in them, nor do they dwell in the Buddha's pristine wisdom; They do not dwell in the unconditioned, but know the nature of the path.
examples.sa: तथ ज्ञान श्रावकविमुक्तिसप्रत्ययानां सर्वत्र भोति कुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । नो चापि तत्र स्थिहते न च बुद्धज्ञाने न च संस्कृते भवति मार्गविदू विधिज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Whether the wise remain in the world or pass into nirvāṇa, This flawless true nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, remains. Bodhisattvas realize this suchness; And therefore, the Buddha is given the name "Tathāgata."
examples.gm: Whether the wise remain in the world or have passed into nirvāṇa, This flawless dharmatā, the emptiness of dharmas, remains; Bodhisattvas subsequently realize this suchness, Therefore, the Buddhas are given the name Tathāgata.
examples.sa: तिष्ठन्तु लोकविदुनां परिनिर्वृतानां स्थित एष धर्मतनियाम शून्यधर्मा । तां बोधिसत्त्व तथताम् अनुबुद्धयन्ति तस्मा हु बुद्ध कृत नाम तथागतेभिः ॥

examples.dm: When this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Tathāgatas, is taught, Any bodhisattva who feels devotion and, with sincere resolve, Applies themselves with effort to its realization, Should be known as one who has entered into omniscience itself.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Tathāgatas, When it is taught, whichever bodhisattva aspires to it, And clearly exerts themselves to accomplish it with sincere intent, That noble one should be known to have entered into omniscience.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व अधिमुच्यति भाष्यमाणाम् इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात तथागतानाम् । प्रतिपत्तिया च अभियुज्यति आशयेन सर्वज्ञताय अभिप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, a bodhisattva whose power of wisdom is weak, Even if they have set out, will decline along the way. If they are fully embraced by skillful means and supreme wisdom, They will not decline and will reach the awakening of a Tathāgata.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva whose power of wisdom is small, Even if they fully engage, will completely fall away. If they are fully embraced by skillful means and supreme wisdom, Without falling away, they will touch the enlightenment of the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञ इह दुर्बलु बोधिसत्त्वो किंचापि प्रस्थिहति भज्यति अन्तरेण । सो वा उपायबलप्रज्ञपरिगृहीतो न च भज्यते स्पृशति बोधि नरर्षभाणाम् ॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Wisdom is the pleasure grove where they abide; It is the sphere of activity for the Guides who possess the ten powers. Although they completely deliver sentient beings from the sufferings of the three lower realms, They never entertain the notion of a "sentient being."
examples.gm: Relying on the perfection of wisdom as a pleasure grove, This is the domain of the guides with the ten powers; Even though they fully extract sentient beings from the suffering of the three lower realms, They never have the notion of "sentient beings".
examples.sa: अयु गोचरो दशबलान विनायकानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित रम्यवनाश्रितानाम् । दुखितांश्च सत्त्व त्रिअपाय समुद्धरन्ति न पि सत्त्वसंज्ञ अपि तेषु कदाचि भोति ॥

examples.dm: They are free from the perception of diversity and speak words consistent with reason; They do not rely on other śramaṇas or brahmins. These wise ones have forever abandoned the three lower realms; They are intensely devoted to the paths of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.gm: Free from differentiated perceptions and speaking rational words, Not relying on other śramaṇas and brahmins; The wise always abandon the three lower realms at all times, And vividly strive in the path of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.sa: नानात्वसंज्ञविगता गिर युक्तभाणी न च अन्य ते श्रमण ब्राह्मण आश्रयन्ति । त्रियपायवर्जित विदू सदकालि भोन्ति दशभिश् च ते कुशलकर्मपथेभि युक्ता ॥

examples.dm: If, in a dream, one sees sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms, And in that very moment makes a prayer to cut the continuum of the lower realms, And pacifies a mass of fire through the power of the blessing of truth— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In a dream, seeing sentient beings abiding in the three lower realms, In that instant they make aspirations to cut off the stream of the lower realms. Through the blessing of truth, the masses of fire are pacified; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: त्रि-अपायप्राप्तु सुपिनस्मि विदित्व सत्त्वान् प्रणिधेति तत्क्षण अपाय उच्छोषयेयम् । सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति स चाग्निस्कन्धम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: Both are distant and will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own commitments to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience? At that time, the Māras and their factions will be delighted.
examples.gm: "Those two will become distant, and they will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own promises to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience?" At that time, the Māras along with their factions will become joyful.
examples.sa: उभि एति दूरि भविष्यन्ति पिशाचतुल्या उभि एति आत्म करिष्यन्ति प्रतिज्ञहानिम् । दुष्टान क्षान्तिविकलान कुतोऽस्ति बोधि तद मारु तुष्टु भवती नमुचीसपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure, Possessing the thirty-two major marks and infinite power; They proclaim the supreme Dharma of emptiness to sentient beings. Wise and patient, they bring joy to the world.
examples.gm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure; With the thirty-two marks and boundless power and strength, They proclaim the supreme empty dharma to sentient beings; Beings will rejoice in this wise one endowed with patience.
examples.sa: क्षान्तीस्थितस्य परिशुध्यति आत्मभावो द्वात्रिंशलक्षणप्रभाव अनन्तपारो । सत्त्वान शून्यवरधर्म निशामयाती प्रियु भोति सर्वजगती क्षममाणु विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: They have completely avoided the borderlands and the regions of barbarian peoples. They are never uncertain about their own stage, remaining as steadfast as Mount Meru. They would even sacrifice their lives for the sake of the Dharma and are devoted to the diligence of yoga. One should know that these are the signs of the state of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: They completely abandon the borderlands of uncivilized border-dwellers. Without self-doubt, they are always like Mount Sumeru. Giving up even their lives for the sake of the dharma, they vividly strive in yoga. One should know that these are the signs of an irreversible one.
examples.sa: प्रत्यन्तम्लेच्छजनवर्जित-अन्तदेशाः स्वकभूमि काङ्क्षविगताः सद मेरुकल्पाः । धर्मार्थ जीवित त्यजन्ति प्रयुक्तयोगा अविवर्तियान इमि लिङ्ग प्रजानितव्या ॥

examples.dm: "And such will be the nature of your future ascetic discipline and yoga; Your former qualities were also like this," he declares. Any bodhisattva who, upon hearing such words, becomes conceited, Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
examples.gm: "Whatever ascetic practices, vows, and yogas you will possess, Your past qualities and conduct were also like this," he says. Whatever bodhisattva hears such words and becomes conceited, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
examples.sa: धुतवृत्त यादृशु स भेष्यति युक्तयोगी पूर्वं पि तुभ्य इमि आसि गुणोवरूपा । यो एव श्रुत्व अभिमन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्यु मारु पर्युत्थितु अल्पबुद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those who have entered supreme enlightenment should never abandon The yoga of the perfection of wisdom, which is like a precious jewel. Just as one who finds a jewel, takes it up, and wraps it with great care, Will quickly travel on and reach a state of peace.
examples.gm: Likewise, one entered into supreme awakening should not abandon yoga In the jewel-like perfection of wisdom; Having found and taken the jewel, one should thoroughly apply exertion, Swiftly progressing, just as one becomes pacified.
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थित रत्नतुल्यो प्रज्ञाय पारमित योगु न रिञ्चितव्यो । रतनं व लब्ध्व गृहमाणु अभिन्नसत्त्वो अनुबुद्धयति त्वरितो शिवमभ्युपैति ॥

examples.dm: For example, consider a man who indulges in desire and, Having made an appointment with a woman, fails to meet her; However many conceptual thoughts he experiences in his mind throughout a single day, For that many eons, the bodhisattva will achieve attainment.
examples.gm: For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire, Having made an appointment with a woman and not meeting her, However many discursive thoughts of his mind operate in a single day, The bodhisattva will gain that many eons.
examples.sa: यथ रागधर्मचरितः पुरुषः स्त्रियाये संकेत कृत्व अलभन्तु विवर्तयेया । यावन्ति चित्तचरिता दिवसेन तस्य तावन्त कल्प अनुबुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: Even a massive heap of ordinary glass trinkets Is outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli gem; Likewise, all the vast heaps of generosity of all beings Are outshone by a bodhisattva who rejoices.
examples.gm: Even a great heap of imitation glass jewels Is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli; Likewise, all the vast heaps of giving of all beings Are outshone by the rejoicing bodhisattva.
examples.sa: काचस्य वा मणिन राशि सिया महन्तो वैडूर्यरत्न अभिभोति स सर्व एको । एमेव सर्वजगती पृथु दानस्कन्धो अभिभोति सर्वपरिणामकु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Acting through wisdom, skillful means, strength, and miraculous powers, As long as their roots of virtue are not yet complete, So long will they not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, Thoroughly practicing by means of the power of wisdom, skillful means, and miracles, As long as their roots of virtue are not perfected, For that long they do not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितां चरन्तो प्रज्ञा उपाय बल ऋद्धि विचारमाणो । तावन् न तां परमशून्यत प्रापुणोति यावन् न ते कुशलमूल भवन्ति पूर्णाः ॥

examples.dm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles Might remain in the sky and simultaneously display various transformations; He demonstrates walking, moving, lying down, and sitting, And he does not grow weary, nor does he become exhausted.
examples.gm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles, Abiding in space, simultaneously emanates magical creations, Demonstrating walking, pacing, sleeping, and sitting; He has no weariness, and he has no fatigue.
examples.sa: भिक्षू यथा परमऋद्धिबलेनुपेतो गगने स्थितो यमक कुर्वति प्रातिहार्यां । गतिचंक्रमं शयनिषद्य निदर्शयाति न निवर्तते न पि च खिद्यति याव तत्र ॥

examples.dm: In the midst of a crowd, a conjured person does not think, "I must please these people," and yet they perform that very action; Although they are seen displaying various miraculous feats, They possess no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.gm: In the midst of people, an illusory person does not think, "I will please these people," yet still pleases them; Though seen to display various miracles, They have no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.sa: यथ मायकारपुरुषस्य न एव भोति ते शिष्य मां जनत सो च करोति कार्यम् । पश्यन्ति तं विविध कार्यु निदर्शयन्तं न च तस्य कायु न पि चित्त न नामधेयम् ॥

examples.dm: In this way, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Bestows the nectar of immortality and brings joy to gods and humans. If even now they strive for the benefit of many sentient beings, What need is there to mention when they are established as Kings of Dharma?
examples.gm: Likewise, the bodhisattva wise in practicing wisdom too, Gives the nectar and pleases gods and humans. Even as they are, they strive to benefit many sentient beings; What need is there to mention when they come to abide as the Dharma King!
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञचरितो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो अमृतस्य दायकु प्रियो मरुमानुषाणाम् । अयु एष एषति हि सत्त्वसुखाभियुक्तो प्रागेव याव स्थितु भेष्यति धर्मराजो ॥

examples.dm: To those who practice skillfully in this way, the many hosts of gods Join their palms in reverence and prostrate. All the Buddhas throughout the world systems of the ten directions Likewise utter garlands of praise for their qualities.
examples.gm: To the wise who practice thus, many hosts of gods Join their palms, bow down, and pay homage; And however many Buddhas there are in the world systems of the ten directions, They completely proclaim a garland of praise for their qualities.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु ना पृथुदेवसंघाः कृतअञ्जलीपुट प्रणम्य नमस्ययन्ति । बुद्धा पि यावत दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ गुणवर्णमालपरिकीर्तन कुर्वयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: The Buddha’s heirs, the listeners, the solitary realizers, the gods, And all the various phenomena of happiness and well-being for all beings, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom; Yet these wisdoms are also neither exhausted nor increased.
examples.gm: The sons of the Buddha, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and gods, And however many dharmas of happiness and joy of all beings there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom, And yet wisdom has no exhaustion and has no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त बुद्धसम श्रावकप्रत्ययाश् च मरुतश् च सर्वजगती सुखसौख्यधर्माः । सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूता न च क्षीयते न च विवर्धति जातु प्रज्ञा ॥

examples.dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
examples.gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.
examples.sa: अविवर्तियस्य वरबोधयि प्रस्थितस्य यो चित्तुपादु अनुमोदितु आशयेन । त्रिसहस्र मेरु तुलयित्व सियाप्रमाणो न त्वेव तस्य कुशलस्यनुमोदनाये ॥

examples.dm: I also rejoice in the mass of merit of all sentient beings, as many as there are, Who strive for virtue and desire to be of benefit; Therefore, once they have attained the qualities of the Victors, They bestow the gift of Dharma upon the world in order to bring suffering to an end.
examples.gm: Seeking virtue and desiring to benefit however many sentient beings there are, They also rejoice in the heaps of merit of them all; Therefore, having attained the qualities of the Victorious Ones, In order to exhaust suffering, they give the gift of Dharma to the world.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व कुशलार्थिक मोक्षकामा सर्वेष भोन्ति अनुमोदितु पुण्यराशि । सत्त्वर्थि ते जिनगुण अनन्त प्रापुणित्वा दास्यन्ति धर्म जगती दुखसंक्षयाये ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: For example, a skillful person endowed with all excellent qualities, Who is powerful, invincible, diligent, and knowledgeable in the techniques of the arts, Who has mastered archery and many other fields of craftsmanship, And who, knowing how to perform illusions, greatly desires the welfare of beings—
examples.gm: For example, a skilled person endowed with all qualities, Powerful, invincible, having made effort, knowing the rites of arts, Who has reached the far shore of archery and many crafts, Knowing how to conjure illusions, intensely desiring the welfare of beings,
examples.sa: पुरुषो यथा कुशल सर्वगुणैरुपेतो बलवान् दुधर्षु कृतयोग्य कलाविधिज्ञो । इष्वस्त्रपारमिगतो पृथुशिल्पयुक्तो मायाविधिज्ञपरमो जगदर्थकामो ॥

examples.dm: Whether one dwells in a town or in a forest, If one is free from the mind of the two vehicles and is certain of supreme enlightenment, This is the solitude of those who have entered into the service of beings; Any bodhisattva who feels superior to them has degraded themselves.
examples.gm: Whether abiding in a village or else in an isolated monastery, If free from the minds of the two vehicles and certain of supreme awakening, This is the solitude of those engaged in the benefit of beings; That conceited bodhisattva ruins themselves.
examples.sa: ग्रामान्ति यो विहरते अथवा अरण्ये द्वययानचित्तविगतो नियतोऽग्रबोधिम् । एषो विवेकु जगदर्थभिप्रस्थितानां आत्मा क्षिणोति तुलयेय स बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, or intention, And does not practice in consciousness, practices without a fixed abode. Not apprehending the thought "I am practicing," such a one relies on wisdom; The unborn and intelligent touch the supreme peace of meditative stabilization.
examples.gm: Whoever does not practice regarding form, feeling, perception, or volition, And does not practice regarding consciousness, practices without dwelling. Not apprehending what is called "practicing," they rely on wisdom. Possessing the intelligence of the unborn, they contact the supreme, peaceful samādhi.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतनाया विज्ञानि यो न चरती अनिकेतचारी । चरतीति सो न उपगच्छति प्रज्ञधारी अनुपादधी स्पृशति शान्ति समाधि श्रेष्ठाम् ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, without deep understanding, regards Form, perception, feeling, intention, and consciousness As impermanent, they are practicing a counterfeit; The wise never cause the destruction of phenomena.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva, while lacking full understanding, Fully demonstrates form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness As impermanent, he acts upon fabrication; The wise never destroy dharmas.
examples.sa: सचि रूप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायां चित्तं अनित्य परिणामयि बोधिसत्त्वो । प्र(ति)वर्णिकाय चरते अप्रजानमानो न हि धर्म पण्डित विनाश करोति जातु ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.
examples.sa: रूपस्य दर्शनु अदर्शनु वेदनाये संज्ञाय दर्शनु अदर्शनु चेतनाये । विज्ञानचित्तमनुदर्शनु यत्र नास्ति अय धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्टु तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this person called a 'bodhisattva'?" They seek the total exhaustion of all attachment, cutting through attachment. They touch the unattached awakening of the Victors; Therefore, they receive the name "bodhisattva."
examples.gm: Why are they called a "bodhisattva"? They sever attachment, desiring the exhaustion of attachment to all things. They contact the unattached awakening of the Jinas; Therefore, they obtain the name of "bodhisattva."
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वत्र सङ्गक्रिय इच्छति सङ्गछेदी । बोधिं स्पृशिष्यति जिनान असङ्गभूतां तस्माद्धि नाम लभते अयु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: When one whose conduct is completely pure does not engage with form, And does not engage with consciousness, perception, feeling, or intention, Practicing in that way, they completely abandon all attachments, And, liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: Whoever, with perfectly pure conduct, does not practice in form, And does not practice in consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition, Practicing like that, entirely abandoning all attachment, Liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: रूपस्मि यो न चरते परिशुद्धचारी विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायाम् । एवं चरन्तु परिवर्जयि सर्वसङ्गां सङ्गाद् विमुच्य चरते सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva who practices in this way, Having severed attachment, moves through the world without clinging, Like the sun shining brightly when freed from the eclipse of Rāhu, Or like a fire that blazes, consuming grass, wood, and forests.
examples.gm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva practicing like that, Having cut off attachment, goes among beings without attachment, Remaining brightly like the sun freed from the eclipse of Rāhu, And like a spreading fire burning grass, trees, and forests.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो सङ्गा उछिन्नु व्रजते जगती असक्तो । सूर्यो व राहुग्रहमुक्त विरोचमानो अग्नीव युक्त तृणकाष्ठवनं दहाति ॥

examples.dm: Possessing great generosity, great intelligence, and great power, They have entered the supreme Great Vehicle of the Victors; Clad in great armor, they subdue the illusions of Māra; For that reason, they are truly called "great beings."
examples.gm: Great giving, great intelligence, and great power, Entering into the supreme Great Vehicle of the Jinas, Donning the great armor and subduing the illusions of Mara; Therefore they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महनायको महतबुद्धि महानुभावो महयान उत्तमजिनान समाधिरूढो । महता सनद्धु नमुचिं शठ धर्षयिष्ये महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, having heard that these phenomena are like emanations and illusions, Is without doubt and repeatedly practices the training, Know that such a person has long since entered the Mahayana, And has performed service to many tens of billions of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whoever, having heard that these dharmas are like emanations and illusions, Without doubt, trains and continuously applies themselves, That being should be known to have entered the Great Vehicle long ago, And to have served many tens of millions of billions of Buddhas.
examples.sa: चिरयानप्रस्थितु स वेदयितव्य सत्त्वो बहुबुद्धकोटिनयुतेहि कृताधिकारो । यो श्रुत्व धर्मि इमि निर्मितमायकल्पां न च काङ्क्षते अयु प्रयुज्यति शिक्षमाणः ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening?" It is because by mounting it, one delivers all sentient beings from suffering. This vehicle is a vast celestial palace, as immense as space; It is the supreme vehicle, the means for fully attaining joy, delight, and bliss.
examples.gm: Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Mounting it, all sentient beings pass beyond sorrow. This vehicle is a great immeasurable palace like space, The supreme vehicle, which brings about the attainment of joy, happiness, and bliss.
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधियानो यत्रारुहित्व स निर्वापयि सर्वसत्त्वान् । आकाशतुल्य अयु यान महाविमानो सुखसौख्यक्षेमभिप्रापणु यानश्रेष्ठो ॥

examples.dm: One who does not dwell in form, does not dwell in feeling, One who does not dwell in perception, does not dwell in volition, And one who does not dwell in consciousness, dwells in the nature of reality; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling, Whoever does not abide in perception, does not abide in volition, And whoever does not abide in consciousness, abides in the nature of phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: रुपस्मि यो न स्थिहते न च वेदनायां संज्ञाय यो न स्थिहते न च चेतनायाम् । विज्ञानि यो न स्थिहते स्थितु धर्मतायां एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Whether the wise remain in the world or pass into nirvāṇa, This flawless true nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, remains. Bodhisattvas realize this suchness; And therefore, the Buddha is given the name "Tathāgata."
examples.gm: Whether the wise remain in the world or have passed into nirvāṇa, This flawless dharmatā, the emptiness of dharmas, remains; Bodhisattvas subsequently realize this suchness, Therefore, the Buddhas are given the name Tathāgata.
examples.sa: तिष्ठन्तु लोकविदुनां परिनिर्वृतानां स्थित एष धर्मतनियाम शून्यधर्मा । तां बोधिसत्त्व तथताम् अनुबुद्धयन्ति तस्मा हु बुद्ध कृत नाम तथागतेभिः ॥

examples.dm: Just as a king does not travel to towns or the countryside, Yet from within his own domain he gathers all that is collected, A bodhisattva does not go anywhere away from the nature of phenomena, Yet they gather all the qualities of the state of buddhahood.
examples.gm: Just as a king does not go to villages and does not go to provinces, But gathers all the revenue from his own realm, The dharmatā of the bodhisattvas does not go anywhere, But gathers all the qualities of the Buddha grounds.
examples.sa: न च राज ग्राम व्रजते न च राज्यराष्ट्रान् सर्वं च आददति सो विषयातु आयम् । न च बोधिसत्त्व चलते क्वचि धर्मतायां सर्वांश्च आददति ये गुण बुद्धधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like being stricken by poison through the mere perception of suspicion; Even if that poison has not entered the body, one will fall unconscious. Likewise, the childish who claim "I" and "mine," Have the notion of a self, and through unreal conceptualization, are born and die in impermanence.
examples.gm: For example, just as poison aroused by the perception of suspicion, Even if that poison has not gone inside, one will faint; Likewise, childish beings, accepting self and what belongs to self, Perceiving that self, which is not real, constantly are born and die.
examples.sa: यथ शङ्कितेन विषसंज्ञत अभ्युपैति नो चास्य कोष्ठगतु सो विषु पात्यते च । एमेव बालुपगतो अहु मह्य एषो अहसंज्ञि जायि म्रियते च सदा अभूतो ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, without deep understanding, regards Form, perception, feeling, intention, and consciousness As impermanent, they are practicing a counterfeit; The wise never cause the destruction of phenomena.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva, while lacking full understanding, Fully demonstrates form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness As impermanent, he acts upon fabrication; The wise never destroy dharmas.
examples.sa: सचि रूप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायां चित्तं अनित्य परिणामयि बोधिसत्त्वो । प्र(ति)वर्णिकाय चरते अप्रजानमानो न हि धर्म पण्डित विनाश करोति जातु ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: One should understand that the purity of form is the purity of the fruition; The purity of the fruition and the purity of form become the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruition, and the purity of form Are like the element of space—indivisible and inseparable.
examples.gm: The purity of form should be known as the purity of the fruit; The purity of the fruit and form becomes the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form Are equal to the realm of space, indivisible and unseverable.
examples.sa: रूपस्य शुद्धि फलशुद्धित वेदितव्या फलरूपशुद्धित सर्वज्ञतशुद्धिम् आहुः । सर्वज्ञताय फलशुद्धित रूपशुद्धी आकाशधातुसमताय अभिन्नछिन्नाः ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Whoever, as a protector, practices this perfection of wisdom, And whoever holds and masters it with devotion, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water; Mara and the factions of Mara will find no opportunity to harm them.
examples.gm: The perfection of wisdom, in which the Protectors practice— Whoever respects, apprehends, and masters it, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water, And Māra and the factions of Māra will find no opportunity against them.
examples.sa: य इमां ग्रहीष्यति पर्यापुणती स नित्यं प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति नाथाः । विष वह्नि शस्त्र उदकं न क्रमाति तस्यो ओतारु मारु न च विन्दति मारपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: The nature of all objective referents is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless. The nature of the expanse of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.gm: The nature of objects of apprehension is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless; The nature of the realm of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.sa: आरम्बणान प्रकृती स अ(न)न्तपारा सत्त्वान या च प्रकृती स अनन्तपारा । आकाशधातुप्रकृती स अनन्तपारा प्रज्ञा पि लोकविदुनां स अनन्तपारा ॥

examples.dm: If, while dedicating, the notion of a mind arises, Or the notion of enlightenment, or the notion of sentient beings, Then because of such notions, one dwells in views and the mind is attached to the three; Because there is an object of observation, it is not a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If, when dedicating, the notion of 'mind' arises, If there is the notion of awakening, the notion of dedicating, and the notion of sentient beings, Because of these notions, residing in views, the mind is attached to the three; Since there are apprehensions, it does not amount to dedication.
examples.sa: परिणामयन्तु यदि वर्तति चित्तसंज्ञा तथ बोधिसत्त्वपरिणामन सत्त्वसंज्ञा । संज्ञाय दृष्टिस्थितु चित्त त्रिसङ्गयुक्तो परिणामितं न भवती उपलभ्यमानम् ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Just as seeds that are sown and remain in the earth will eventually grow, Once the assembly of conditions is found, diverse forms are fully produced; The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them are born from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Seeds, having been sown and resting in the earth, will arise; Having found the proper conditions, many kinds of forms are fully produced. The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them also are produced from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: How could billions of blind people, lacking a guide, Ever know the path or enter the city? Without wisdom, these five perfections are sightless; Lacking a guide, they are unable to reach enlightenment.
examples.gm: Hundreds of billions of blind people without a guide, Not even knowing the way, how could they enter the city? Without wisdom, these five blind perfections, Being without a guide, are unable to touch awakening.
examples.sa: जात्यन्धकोटिनियुतान्यविनायकानां मार्गे अकोविदु कुतो नगरप्रवेशे । विन प्रज्ञ पञ्च इमि पारमिता अचक्षुः अविनायका न प्रभवन्ति स्पृशेतु बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, these five perfections of the Victors Also acquire the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When they are fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, known as "awakening."
examples.gm: Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also Will attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित नामतया भवन्ति । सर्वज्ञताय परिणामयमाण सर्वे षडपीह एकनयम् अर्छति बोधिनामा ॥

examples.dm: The Victor, having been asked a question by Śakra, replied: If there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would still take this very Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Victor fully asked Śakra a question, and he replied: "Even if there were buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनेन परिपृच्छितु प्रश्नमाहु सचि गङ्गवालिकसमा सिय बुद्धक्षेत्राः । जिनधातु सर्वि परिपूरित चूडिबद्धा इमम् एव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताहु गृह्णे ॥

examples.dm: If no sprout exists, a tree could never grow in the world; In that case, how could branches, flowers, and fruit ever appear? If the mind of enlightenment did not exist, no Victors would ever arise in the world; And if so, how could the fruits—Indra, Brahmā, and the Hearers—ever appear?
examples.gm: If the emergence of a tree in the world never happens without a sprout, How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it? If the emergence of a Victor in the world does not exist without the mind of awakening, How could the fruits of Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas emerge?
examples.sa: असतोऽङ्कुरस्य द्रुमसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शाखपत्रफलपुष्पौपादु तत्र । विन बोधिचित्त जिनसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शक्रब्रह्मफल श्रावकप्रादुभावः ॥

examples.dm: The fourth chapter explains the complete realization of all aspects. Śakra, the king of the gods, asked the Victor: "How do Bodhisattvas practicing wisdom apply diligence?" "They do not apply even a particle of diligence toward the aggregates or the elements; Not applying diligence toward the aggregates is the Bodhisattva's diligence."
examples.gm: The fourth chapter: teaching the complete realization of all aspects. The king of gods, Śakra, asked the Victor: "How does a bodhisattva strive in the practice of wisdom?" "They do not strive even a speck of dust in the aggregates and elements; Not striving in the aggregates, that is the striving of a bodhisattva."
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनस्य परिपृच्छति देवराजो चरमाण प्रज्ञ कथ युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । अणुमात्र यो न खलु युज्यति स्कन्धधातौ यो एव युज्यति स युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वः ॥

examples.dm: The Victor, having been asked a question by Śakra, replied: If there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would still take this very Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Victor fully asked Śakra a question, and he replied: "Even if there were buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनेन परिपृच्छितु प्रश्नमाहु सचि गङ्गवालिकसमा सिय बुद्धक्षेत्राः । जिनधातु सर्वि परिपूरित चूडिबद्धा इमम् एव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताहु गृह्णे ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? It is not that I lack respect for the bodily relics; However, because they are completely suffused with wisdom, they are worthy of worship. For example, just as a person who relies on a king receives honor, So too the relics of the Buddha rely upon the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: "If asked why, it is not that I am disrespectful of the bodily relics; But because they are fully permeated by wisdom, they are worshipped. For example, just as a man relying on a king obtains reverence, The relics of the Buddha rely on the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: किं कारणं न मि शरीरि अगौरवत्वं अपि तू खु प्रज्ञपरिभावित पूजयन्ति । यथ राजनिश्रित नरो लभि सर्वि पूजां तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित बुद्धधातुः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom, The Victors receive worship of their relics even after they have passed into nirvana. Therefore, those who wish to grasp the qualities of the Victors Should take up this perfection of wisdom; it is liberation.
examples.gm: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even though the Victors pass into nirvana, their relics gain worship. Therefore, whoever wishes to hold the qualities of the Victors Should take up the perfection of wisdom; this is liberation.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितागुणानि यन्निर्वृतेऽपि जिनधातु लभन्ति पूजाम् । तस्मा हु तान् जिनगुणा(न्) परिघेत्तुकामो सो प्रज्ञपारमित गृह्णतु एष मोक्षो ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, these five perfections of the Victors Also acquire the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When they are fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, known as "awakening."
examples.gm: Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also Will attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित नामतया भवन्ति । सर्वज्ञताय परिणामयमाण सर्वे षडपीह एकनयम् अर्छति बोधिनामा ॥

examples.dm: If one understands that these phenomena have ceased and are exhausted, And that which is dedicated is also exhausted, And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon, Then by knowing in such a way, it is a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If in this way one knows that this dharma has ceased and is exhausted, And that to which it is dedicated is also exhausted, And knows that a dharma is never dedicated to a dharma, Through knowing in that way, it is perfectly dedicated.
examples.sa: सचि एव जानति निरुध्यति क्षीणधर्मा तच्चैत क्षीण परिणामयिष्यन्ति यत्र । न च धर्म धर्मि परिणामयते कदाचित् परिणामितं भवति एव प्रजानमाने ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, those who have truly entered into supreme awakening should understand that by hearing This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Even if they have not received a direct prophecy from the Guide, "Before long, I shall touch the awakening of a Buddha."
examples.gm: Likewise, one who has fully entered supreme enlightenment Should be known as hearing this perfection of wisdom of the Victors; Even if they have not been directly prophesied by the Leaders, They think, 'Before long, I will touch the enlightenment of the Buddhas.'
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो श्रुणमाण प्रज्ञ इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् । यद्यापि संमुख न व्याकृतु नायकेनो तथपि स्पृशिष्यति नचिरेण हु बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Bodhisattvas who have entered the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on the perfections as their spiritual friends. Those who provide such instruction are the ground of accomplishment; Through these two causes, the awakening of a Buddha is swiftly realized.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on spiritual friends together with the perfections. Those who teach accordingly, this is the stage of accomplishment; By these two causes, they will swiftly realize the awakening of a Buddha.
examples.sa: बुद्धा य बोधिवरप्रस्थित बोधिसत्त्वा कल्याणमित्र इमि पारमिता निदिष्टाः । ते चानुशासक इयं प्रतिपत्तिभूमी दुवि कारणेन अनुबुध्यति बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: However much the hosts of śrāvakas generate a mass of merit Through being endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, It cannot match even a fraction of a bodhisattva’s single thought of rejoicing; The mass of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Even if however many hosts of śrāvakas generate collections of merit, Fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, Compared to a single mind of rejoicing of a bodhisattva, The heap of merit of the hosts of śrāvakas cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति श्रावकगणाः प्रसवन्ति पुण्यं दानं च शीलमपि भावनसंप्रयुक्तम् । स हि बोधिसत्त्व अनुमोदन एकचित्ते न च सर्वश्रावकगणे सिय पुण्यस्कन्धो ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who, for many billions of eons, Practices generosity toward Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas and maintains ethical discipline, Cannot match the merit of one who speaks of the Dharma that possesses the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even if that merit from giving and morality were spoken of well.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva, for many thousands of millions of eons, Gives gifts to arhats and pratyekabuddhas and observes ethical discipline, For anyone who teaches the dharma endowed with the supreme perfection of wisdom, Giving and ethical discipline do not bear a fraction of the goodness of that teaching.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व बहुकल्पसहस्रकोटयो दानं ददेयु विमलं तथ शील रक्षे । यश् चैव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रयुक्तो धर्मं भणेय कल पुण्य न दानशीले ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥
