examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: The great beings exist solely to bring sentient beings to maturity, To purify the fields, and to complete the perfections; They do not seek rebirth in the formless realm, thinking That the qualities of enlightenment and the perfections would thereby decline.
examples.gm: The great beings, to completely ripen sentient beings, Act only to purify the realms and complete the perfections; Thinking, "The qualities of awakening and the perfections will diminish," They do not seek birth in the formless realm.
examples.sa: अन्यत्र सत्त्वपरिपाचन क्षेत्रशोधी परिपूरणार्थ इमि पारमिता महात्मा । आरूप्यधातुउपपत्ति न प्रार्थयन्ती यत्रेह बोधिगुणपारमितान हानि ॥

examples.dm: If someone were to take as many sentient beings as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, And, having disciplined them all, establish them in the state of an arhat, Compared to one who writes down this perfection of wisdom, And gives the text to a supreme being, the merit of the latter is far more sublime.
examples.gm: Compared to someone who, in fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, Tames all however many beings reside there to arhatship, Whoever writes down this perfection of wisdom And gives the book to supreme beings has particularly exalted merit.
examples.sa: यावन्ति गङ्गनदिवालिकतुल्यक्षेत्रे तावन्ति सत्त्व अरहन्ति विनेय कश्चित् । यश् चैव प्रज्ञ इम पारमिता लिखित्वा परसत्त्वि पुस्तकु ददेय विशिष्टपुण्यः ॥

examples.dm: Even if all the sentient beings in realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges Were to be considered as having become Māras, And even if each of them emanated that many more from every single hair, All of them together would be unable to create obstacles for the wise.
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are in fields equal to the Ganges, If all of them, taking on assumed forms, became Māras, And even if they emanated that many from each and every single hair pore, All of them would not be able to cause hindrances for the wise.
examples.sa: यावन्ति गङ्गनदिवालिसमे हि क्षेत्रे सत्त्वा त सर्वि परिकल्प भवेयु माराः । एकैक रोम पुन तान्तक निर्मिणेय्या सर्वे न शक्य करणे विदु अन्तरायम् ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who abides in emptiness, Through aspirations based on the knowledge of sentient beings in the world, Manifests a great variety of diverse activities, Yet does not touch upon nirvana, nor do they remain in emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, Supported by aspirations knowing sentient beings among wanderers, Demonstrates many various kinds of activities, Does not touch nirvāṇa, and does not dwell in emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यतप्रतिष्ठितु एष सत्त्वो जगति क्रियां विविध दर्शयते विचित्राम् । सत्त्वान ज्ञानप्रणिधानअधिष्ठानमेव न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति शून्यत नास्ति स्थानम् ॥

examples.dm: If no sprout exists, a tree could never grow in the world; In that case, how could branches, flowers, and fruit ever appear? If the mind of enlightenment did not exist, no Victors would ever arise in the world; And if so, how could the fruits—Indra, Brahmā, and the Hearers—ever appear?
examples.gm: If the emergence of a tree in the world never happens without a sprout, How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it? If the emergence of a Victor in the world does not exist without the mind of awakening, How could the fruits of Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas emerge?
examples.sa: असतोऽङ्कुरस्य द्रुमसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शाखपत्रफलपुष्पौपादु तत्र । विन बोधिचित्त जिनसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शक्रब्रह्मफल श्रावकप्रादुभावः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, when seeking complete awakening, those who get to hear This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Will find relief and become fearless; This is not the level of an Arhat, nor the level of a Pratyekabuddha.
examples.gm: Likewise, when seeking enlightenment, whoever attains the hearing Of this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, They attain relief and become fearless— Not of the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमिता जिनानां शृणु तात यो लभति बोधि गवेषमाणः । आश्वासप्राप्त भवती न च तस्य त्रासो नार्हन्तभूमि न पि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमी ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Buddhas of the past, numbering tens of millions of billions, Who reside in infinitely many billions of fields, and those who have passed into parinirvāṇa, Those protectors of the world, Teach the precious Dharma for the sake of completely ending suffering.
examples.gm: Whatever tens of millions of hundreds of billions of buddhas of the past, And whoever resides in many infinite thousands of tens of millions of fields, And whatever protectors of the world who have passed into nirvāṇa, Demonstrate the precious dharma in order to exhaust suffering:
examples.sa: ये बुद्धकोटिनियुता पुरिमा व्यतीता ये वा अनन्तबहुक्षेत्रसहस्रकोटयः । तिष्ठन्ति येऽपि परिनिर्वृत लोकनाथा देशन्ति धर्मरतनं दुखसंक्षयाय ॥

examples.dm: This is the supreme treasure of Dharma and the most excellent Dharma treasury; It is the Buddha lineage, the treasury of happiness and joy for all beings. The protectors of the world in the ten directions—those of the past and those yet to come— All arise from this, yet the expanse of reality is never exhausted.
examples.gm: This is the supreme Dharma-treasure and the holy Dharma-treasury; It is the lineage of the Buddhas, the treasury of happiness and joy of beings. The protectors of the world of the past, future, and the ten directions, Though they are born from this, the dharmadhātu does not become exhausted.
examples.sa: अग्रं निधान अयु उत्तमधर्मकोश बुद्धान गोत्रजननं सुखसौख्यगञ्जो । अतिक्रान्तनागत दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत न च क्षीयति धर्मधातुः ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: The Buddha’s heirs, the listeners, the solitary realizers, the gods, And all the various phenomena of happiness and well-being for all beings, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom; Yet these wisdoms are also neither exhausted nor increased.
examples.gm: The sons of the Buddha, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and gods, And however many dharmas of happiness and joy of all beings there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom, And yet wisdom has no exhaustion and has no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त बुद्धसम श्रावकप्रत्ययाश् च मरुतश् च सर्वजगती सुखसौख्यधर्माः । सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूता न च क्षीयते न च विवर्धति जातु प्रज्ञा ॥

examples.dm: If, while dedicating, the notion of a mind arises, Or the notion of enlightenment, or the notion of sentient beings, Then because of such notions, one dwells in views and the mind is attached to the three; Because there is an object of observation, it is not a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If, when dedicating, the notion of 'mind' arises, If there is the notion of awakening, the notion of dedicating, and the notion of sentient beings, Because of these notions, residing in views, the mind is attached to the three; Since there are apprehensions, it does not amount to dedication.
examples.sa: परिणामयन्तु यदि वर्तति चित्तसंज्ञा तथ बोधिसत्त्वपरिणामन सत्त्वसंज्ञा । संज्ञाय दृष्टिस्थितु चित्त त्रिसङ्गयुक्तो परिणामितं न भवती उपलभ्यमानम् ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of intrinsic characteristics, One should understand that all these phenomena are likewise empty of such characteristics. When one thoroughly understands that all phenomena are empty and signless, To practice in such a manner is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of characteristics, Knowing all these phenomena to be similar to that characteristic, If one thoroughly knows phenomena as empty and signless, Practicing like that is the wisdom practice of the Sugata.
examples.sa: यथ प्रज्ञपारमित शून्यत लक्षणेन तथलक्षणा य इमि जानति सर्वधर्मान् । शून्यानलक्षण प्रजानयमान धर्मान् एवं चरन्तु चरती सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who, while practicing in the past, Practiced this perfection skillfully and without doubt, Will, upon hearing this, immediately perceive it as the Teacher, And will quickly realize the peace of awakening.
examples.gm: When a bodhisattva practiced previously, The wise one practicing this perfection has no doubt. As soon as they hear it, they give rise to the notion of the Teacher; They will swiftly realize peaceful awakening.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व वरपारमितेति चीर्णो परिचारिका य न च काङ्क्षति पण्डितेहि । सह श्रुत्व तस्य पुन भेष्यति शास्तृसंज्ञा सो वा लघू अनुबुधिष्यति बोधि शान्ताम् ॥

examples.dm: Supreme enlightenment is not reached by the initial mind, Yet without that initial mind, it cannot be reached. Peaceful enlightenment is not attained by the final mind, Yet without that, it is also impossible to attain it.
examples.gm: By the first mind, supreme awakening is not touched, Yet without it, one is not able to touch it. By the final mind, peaceful awakening is not attained, Yet without it, one is not able to attain it.
examples.sa: प्रथमेव चित्त स्पृशती न च अग्रबोधिम् असता न तस्य स्पृशता पुन शक्य भोन्ति । न च चित्त पश्चिम शिवाम् अनुप्रापुणाति असता न तस्य पुन प्रापणनाय शक्यम् ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the knowledge of all bases
examples.gm: Teaching on the Knowledge of All Bases

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: These beings are stuck in the mire of name and form; They wander in the wheel of cyclic existence, which is like a wheel driven by wind. Knowing that deluded beings are like deer caught in a snare, Those endowed with wisdom move through the sky like birds.
examples.gm: These wandering beings are attached to the mud of name and form; They wander in the wheel of samsara like a wheel of wind. Knowing that deluded beings are like deer caught in a snare, The wise one roams like a bird in the sky.
examples.sa: नामेव रूपि जगती अयु पङ्कसक्ता संसारचक्रि भ्रमतेऽनिलचक्रतुल्ये । जानित्व भ्रान्तु जगती मृगवागुरेव आकाश पक्षिसदृशा विचरन्ति प्रज्ञाः ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings, completely famished, desire food, And those with minds attached to cyclic existence wander perpetually. The two phenomena of "self" and "mine" are unreal and empty; Yet the foolish, by their own doing, tie knots in the sky.
examples.gm: Fully starving sentient beings desire food, and Those possessing a mind attached to saṃsāra constantly wander. Both self and the phenomena of self are unreal and empty; Childish beings themselves have cast a knot in space.
examples.sa: आहारकाम परिकल्पयमान सत्त्वाः संसारि युक्तमनसः सद संस्मरन्ति । अहु मह्य धर्म उभि एति अभूत शून्या आकाशगण्ठि अयु आत्मन बद्ध बाले ॥

examples.dm: When one whose conduct is completely pure does not engage with form, And does not engage with consciousness, perception, feeling, or intention, Practicing in that way, they completely abandon all attachments, And, liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: Whoever, with perfectly pure conduct, does not practice in form, And does not practice in consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition, Practicing like that, entirely abandoning all attachment, Liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: रूपस्मि यो न चरते परिशुद्धचारी विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायाम् । एवं चरन्तु परिवर्जयि सर्वसङ्गां सङ्गाद् विमुच्य चरते सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all the knowledge and liberations Of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; He does not abide in those, nor does he abide in the primordial wisdom of a Buddha; He does not abide in the unconditioned; he is one who knows the nature of the path.
examples.gm: Likewise, a brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all The knowledges and liberations of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; They do not dwell in them, nor do they dwell in the Buddha's pristine wisdom; They do not dwell in the unconditioned, but know the nature of the path.
examples.sa: तथ ज्ञान श्रावकविमुक्तिसप्रत्ययानां सर्वत्र भोति कुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । नो चापि तत्र स्थिहते न च बुद्धज्ञाने न च संस्कृते भवति मार्गविदू विधिज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the complete realization of all aspects
examples.gm: Teaching on the Clear Realization of All Aspects

examples.dm: The fourth chapter explains the complete realization of all aspects. Śakra, the king of the gods, asked the Victor: "How do Bodhisattvas practicing wisdom apply diligence?" "They do not apply even a particle of diligence toward the aggregates or the elements; Not applying diligence toward the aggregates is the Bodhisattva's diligence."
examples.gm: The fourth chapter: teaching the complete realization of all aspects. The king of gods, Śakra, asked the Victor: "How does a bodhisattva strive in the practice of wisdom?" "They do not strive even a speck of dust in the aggregates and elements; Not striving in the aggregates, that is the striving of a bodhisattva."
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनस्य परिपृच्छति देवराजो चरमाण प्रज्ञ कथ युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । अणुमात्र यो न खलु युज्यति स्कन्धधातौ यो एव युज्यति स युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, those who have truly entered into supreme awakening should understand that by hearing This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Even if they have not received a direct prophecy from the Guide, "Before long, I shall touch the awakening of a Buddha."
examples.gm: Likewise, one who has fully entered supreme enlightenment Should be known as hearing this perfection of wisdom of the Victors; Even if they have not been directly prophesied by the Leaders, They think, 'Before long, I will touch the enlightenment of the Buddhas.'
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो श्रुणमाण प्रज्ञ इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् । यद्यापि संमुख न व्याकृतु नायकेनो तथपि स्पृशिष्यति नचिरेण हु बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, those who seek supreme enlightenment, Being wise and possessing intense resolve, should utterly conquer pride; Just as a multitude of the sick rely on a physician for healing, One should rely on a spiritual friend without any distraction.
examples.gm: Therefore, one who seeks holy awakening, A wise one possessing strong intention, having definitely destroyed pride, Just as a multitude of sick people rely on a doctor to be cured, Should rely on spiritual friends without wavering.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु मानु निहनित्वन पण्डितेन गुरुआशयेन वरबोधि गवेषमाणः । वैद्यो व आतुर स्वरोगचिकित्सनार्थं कल्याणमित्र भजितव्य अतन्द्रितेन ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme Perfection of Wisdom, Do not see any increase or decrease in form. One who does not see phenomena, non-phenomena, or the sphere of phenomena, And does not touch nirvana, is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: When practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, the yogi Does not see the increase or complete decrease of form; Whoever does not see dharma, non-dharma, or the dharmadhātu, And does not touch nirvāṇa, they abide in wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी न च रूपवृद्धि न च पश्यति पारिहाणिम् । धर्मा अधर्म इमु पश्यति धर्मधातुं न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Subhūti asked the Buddha, the Moon of Speakers: "What are the obstacles for those who delight in virtuous qualities?" The Teacher replied: "The obstacles that will arise are many; Of those, I shall briefly describe just a few."
examples.gm: Subhūti asked the Buddha, the moon among speakers: What are the obstacles for those who delight in qualities? The Teacher replied: There are many obstacles; Of those, I will fully explain just a few for now.
examples.sa: बुद्धं सुभूति परिपृच्छति वादिचन्द्रं क्यन्तन्तरायु भविष्यन्ति गुणे रतानाम् । बहु अन्तरायु भविष्यन्ति भणाति शास्त ततु अल्पमात्र परिकीर्तयिष्यामि तावत् ॥

examples.dm: Thus did the elder Subhūti request of the Protector of the World: "Please explain the signs of the ocean of qualities free from afflictions, And how those of great power do not turn back; O Victor, please grant a prophecy regarding even a mere portion of such qualities."
examples.gm: The elder Subhūti thoroughly requested the Protector of the World: "Ocean of Qualities, please teach the signs of those free from afflictions. How those of great power will not turn back again— Thus, may the Victor explain just a fraction of their qualities."
examples.sa: स्थविरो सुभूति परिपृच्छति लोकनाथं अरणाय लिङ्ग भणही गुणसागराणाम् । अविवर्तिया यथ भवन्ति महानुभावा तां व्याकुरुष्व जिनगुणान प्रदेशमात्रम् ॥

examples.dm: At that time, these activities of Māra will occur. At that time, after many monks have been stirred to agitation, Many other various obstacles will also arise, Which prevent them from upholding this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: At that time, this work of Māra will arise: At that time, whoever disturbs many monks, They will not uphold this perfection of wisdom; And many other various obstacles will also arise.
examples.sa: इमि मारकर्म भविष्यन्ति य तस्मि काले अन्ये च नेक विविधा बहु अन्तराया । येही समाकुलिकृता बहु भिक्षु तत्र प्रज्ञाय पारमित एतु न धारयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles Might remain in the sky and simultaneously display various transformations; He demonstrates walking, moving, lying down, and sitting, And he does not grow weary, nor does he become exhausted.
examples.gm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles, Abiding in space, simultaneously emanates magical creations, Demonstrating walking, pacing, sleeping, and sitting; He has no weariness, and he has no fatigue.
examples.sa: भिक्षू यथा परमऋद्धिबलेनुपेतो गगने स्थितो यमक कुर्वति प्रातिहार्यां । गतिचंक्रमं शयनिषद्य निदर्शयाति न निवर्तते न पि च खिद्यति याव तत्र ॥

examples.dm: For those small-minded beings who have newly entered the vehicle, If they have not attained this rare and precious jewel, Mara will strive to create obstacles for them; The Buddhas of the ten directions apply themselves to protecting them.
examples.gm: Sentient beings of small intellect who have newly entered the vehicle, Who have not found this rare jewel— In order to create obstacles for them, Māra will become energetic; But the Buddhas of the ten directions will apply themselves to fully protecting them.
examples.sa: नवयानप्रस्थित स सत्त्व परीत्तबुद्धिः य इमं दुर्लाभु धर्मरतनं परापुणन्ति । मारोऽत्र उत्सुकु भविष्यति अन्तराये बुद्धा दशद्दिशि परिग्रहसंप्रयुक्ताः ॥

examples.dm: Even if all the sentient beings in realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges Were to be considered as having become Māras, And even if each of them emanated that many more from every single hair, All of them together would be unable to create obstacles for the wise.
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are in fields equal to the Ganges, If all of them, taking on assumed forms, became Māras, And even if they emanated that many from each and every single hair pore, All of them would not be able to cause hindrances for the wise.
examples.sa: यावन्ति गङ्गनदिवालिसमे हि क्षेत्रे सत्त्वा त सर्वि परिकल्प भवेयु माराः । एकैक रोम पुन तान्तक निर्मिणेय्या सर्वे न शक्य करणे विदु अन्तरायम् ॥

examples.dm: When a mother falls ill, though she has many children, They all become distressed and perform healing rites for her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions Direct their intention toward this supreme Perfection of Wisdom, who is their mother.
examples.gm: When a mother becomes sick and has many sons, They all become unhappy and attend upon her. Likewise, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions also Keep in mind this holy wisdom, which is their mother.
examples.sa: मात्राय पुत्र बहु सन्ति गिलानि काये ते सर्वि दुर्मनस तत्र प्रयुज्ययेयुः । एमेव बुद्धपिं दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात्र समन्वाहरन्ति ॥

examples.dm: To those who practice skillfully in this way, the many hosts of gods Join their palms in reverence and prostrate. All the Buddhas throughout the world systems of the ten directions Likewise utter garlands of praise for their qualities.
examples.gm: To the wise who practice thus, many hosts of gods Join their palms, bow down, and pay homage; And however many Buddhas there are in the world systems of the ten directions, They completely proclaim a garland of praise for their qualities.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु ना पृथुदेवसंघाः कृतअञ्जलीपुट प्रणम्य नमस्ययन्ति । बुद्धा पि यावत दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ गुणवर्णमालपरिकीर्तन कुर्वयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Those who have firm faith in the Sugatas and bodhisattvas, And whose intentions are focused on the supreme perfection of wisdom, Having completely transcended the two levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, May they swiftly attain the unassailable awakening of the Victors.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva has firm faith in the Sugata, And applies their mind to the supreme perfection of wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, Will quickly attain the unconquerable enlightenment of the Victors.
examples.sa: यस्यामि श्रद्ध सुगते दृढ बोधिसत्त्वो वरप्रज्ञपारमित आशयसंप्रयोगो । अतिक्रम्य भूमिद्वय श्रावकप्रत्ययानां लघु प्राप्स्यते अनभिभू(तु) जिनान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may possess great faith, If they lack wisdom, they will quickly deteriorate. When faith is fully embraced by wisdom, They will transcend the two levels and attain supreme awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may have much faith, If they are completely lacking in wisdom, they will quickly become unfit. If their faith is fully embraced by wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds, they will attain supreme enlightenment.
examples.sa: किंचापि श्रद्धबहुलो सिय बोधिसत्त्वो प्रज्ञाविहीन विलयं लघु प्रापुणाति । तं चैव श्रद्ध परिगृह्णयमान प्रज्ञा अतिक्रम्य बोधिद्वय प्राप्स्यति अग्रबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings delight in foundations and desire sense objects; Abiding in grasping, they are unskilled, foolish, and deluded like darkness. The phenomena to be attained are without foundation and without grasping; Therefore, conflict with the world arises.
examples.gm: Beings delight in resting places and desire sense objects; Abiding in grasping, the unwise are foolish and obscured like darkness. The dharma to be attained is without resting place and without grasping; Therefore, conflict arises with the worlds.
examples.sa: सत्त्वश् च आलयरतो विषयाभिलाषी स्थित अग्रहे अबुध यो महअन्धभूतो । धर्मो अनालयु अनाग्रहु प्रापितव्यो लोकेन सार्ध अयु विग्रहु प्रादुभूतो ॥

examples.dm: Those of great renown don the armor of difficult deeds, Which is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources. They are free from the concept of the three vehicles and have no grasping; They are irreversible, unwavering, and possess the quality of being imperturbable.
examples.gm: Those endowed with great renown don the armor that is difficult to do; It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. They are free from the perception of the three vehicles and have no grasping. They are irreversible, unwavering, and of unperturbed nature.
examples.sa: संनाहु दुष्करू महायशु संनहन्ती न च स्कन्धधातु न च आयतनैः सनद्धाः । त्रिभि यानसंज्ञविगता अपरिगृहीता अविवर्तिका अचलिताश्च अकोप्यधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who has become profound in that way, And who realizes this Dharma—the ultimate, unattached vehicle in which aggregates, Elements, and sense sources do not exist— What could there be that is a more perfect accomplishment of merit than that?
examples.gm: For any bodhisattva who realizes this profound Vehicle, ultimate and unattached, wherein the aggregates, Elements, and sense-sources do not exist— What perfectly accomplished merit is there beyond that?
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व इमु बुध्यति एव धर्मां गम्भीरयानपरमार्थनिरुपलेपान् । यस्मिन् न स्कन्ध न पि आयतनं न धातु किं वा स्वपुण्यसमुदागमु किंचि तस्य ॥

examples.dm: Just as a bird with a massive body of one hundred and fifty yojanas, If its wings are exhausted and it lacks strength and skill, Even if it leaps from the Abode of the Thirty-Three to this world of Jambudvīpa, It will surely meet with disaster and ruin.
examples.gm: If a bird with a large body of one hundred and fifty yojanas, Whose wings are worn out, lacks strength and skill, And jumps from the abode of the Thirty-Three to this Jambudvīpa, In jumping itself, it will come to ruin there.
examples.sa: पक्षिस्य योजनशतं महतात्मभावो पञ्चाशता पि अबलोभयक्षीणपक्षो । सो त्रायत्रिंशभवनादिषु जम्बुद्वीपे आत्मानमोसरियि तं विलयं व्रजेय्या ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like a person of Jambudvīpa who had never before Reached the supreme city of the gods, but later goes there; Having seen those lands that are fully possessed there, Just as one who returns here does not become attached,
examples.gm: For example, if a man of Jambudvīpa who previously Had not gone to the supreme city of the gods of the divine realm were to go later, Having seen those completely possessed objects, When he returns here, he does not become attached to them;
examples.sa: यथ जम्बुद्वीपक मनुष्य अलब्धपूर्वा दिवि देवौत्तमपुरा अनुप्रापुणेया । पश्यित्व ते विषय तत्र परिगृहीता पुनरागमेय न च निश्रयु तत्र कुर्यात् ॥

examples.dm: Pure and wearing clean robes, they are pure in the three isolations; They do not desire gain, and like great bulls, they always long for the Dharma. They have transcended the realm of Māra and are not dependent on others; They meditate on the four concentrations, yet do not dwell within those concentrations.
examples.gm: Making themselves clean and wearing clean clothes, the three are isolated and pure; Without desire for gain, the supreme leaders always desire the dharma. Passed beyond the realm of Māra and not placing themselves under the control of others, Meditating on the four dhyānas, they do not abide in those dhyānas.
examples.sa: शुचिशौचअम्बरधरा त्रिविवेकशुद्धा न च लाभकाम वृषभा सद धर्मकामाः । मारस्यतीतविषया अपरप्रणेया चतुध्यानध्यायि न च निश्रित तत्र ध्याने ॥

examples.dm: Possessing great power, they also dwell in the four concentrations, Yet they do not rely upon them, nor do they make them a fixed abode. Nevertheless, these four concentrations, along with their respective branches, Serve as the basis for attaining the supreme and most excellent awakening.
examples.gm: Endowed with great power, they even abide in the four dhyānas; They do not rely on them and do not abide in them; Nevertheless, these four dhyānas along with their branches, Become the support for attaining supreme holy awakening.
examples.sa: चतुर्भी च ध्यान विहरन्ति महानुभावा न च आलयो न पि च निश्रयु कुर्वयाति । अपि खो पुनाश्रयु इमे चतुध्यान साङ्गा भेष्यन्ति बोधिवर-उत्तमप्रापणाय ॥

examples.dm: They do not desire fame, and their minds are not entangled by anger. Even if they live as householders, they are always without attachment to any material things. For the sake of their livelihood, they do not seek out vast possessions. They do not practice wrathful spells of violence, nor do they practice spells for union with women.
examples.gm: Not desiring fame, their minds are not wrapped by anger. Even if they are householders, they are always unattached to all things. For the sake of livelihood, they do not seek resources through appalling means. They do not practice mantras of fierce actions, nor mantras for uniting men and women.
examples.sa: न च कीर्तिकाम न च क्रोधपरीतचित्ता गृहिभूत नित्य अनध्योषित सर्व वस्तुं । न च जीविकाविषयभोग गवेषयन्ति अभिचारमन्त्र न च इस्त्रिप्रयोगमन्त्राः ॥

examples.dm: It does not abide within the dharmadhātu or suchness; For example, like a cloud in the sky, it abides without a place to abide. A mantra-holder, a sky-traveler without a fixed abode, desiring a place to stay, Through the power of mantra, blesses trees to be endowed with out-of-season flowers.
examples.gm: They do not dwell in the dharmadhātu or suchness, For example, like clouds in space, they dwell without dwelling. A mantra-holder, without a dwelling, moving in space, wishing to dwell, By the power of mantras, is endowed with out-of-season flowers and blesses them.
examples.sa: न च धर्मधातुतथताय उपैति स्थानं भवती अथानस्थित सो लघु अन्तरीक्षे । विद्याधरो व अभिलम्भु वनाभिप्राया खगु कालहीन द्रुम मन्त्रबलाधिष्ठानो ॥

examples.dm: They do not act as diviners, predicting whether those engaged in desire will have a boy or a girl. They strive in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which is utterly secluded, free from strife and contention, and their minds of loving-kindness are firm. Desiring omniscience, they are steadfast and possess a mind constantly dedicated to it.
examples.gm: They do not predict, saying, 'You will become a man or a woman engaged in actions of desire.' In the utterly isolated perfection of wisdom, they are free from conflict and dispute, and their mind of loving-kindness is firm. Desiring omniscience, they are steadfast and always endowed with a mind inclined toward it.
examples.sa: न च आदिशन्ति पुरुषैः स्त्रिय इच्छकर्मां प्रविविक्त प्रज्ञवरपारमिताभियुक्ताः । कलहाविवादविगता दृढमैत्रचित्ता सर्वज्ञकाम सद शासनि निम्नचित्ताः ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: For example, consider a man who indulges in desire and, Having made an appointment with a woman, fails to meet her; However many conceptual thoughts he experiences in his mind throughout a single day, For that many eons, the bodhisattva will achieve attainment.
examples.gm: For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire, Having made an appointment with a woman and not meeting her, However many discursive thoughts of his mind operate in a single day, The bodhisattva will gain that many eons.
examples.sa: यथ रागधर्मचरितः पुरुषः स्त्रियाये संकेत कृत्व अलभन्तु विवर्तयेया । यावन्ति चित्तचरिता दिवसेन तस्य तावन्त कल्प अनुबुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: Just as a water jar is gradually filled from the first drop to the last, Little by little, it is completely filled; So too, the initial mind is the cause of supreme enlightenment, And by gradually perfecting virtuous qualities, one becomes a Buddha.
examples.gm: By drops of water, a vase from the first to the last, Is gradually, little by little, fully filled—just as, Likewise, the first mind too is the cause of supreme awakening, Gradually, perfecting white virtues, one becomes a buddha.
examples.sa: उदकबिन्दु कुम्भ परिपूर्यति स्तोकस्तोकं प्रथमे निपाति अनुपूर्व स पश्चिमेन । एमेव चित्त प्रथमं वरबोधिहेतुर् अनुपूर्व शुक्लगुणपूर्ण भवन्ति बुद्धाः ॥

examples.dm: Through diligence, virtuous qualities will not decline; One will find the treasury of the Victors, which is infinite primordial wisdom. Through meditative concentration, one abandons the base qualities of sensual desire; One fully accomplishes knowledge, supernormal powers, and meditative absorption.
examples.gm: By diligence, pure qualities will not diminish, And infinite pristine wisdom, the treasury of the Victors, will be found. By concentration, the despised qualities of desire are discarded, And knowledge, superknowledges, and samadhi are accomplished.
examples.sa: वीर्येण शुक्लगुण हानि न अभ्युपैति ज्ञानं अनन्त लभते जिनकोशगञ्जम् । ध्यानेन कामगुण उत्सृजते जुगुप्स्यान् विद्या अभिज्ञ अभिनिर्हरते समाधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the skillful bodhisattva also, Generates great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, And having completely transcended the four Māras and even the two levels, Abides in supreme meditative absorption, yet does not touch upon awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, at that time, a skilled bodhisattva, Generating great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, Having utterly passed beyond the four māras and the two, Dwells in the supreme samādhi and does not touch awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव यस्मि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो महमैत्रि सर्वि उपबन्धति सत्त्वधातौ । चतुरो स मार अतिक्रम्य द्वये च भूमिम् अस्मिन् समाधि स्थितु नो च स्पृशाति बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Through four causes, the wise and powerful bodhisattva Is difficult for the four Māras to overcome and cannot be shaken: Abiding in emptiness, never forsaking sentient beings, Acting exactly as one speaks, and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: By four causes, the wise bodhisattva possesses strength, Is hard to overcome by the four Māras, and cannot be moved: Dwelling in emptiness, not forsaking sentient beings, Acting as they have spoken, and possessing the blessing of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: चतुकारणेहि बलवां विदु बोधिसत्त्वो भवते दुघर्षु चतुमारअसंप्रकम्प्यो । शून्याविहारि भवते न च सत्त्वत्यागी यथवादि सत्त्वकरुणानुगतावस्थानः ॥

examples.dm: Wind relies upon space, and the mass of water relies upon that. This great earth relies upon that, and living beings rely upon it. Such is the causal basis for sentient beings' engagement in karma; Reflect on the meaning of this: upon what does space abide?
examples.gm: Wind is supported on space, on that is supported the mass of water, On that is supported this great earth, on that are supported living beings; Such is the cause of sentient beings engaging in karma; Think about this meaning of space being a pervasive foundation!
examples.sa: आकाशनिश्रित समीरण आपस्कन्धो त हि निश्रिता इह महापृथिवी जगच्च । सत्त्वान कर्म-उपभोगनिदानम् एव आकाशस्थानु कुतु चिन्तयि एतम् अर्थम् ॥

examples.dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: When a bodhisattva who is wise and clear-minded Practices this supreme samadhi of empty peace, During that time, one does not cultivate any signs; Abiding in the signless, one practices peace and utter tranquility.
examples.gm: Whenever a skilled and brilliant bodhisattva Engages in this supreme samādhi of peaceful emptiness, During that time they do not intensely cultivate signs; Dwelling in signlessness, they practice peace and profound peace.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो चरती इमां प्रवर शून्य समाधि शान्ताम् । अत्रान्तरे न च निमित्त प्रभावितव्यो न च आनिमित्तस्थितु शान्त प्रशान्तचारी ॥

examples.dm: If, having thoroughly inquired about their conduct and faculties, The bodhisattva does not fully demonstrate the dharmas of emptiness and signlessness, Nor explain the dharmas of the irreversible stage, One should understand that such a person has not been prophesied.
examples.gm: If, when completely questioned about their practice and faculties, A bodhisattva, the dharmas of emptiness and signlessness Does not completely teach, and the dharmas of the irreversible stage Does not explain, they should be known as unprophesied.
examples.sa: यदि पृच्छमान चरि इन्द्रिय बोधिसत्त्वो गम्भीरधर्मपरिदीपन नो करोति । शून्यानिमित्त अविवर्तियबोधिधर्मां न च शोचती न च स व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: A bird flying in the sky has no fixed station; It does not remain there, yet it does not fall to the ground. In this way, a bodhisattva who practices the gateways to liberation Does not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet does not engage with signs.
examples.gm: For a bird flying in the air, there is no place to abide; It does not abide there, nor does it fall to the ground. Likewise, a bodhisattva practicing in the doors of liberation Does not touch nirvāṇa and does not engage in signs.
examples.sa: पक्षिस्य नास्ति पदु गच्छत अन्तरीक्षे नो चापि तत्र स्थितु नो च पताति भूमौ । तथ बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु विमोक्षद्वारे न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति नो च निमित्तचारी ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the body of a magically conjured person is not invisible, And can be designated even by a name, Likewise, a bodhisattva who practices the doors of liberation Can be designated even by a name.
examples.gm: For example, just as an emanated human body is not invisible, And it can also be designated by a name; Likewise, a bodhisattva practicing in the doors of liberation Can also be designated by a name.
examples.sa: यथ निर्मितो पुरुष नो व अदृश्यकायो नामेन वा पुन स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः । तथ बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु विमोक्षद्वारं नामेन वा पुन स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Acting through wisdom, skillful means, strength, and miraculous powers, As long as their roots of virtue are not yet complete, So long will they not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, Thoroughly practicing by means of the power of wisdom, skillful means, and miracles, As long as their roots of virtue are not perfected, For that long they do not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितां चरन्तो प्रज्ञा उपाय बल ऋद्धि विचारमाणो । तावन् न तां परमशून्यत प्रापुणोति यावन् न ते कुशलमूल भवन्ति पूर्णाः ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, having given a gift to living beings, Does not regard it as their own and has no attachment to the object, From that, the roots of virtue will grow to have great power, Like the bright orb of the waxing moon in a cloudless sky.
examples.gm: If the bodhisattva, having given gifts to beings, Does not make them "mine" and is unsparing of entities, Their roots of virtue will increase with great power, Like the radiant, cloudless moon disk in the waxing fortnight.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व ददमान जगस्य दानं ममतां न तत्र करयेन् न च वस्तुप्रेम । ततु वर्धते कुशलमूल महानुभावो चन्द्रो व तत्र प्रभमण्डलु शुक्लपक्षे ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Acting through wisdom, skillful means, strength, and miraculous powers, As long as their roots of virtue are not yet complete, So long will they not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, Thoroughly practicing by means of the power of wisdom, skillful means, and miracles, As long as their roots of virtue are not perfected, For that long they do not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितां चरन्तो प्रज्ञा उपाय बल ऋद्धि विचारमाणो । तावन् न तां परमशून्यत प्रापुणोति यावन् न ते कुशलमूल भवन्ति पूर्णाः ॥

examples.dm: So too, the bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, Having attained the meditative concentrations, faculties, and powers, Does not take delight in merely touching nirvana alone, And does not leave the suffering of sentient beings behind.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, And attained the powers of the faculties of concentration, Does not merely delight in touching nirvāṇa, And leave sentient beings in suffering.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यत व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं लब्ध्वान ध्यान बल इन्द्रिय बोधिसत्त्वो । किंचापि निर्वृति स्पृशेदभिनन्दमानो अपि सर्वसत्त्व दुखिता मनसी भवन्ति ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as those who desire jewels go to a jewel island, And having found jewels, return home again, They do not live in happiness there as solitary captains, While leaving their circle of kinsmen and friends in misery.
examples.gm: For example, a person desiring jewels, having gone to a jewel island, And having found jewels, returns home again; Just as that merchant does not merely live happily by himself there, And leave his host of relatives and friends unhappy.
examples.sa: रतनार्थिको यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं लब्ध्वान रत्न पुन गेहम् उपागमेय्या । किंचापि तत्र सुख जीवति सार्थवाहो अपि दुःखितो मनसि भोति स जातिसंघो ॥

examples.dm: For example, in order to gain knowledge of the route, a merchant seeking profit Travels to whatever cities, towns, or villages lie along the way; He does not remain there, nor does he remain even on the Island of Jewels, And without staying at home, he becomes an expert on the path.
examples.gm: For example, an ambitious merchant, in order to know the routes, Goes to whatever intermediate cities, towns, and villages there are. He does not dwell there, nor does he dwell on the jewel island; The wise one does not dwell at home, but becomes skilled in the path.
examples.sa: अभ्यन्तरे य नगरे निगमे च ग्रामे कामार्थ वाणिजु यथा गमि जाननाय । नो चापि तत्र स्थिहती न च रत्नद्वीपे न च गेह मार्गि कुशलो पुन भोति विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all the knowledge and liberations Of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; He does not abide in those, nor does he abide in the primordial wisdom of a Buddha; He does not abide in the unconditioned; he is one who knows the nature of the path.
examples.gm: Likewise, a brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all The knowledges and liberations of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; They do not dwell in them, nor do they dwell in the Buddha's pristine wisdom; They do not dwell in the unconditioned, but know the nature of the path.
examples.sa: तथ ज्ञान श्रावकविमुक्तिसप्रत्ययानां सर्वत्र भोति कुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । नो चापि तत्र स्थिहते न च बुद्धज्ञाने न च संस्कृते भवति मार्गविदू विधिज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Those who wish to attain the supreme qualities of all beings, To touch the most marvelous and supreme primordial wisdom of the Buddha, And to bestow the most excellent and holy gift of Dharma, Should rely upon this supreme state of the benefactors.
examples.gm: To go to the supreme qualities of all sentient beings, And to touch the supremely marvelous, supreme Buddha-wisdom, Whosoever desires to give the supreme, holy gift of Dharma, Rely on this supreme dwelling of those who bring benefit!
examples.sa: यो सर्वसत्त्वगुण-अग्रतु गन्तुकामो अग्रं स्पृशेय परमाद्भुत बुद्धज्ञानम् । अग्रं ददेय वर उत्तमधर्मदानम् इमु अग्रु सेवतु विहारु हितंकराणाम् ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the peak of complete realization
examples.gm: Teaching on the Culminating Clear Realization

examples.dm: The fifth chapter explains the clear realization of the pinnacle. One who does not desire the level of an Arhat, the wisdom of a Pratyekabuddha, Or the three realms, even in a dream, But sees the Buddhas and teaches the Dharma to beings— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: Chapter Five: Teaching the Clear Realization of the Peak. The stage of an arhat and the pristine wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, And the three realms, they do not desire even in dreams; Seeing the buddhas and teaching the dharma to wanderers, They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: अर्हन्तभूमिम् अपि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ त्रैधातुकं न स्पृशते सुपिनान्तरेऽपि । बुद्धांश् च पश्यति कथेति जनस्य धर्मं अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, having attained the fourfold tranquility Of concentration and meditative absorption that bestows joy and bliss, Relinquishes that blissful concentration and the meditative absorptions they have attained, And out of compassion for beings, enters again into the realm of desire.
examples.gm: Similarly, the wise bodhisattva, joy and Having attained the happiness-bestowing four peaceful samādhis of the dhyānas, Lets go of the attainment of the dhyāna samādhis endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, And endowed with compassion for beings, again enters the desire realm.
examples.sa: एमेव ध्यान चतुर् एव समाधि शान्तां लब्ध्वान प्रीति सुखदां विदु बोधिसत्त्वाः । अवसृज्य ध्यानसुखप्रीतिसमाधिलाभं पुन कामधातु प्रविशन्ति जगानुकम्पी ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, those who seek supreme enlightenment, Being wise and possessing intense resolve, should utterly conquer pride; Just as a multitude of the sick rely on a physician for healing, One should rely on a spiritual friend without any distraction.
examples.gm: Therefore, one who seeks holy awakening, A wise one possessing strong intention, having definitely destroyed pride, Just as a multitude of sick people rely on a doctor to be cured, Should rely on spiritual friends without wavering.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु मानु निहनित्वन पण्डितेन गुरुआशयेन वरबोधि गवेषमाणः । वैद्यो व आतुर स्वरोगचिकित्सनार्थं कल्याणमित्र भजितव्य अतन्द्रितेन ॥

examples.dm: Even if they frequent secluded villages, cities, mountain caves, And rely upon remote hermitages and forest retreats, A bodhisattva who praises themselves and disparages others Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
examples.gm: Very solitary villages, cities, and mountain valleys, And isolated monasteries and forests, they thoroughly rely upon; But a bodhisattva who praises themselves and deprecates others, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
examples.sa: प्रविविक्त ग्रामनगरे गिरिकन्दराणि रण्या विविक्त वनप्रस्थ निषेवमाणो । आत्मानुकर्षि पर पंसयि बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्यु मारु पर्युत्थितु अल्पबुद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: Whether one dwells in a town or in a forest, If one is free from the mind of the two vehicles and is certain of supreme enlightenment, This is the solitude of those who have entered into the service of beings; Any bodhisattva who feels superior to them has degraded themselves.
examples.gm: Whether abiding in a village or else in an isolated monastery, If free from the minds of the two vehicles and certain of supreme awakening, This is the solitude of those engaged in the benefit of beings; That conceited bodhisattva ruins themselves.
examples.sa: ग्रामान्ति यो विहरते अथवा अरण्ये द्वययानचित्तविगतो नियतोऽग्रबोधिम् । एषो विवेकु जगदर्थभिप्रस्थितानां आत्मा क्षिणोति तुलयेय स बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: A bodhisattva who strives for the benefit of beings and has attained meditative concentration, Powers, faculties, liberations, and absorptions—if one treats them with contempt, Thinking, "This person does not practice in forest isolation," The Victor has declared that such a person dwells within the domain of Māra.
examples.gm: When a bodhisattva striving for the benefit of beings attains dhyāna, Powers, faculties, liberations, and samādhi, If one despises them, thinking, "This is not the conduct of isolated monasteries," The Victorious One says they abide in the domain of Māra.
examples.sa: सो चंक्रमार्थम् अभियुक्तकबोधिसत्त्वान् बलध्यान-इन्द्रियविमोक्षसमाधिप्राप्तान् । अभिमन्यते न इमि रण्यविवेकचारी न विवेकगोचरु अयं हि जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Apart from the liberation of the Tathāgatas and the Arhats, This state is the dwelling of the Hearers and the Pratyekabuddhas; It is a dwelling in the meditative concentration of peace, endowed with sublime tranquility and bliss, The most supreme and unsurpassed of all such states.
examples.gm: Except for the liberations of Arhats and Tathāgatas, This dwelling, among those of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, This dwelling in peaceful samādhi, supremely peaceful and endowed with bliss, Is the supreme and unsurpassed of all however many there are.
examples.sa: यावन्त श्रावकविहार सप्रत्ययानां शान्ता समाधिप्रशमे सुखसंप्रयुक्ता । अर्हन्विमोक्ष स्थपयित्व तथागतानां सर्वेषु अग्र अयु विहारु निरुत्तरश् च ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like being stricken by poison through the mere perception of suspicion; Even if that poison has not entered the body, one will fall unconscious. Likewise, the childish who claim "I" and "mine," Have the notion of a self, and through unreal conceptualization, are born and die in impermanence.
examples.gm: For example, just as poison aroused by the perception of suspicion, Even if that poison has not gone inside, one will faint; Likewise, childish beings, accepting self and what belongs to self, Perceiving that self, which is not real, constantly are born and die.
examples.sa: यथ शङ्कितेन विषसंज्ञत अभ्युपैति नो चास्य कोष्ठगतु सो विषु पात्यते च । एमेव बालुपगतो अहु मह्य एषो अहसंज्ञि जायि म्रियते च सदा अभूतो ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are throughout Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them were to generate the mind of supreme enlightenment, And were to practice generosity for many tens of millions of millennia, And were to dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the sake of all beings,
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are in Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them, having generated the mind toward supreme awakening, Were to give gifts for many tens of millions of thousands of years, And dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the benefit of beings;
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व निखिले इह जम्बुद्विपे ते सर्वि बोधिवरचित्त उपादयित्वा । दानं ददित्व बहुवर्षसहस्रकोटीः सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधौ ॥

examples.dm: From the first generation of the mind set upon supreme enlightenment, Until the attainment of unsurpassed awakening, If one maintains this mental focus for even a single day and night, The wise and clear-minded should be known as having initiated diligence.
examples.gm: From the first generation of the mind for supreme awakening, Up until unsurpassable awakening is attained, If they consider it in their mind as just a single day and night, The radiant wise one should be known as having commenced diligence.
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो सो वा अनुत्तरशिवाम् अनुप्रापुणेया । रात्रिंदिवैकमनसा तम् अधिष्ठिहेया आरम्भवीर्य विदु पण्डितु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: If someone were to diligently apply themselves to the supreme perfection of wisdom, And practice in accordance with it for even a single day, The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this. Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without distraction.
examples.gm: Whoever visibly strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom, If they conform to it for even a single day, That aggregate of generosity cannot match a fraction of their merit; Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without wavering.
examples.sa: यश् चैव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताभियुक्तो दिवसं पि अन्तमश एकनुवर्तयेया । कलपुण्य सो न भवती इह दानस्कन्धो तदतन्द्रितेन सद ओसरितव्य प्रज्ञा ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Though they generate great compassion, have no perception of sentient beings. At that time, those wise ones become the objects of offering for all the world; They always make meaningful use of the alms of the country.
examples.gm: The yogi practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even when generating great compassion, has no perception of sentient beings; At that time, the wise one becomes a field of generosity for all beings, And always meaningfully fully enjoys the alms of the realm.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा । तद भोन्ति सर्वजगती विदु दक्षिणीया सततं अमोघु परिभुञ्जति राष्ट्रपिण्डम् ॥

examples.dm: When training, one does not make any claims about the training; One does not perceive a trainee or the qualities to be trained in, And does not conceptualize between training and non-training— Whoever trains in this way trains here in these Buddha-qualities.
examples.gm: When training, whoever does not assert any training, And does not observe the trainer or the dharmas of training, And does not conceptualize these two: having trained and not having trained, Whoever trains like that, trains in this Dharma of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: यो शिक्षमाणु न उपैति कहिंचि शिक्षां न च शिक्षकं लभति नापि च शिक्षधर्मान् । शिक्षा अशिक्ष उभयो अविकल्पमानो यो शिक्षते स इह शिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: When the Guides fully describe the trainings, This training is the supreme and unsurpassed among all trainings. Any wise person who wishes to reach the far shore of all trainings Should train in this Buddha-training, the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: When the Guides fully proclaim this training, It is the supreme and unsurpassed of all trainings however many there are. Whichever wise one desires to go to the other shore of all trainings, Train in this perfection of wisdom, the training of the Buddhas!
examples.sa: यावन्ति शिक्ष परिदीपित नायकेन सर्वेष शिक्ष अयु अग्रु निरुत्तरा च । यः सर्वशिक्षविदु इच्छति पार गन्तुम् इमु प्रज्ञपारमित शिक्षति बुद्धशिक्षाम् ॥

examples.dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
examples.gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.
examples.sa: अविवर्तियस्य वरबोधयि प्रस्थितस्य यो चित्तुपादु अनुमोदितु आशयेन । त्रिसहस्र मेरु तुलयित्व सियाप्रमाणो न त्वेव तस्य कुशलस्यनुमोदनाये ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who possesses the excellent quality of patience— Suppose someone were to fill the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offer them to the Knower of the World, To the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas; The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva is endowed with the excellent dharma of patience, Compared to someone who fills the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offers them to the Knowers of the World, The Buddhas, arhats, and solitary realizers, That mass of generosity cannot match a fraction of the merit of the former.
examples.sa: सो बोधिसत्त्व क्षमते गुणधर्मयुक्तो यश् चैव रत्नभरितं त्रिसहस्र दद्यात् । बुद्धान लोकविदुनार्हतप्रत्ययानां कलपुण्य सो न भवते इह दानस्कन्धे ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are—the lesser, the middling, and the superior— The Sugata taught that they all arise from ignorance. When conditions assemble, the machine of suffering fully emerges; That machine of ignorance neither exhausts nor increases.
examples.gm: However many inferior, middling, and supreme sentient beings there are, The Sugatas have taught that they all arise from ignorance; When conditions come together, the machine of suffering perfectly arises, Yet that machine of ignorance has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व मृदुमध्यमुत्कृष्ट लोके सर्वे अविद्यप्रभवा सुगतेन उक्ताः । सामग्रिप्रत्ययु प्रवर्तति दुःखयन्त्रो न च यन्त्र क्षीयति अविद्य न चापि वृद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who, regarding dependent origination, Understands this wisdom to be without birth and without exhaustion, Just as the cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating its beams of light, Will, by destroying the dense gloom of ignorance, attain the self-arisen state.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva, with regard to dependent origination, Knows this wisdom as unborn and unexhausted, Just as the cloudless sun dispels darkness by emitting rays of light, Having destroyed dense ignorance, will attain the state of the Self-Arisen.
examples.sa: यो तु प्रतीत्यसमुत्पादु अनुद्भवाये इमु प्रज्ञ अक्षयत बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । सो सूर्य अभ्रपटले यथ मुक्तरश्मी विधमित्वविद्यपटलं भवते स्वयंभूः ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are—the lesser, the middling, and the superior— The Sugata taught that they all arise from ignorance. When conditions assemble, the machine of suffering fully emerges; That machine of ignorance neither exhausts nor increases.
examples.gm: However many inferior, middling, and supreme sentient beings there are, The Sugatas have taught that they all arise from ignorance; When conditions come together, the machine of suffering perfectly arises, Yet that machine of ignorance has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व मृदुमध्यमुत्कृष्ट लोके सर्वे अविद्यप्रभवा सुगतेन उक्ताः । सामग्रिप्रत्ययु प्रवर्तति दुःखयन्त्रो न च यन्त्र क्षीयति अविद्य न चापि वृद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are—the lesser, the middling, and the superior— The Sugata taught that they all arise from ignorance. When conditions assemble, the machine of suffering fully emerges; That machine of ignorance neither exhausts nor increases.
examples.gm: However many inferior, middling, and supreme sentient beings there are, The Sugatas have taught that they all arise from ignorance; When conditions come together, the machine of suffering perfectly arises, Yet that machine of ignorance has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व मृदुमध्यमुत्कृष्ट लोके सर्वे अविद्यप्रभवा सुगतेन उक्ताः । सामग्रिप्रत्ययु प्रवर्तति दुःखयन्त्रो न च यन्त्र क्षीयति अविद्य न चापि वृद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: This is a marvelous and wondrous accumulation of qualities: Abiding in meditative concentration and stabilization, they are without signs. If those who abide therein should have their bodies perish, They will be reborn in the desire realm exactly according to their intentions.
examples.gm: This is the marvelous wonder of accumulating qualities: Having abided in the samādhis of the dhyānas, they have no signs; If the bodies of those who abide in them were to fall apart, They are again born in the desire realm according to their intention.
examples.sa: आश्चर्यम् अद्भुतम् इदं गुणसंचयानां ध्याने समाधि विहरन्ति निमित्त नास्ति । तत्र स्थितान यदि भज्यति आत्मभावो पुन कामधातु उपपद्यति यथाभिप्राया ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the bodhisattvas who possess supreme qualities, Diligent in yoga and abiding in meditative concentration and absorption, Dwell once again in the desire realm without attachment; Like a lotus in the water, they are not stained by the qualities of the foolish.
examples.gm: Similarly, those who hold the supreme qualities of a bodhisattva, Exerting themselves in yoga and abiding in the samādhis of the dhyānas, Again abide in the desire realm without attachment; Like a lotus in water, they do not abide in the dharmas of fools.
examples.sa: एमेव ते गुणधरा वरबोधिसत्त्वा ध्याने समाधि विहरित्व प्रयुक्तयोगी । पुन कामधातुस्थित भोन्ति अनोपलिप्ता पद्मेव वारिणि अनिश्रित बालधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: If, with the thought, "I shall bring all beings to maturity and act for their benefit," One applies oneself with body, speech, and mind, Yet remains dwelling in the perception of a self, one has become lazy; They are as far from omniscience as the earth is from the sky.
examples.gm: Thinking, "Having completely ripened beings, I will act for their benefit," If they exert themselves with body, speech, and mind, Because they abide in the perception of a self, they have become lazy, And they become as far from omniscience as the sky is from the earth.
examples.sa: सचि कायचित्तवचसा च पराक्रमेय्या परिपाचयित्व जगती करिष्यामि अर्थम् । कौसीद्यप्राप्त भवती स्थितु आत्मसंज्ञैः नैरात्मभावनविदूरि नभं व भूमेः ॥

examples.dm: Those who grasp at the actual perception of a self and hold things as "mine" are attached; How could fools like these ever have the intention to give? Those who are stingy will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Even if they are born as humans, they will be destitute at that time.
examples.gm: Perceiving a self, one is attached to things through grasping them as "mine"; How could fools have the mind of generosity? Miserly ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Or even if they are born as humans, they will then be impoverished.
examples.sa: अहसंज्ञतस्तु ममता भवते च रागो कुतु त्यागबुद्धि भविष्यति सा मुहानाम् । मात्सर्य प्रेत भवते उपपद्ययाती अथवा मनुष्य तद भोति दरिद्ररूपो ॥

examples.dm: If they should hear others speaking ill or using harsh words, The wise bodhisattva rejoices, thinking, "This is my happiness." Who speaks, who hears, who [speaks] to whom, and for what reason? One who possesses this supreme perfection of patience is wise.
examples.gm: If one hears abusive and harsh words from others, Thinking, "I am happy," the wise bodhisattva rejoices; Who speaks, who hears, by what, what is it, and for what reason? The wise one is endowed with the supreme perfection of patience.
examples.sa: परुषं श्रुणित्व वचनं परतो दुरुक्तं परितोषयाति सुसुखं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । को भाषते क शृणुते कुतु कस्य केन सो युक्त क्षान्तिवरपारमिताय विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Whips, sticks, weapons, being killed, bound, or beaten, Decapitation, and the cutting off of ears, feet, hands, and nose— Thinking, "I shall endure whatever worldly sufferings there may be," The bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.gm: "Whips, sticks, weapons, killing, binding, and beating, Severing of the head, and cutting off ears, hands, feet, and nose— Whatever sufferings exist in the world, I will endure them!" Thinking this, the bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.sa: कशदण्डशस्त्रवधबन्धनताडनाश्च शिरछेदकर्णचरणाकरनासछेदाः । यावन्ति दुःख जगती अहु तत्सहामि क्षान्तीय पारमित तिष्ठति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: When the wise bodhisattva has practiced such patience, And dedicates that generation of the mind toward supreme enlightenment, That hero, through patience, surpasses all the world’s Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, and however many diverse realms of sentient beings there are.
examples.gm: Having practiced patience in that way, the wise bodhisattva, If they completely dedicate that generation of the mind to supreme awakening, The hero, through patience towards the entire world, outshines All arhats, solitary realizers, and the many realms of sentient beings.
examples.sa: एवं क्षमित्व विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो तं चित्तुपादु परिणामयि अग्रबोधौ । यावन्ति क्षान्ति रहप्रत्ययसत्त्वधातोः अभिभोति सर्वजगती क्षममाणु शूरः ॥

examples.dm: If, for ten million eons, one practices the ten paths of virtuous action, Yet generates a desire for the state of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, At that moment, one’s ethical discipline is flawed and has degenerated; That generation of such a thought is far weightier than even a formal defeat.
examples.gm: Even if one practices the ten paths of virtuous action for ten million aeons, If one generates the desire for the state of an arhat or solitary realizer, At that time, one's discipline becomes flawed and one's discipline degenerates; Generating that mind is much heavier even than a defeat.
examples.sa: यदि कल्पकोटि दशभी कुशलैः पथेभिश् चरमाणु प्रत्ययरहत्वस्पृहां जनेति । तद खण्डशीलु भवते अपि छिद्रशीलो पाराजिको गुरुतरो अयु चित्तुपादो ॥

examples.dm: Through ethical discipline, those who desire peace become noble. Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their ethical discipline never declines. They follow all the various activities of the vows; For the benefit of all beings, they also dedicate them to enlightenment.
examples.gm: Through discipline, those who desire peace become exalted; Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their discipline does not wane. They engage in all the activities of vows, whatever they may be, And dedicate them to awakening for the benefit of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: शीलेन उद्गत भवन्ति समाधिकाङ्क्षी स्थित गोचरे दशबलान अखण्डशीलाः । यावन्ति संवरक्रिय अनुवर्तयन्ति तां सर्वसत्त्वहित बोधयि नामयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: If one wishes to attain the awakening of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, One is immoral, unskilled, and one’s conduct has degenerated. But if one fully dedicates toward supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: If one desires to touch the awakening of an arhat or solitary realizer, One's discipline is broken, one is unwise, and thus one's conduct degenerates. But if one completely dedicates it to the supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: सचि प्रत्ययानरहबोधि स्पृहां जनेति दुःशील भोति विदुषां तथ छिद्रचारी । अथ बोधि उत्तमशिवां परिणामयन्ति स्थितु शीलपारमित कामगुणेभि युक्तो ॥

examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
