examples.dm: The eighth chapter: teaching the Dharmakāya. One fully embraces the pure realm and the purity of sentient beings; One fully embraces the lineage of the Buddha and the lineage of the Dharma; Likewise, one fully embraces the lineage of the Saṅgha and all phenomena.
examples.gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching the Dharmakāya. Fully upholds perfectly pure fields and pure sentient beings; Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage; Likewise fully upholds the Sangha lineage and all dharmas.

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victors thinks, "These sentient beings are ethical, but those are unethical," Engaging in such diverse perceptions, they are utterly lacking in ethical discipline; Their morality has degenerated, and they lack completely purified morality.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victorious Ones Thinks, "These sentient beings have discipline; these have broken discipline," By engaging in such diverse perceptions, their discipline is completely broken; Their discipline degenerates, and they lack completely pure discipline.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान मार्गे इमि शीलवानिमि दुशील करोति सत्त्वान् । नानात्वसंज्ञप्रसृतो परमं दुशीलो अपि छिद्रशीलु न तु सो परिशुद्धशीलो ॥

examples.dm: Any pure being who possesses such morality as this, Is without bias toward anything pleasant or unpleasant. They give away their heads, hands, and feet without a trace of discouragement; They give away all their possessions, remaining forever free from attachment.
examples.gm: Any pure sentient being who thus possesses discipline Has no view of anything as pleasant or unpleasant. Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they have no shrinking mind; Giving away all their possessions, they are always free from clinging.
examples.sa: यो एवशीलसमन्वागतु निष्प्रपञ्चो अनपेक्षको भवति सर्वप्रियाप्रियेषु । शिरहस्तपाद त्यजमान अदीनचित्तो सर्वास्तित्यागि भवते सततं अलीनो ॥

examples.dm: Any pure being who possesses such morality as this, Is without bias toward anything pleasant or unpleasant. They give away their heads, hands, and feet without a trace of discouragement; They give away all their possessions, remaining forever free from attachment.
examples.gm: Any pure sentient being who thus possesses discipline Has no view of anything as pleasant or unpleasant. Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they have no shrinking mind; Giving away all their possessions, they are always free from clinging.

examples.dm: Through ethical discipline, one abandons the various states of animal existence, And by abandoning the eight unfree states, one always finds leisure. Through patience, one will attain a sublime, vast, and beautiful form; With a lovely golden complexion, one becomes worthy of being beheld by all beings.
examples.gm: By discipline, the nature of the manifold destinies of animals and The eight unfree states are abandoned, and leisure is always found. By patience, a fine, supreme, and vast form will be obtained, Golden-colored, beautiful, and worthy to be looked at by beings.
examples.sa: शीलेन तीर्यगति वर्जयि नेकरुपाम् अष्टौ च अक्षण क्षणां लभते स नित्यम् । क्षान्तीय रुप लभते परमं उदारं सुवर्णच्छवि प्रियु जगस्य उदीक्षणीयो ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the gradual path
examples.gm: Teaching on the Gradual Approach

examples.dm: The sixth chapter explains the gradual path. Through the generosity of a bodhisattva, the path to the realm of hungry spirits is cut off; It likewise eliminates poverty and all afflictions. When practiced, one will obtain an infinite expansion of resources; Through generosity, one brings sentient beings who are suffering to full maturity.
examples.gm: Chapter Six: Teaching the Gradual Training. By the bodhisattva's giving, the destiny of hungry ghosts is cut off; Poverty and likewise all afflictions are cut off; While practicing, they will obtain infinite, abundant wealth, And by giving, they fully ripen sentient beings who are suffering.
examples.sa: दानेन प्रेतगति छिन्दति बोधिसत्त्वो दारिद्रकं च छिनती तथ सर्वक्लेशान् । भोगांश् चनन्तविपुलां लभते चरन्तो दानेन सत्त्व परिपाचयि कृच्छ्रप्राप्तान् ॥

examples.gm: Teaching on the Complete Awakening in a Single Moment

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: The first chapter teaches omniscience of all aspects. Whatever rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and forests, All depend upon the Naga King, the Lord of Nagas, who dwells in Anavatapta; They are the power and glory of that Lord of Nagas.
examples.gm: Chapter One: The Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects. However many rivers flow in this Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests, All depend upon the nāga king, the lord of nāgas, dwelling in Anavatapta; It is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
examples.sa: यावन्ति नद्य प्रवहन्ति ह जम्बुद्वीपे फल पुष्प औषधाधि वनस्पति रोहयन्ति । भूजत गजेन्द्रनागपतिनिश्रयनोवतनस्य तस्यानुभावश्रिय साभु जगाधिपस्य ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Dharma the Victor’s Śrāvakas may teach, Explain, or express through logical reasoning, And whatever attainment of supreme, noble bliss and its fruits they achieve, All of these are the power of the Tathāgata, the Great Being.
examples.gm: However much the śrāvakas of the Jina teach the Dharma, Explaining and expressing it logically, Creating supreme noble bliss and attaining its results, All of that is the power of the person of the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: यावन्ति धर्म जिनश्रावक देशयन्ति भाषन्ति युक्तिसहितांश् च उदीरयन्ति । परमार्थसौख्यक्रिय तत्फलप्राप्तिता च सर्वो अयं पुरुषकारु तथागतस्य ॥

examples.dm: Just as a wandering mendicant, through his knowledge of craftsmanship, Brings about the disintegration of the aggregates without any objective apprehension, Any bodhisattva who understands phenomena in that way, Does not touch nirvana, and is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as the wanderer Śreṇika, through his knowledge, Understood the aggregates as unapprehendable and subject to destruction; Whatever bodhisattva understands phenomena in that way Does not contact nirvāṇa, and dwells in wisdom.
examples.sa: अथ श्रेणिकस्य अभुती परिव्राजकस्य ज्ञानोपलम्भु न हि स्कन्धविभावना च । यो बोधिसत्त्व परिजानति एव धर्मां न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who abides here in peace in this way, Has been prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceit of thinking, "I am in meditative equipoise," or "I have arisen," Why is that? Because the nature of phenomena is fully understood.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva dwells here thus in peace, Is prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceited thought, "I am in meditative equipoise" or "I have arisen." Why is this? Because they completely understand the nature of phenomena.
examples.sa: एवात्मशान्ति विहरन्निह बोधिसत्त्वो सो व्याकृतो पुरमकेहि तथागतेहि । न च मन्यते अहु समाधितु व्युत्थितो वा कस्मार्थ धर्मप्रकृतिं परिजानयित्वा ॥

examples.dm: One who knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not treat the illusion as one thing and the aggregates as another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in total peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever here knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not make illusion one thing and the aggregates another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in perfect peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: मायोपमां य इह जानति पञ्च स्कन्धां न च माय अन्य न च स्कन्ध करोति अन्यान् । नानात्वसंज्ञविगतो उपशान्तचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: One who knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not treat the illusion as one thing and the aggregates as another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in total peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever here knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not make illusion one thing and the aggregates another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in perfect peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.

examples.dm: Those who possess spiritual friends and possess special insight, Will never become afraid upon hearing the Mother of the Victors. Those who associate with negative friends and rely on others, Are like an unfired clay vessel that disintegrates when touched by water.
examples.gm: Possessing spiritual friends and possessing profound insight, Hearing the Mother of the Jinas, they will not be afraid. Whoever possesses bad friends and depends upon others, Is like an unfired clay vessel that collapses when it contacts water.
examples.sa: कल्याणमित्रसहितस्य विपश्यकस्य त्रासो न भेष्यति श्रुणित्व जिनान मात्राम् । यो पापमित्रसहितो च परप्रणेयो सो आमभाजन यथोदकस्पृष्ट भिन्नो ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this person called a 'bodhisattva'?" They seek the total exhaustion of all attachment, cutting through attachment. They touch the unattached awakening of the Victors; Therefore, they receive the name "bodhisattva."
examples.gm: Why are they called a "bodhisattva"? They sever attachment, desiring the exhaustion of attachment to all things. They contact the unattached awakening of the Jinas; Therefore, they obtain the name of "bodhisattva."
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वत्र सङ्गक्रिय इच्छति सङ्गछेदी । बोधिं स्पृशिष्यति जिनान असङ्गभूतां तस्माद्धि नाम लभते अयु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this one called a 'great being' (mahāsattva)?" Because they have become the foremost among the vast assembly of sentient beings, And because they sever the great thicket of views within the realm of sentient beings; For that reason, they are truly called a "great being."
examples.gm: Why are they called a "great being"? Because they become the supreme among great multitudes of sentient beings, and sever the great views of the realms of sentient beings; Therefore, they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महसत्त्व सोऽथ केनोच्यति कारणेन महताय अत्र अयु भेष्यति सत्त्वराशेः । दृष्टीगतां महति छिन्दति सत्त्वधातोः महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: Possessing great generosity, great intelligence, and great power, They have entered the supreme Great Vehicle of the Victors; Clad in great armor, they subdue the illusions of Māra; For that reason, they are truly called "great beings."
examples.gm: Great giving, great intelligence, and great power, Entering into the supreme Great Vehicle of the Jinas, Donning the great armor and subduing the illusions of Mara; Therefore they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महनायको महतबुद्धि महानुभावो महयान उत्तमजिनान समाधिरूढो । महता सनद्धु नमुचिं शठ धर्षयिष्ये महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: Form, perception, feeling, intention, And consciousness are neither bound nor freed, and they do not exist. Thus, entering into awakening without a discouraged mind, This is the supreme armor of holy beings.
examples.gm: Form and perception, feeling and volition, And consciousness are not bound, not liberated, and do not exist. Entering into awakening in this way, without a discouraged mind, This is the supreme armor of the noble persons.
examples.sa: रुपं च संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान बन्धु न च मुक्त असङ्गभूतो । एवं च बोधि क्रमते न च लीनचित्तो संना ह एष वरपुद्गल-उत्तमानाम् ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening?" It is because by mounting it, one delivers all sentient beings from suffering. This vehicle is a vast celestial palace, as immense as space; It is the supreme vehicle, the means for fully attaining joy, delight, and bliss.
examples.gm: Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Mounting it, all sentient beings pass beyond sorrow. This vehicle is a great immeasurable palace like space, The supreme vehicle, which brings about the attainment of joy, happiness, and bliss.
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधियानो यत्रारुहित्व स निर्वापयि सर्वसत्त्वान् । आकाशतुल्य अयु यान महाविमानो सुखसौख्यक्षेमभिप्रापणु यानश्रेष्ठो ॥

examples.dm: The bodhisattva does not apprehend a prior limit, a later limit, Or a present; they are the purity of the three times. That which is such is unconditioned and free from conceptual elaboration; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas do not apprehend the past limit, the future limit, And the present occurrence; the three times are pure. They are unconditioned and free from conceptual proliferation; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: पूर्वान्ततो न उपलभ्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अपरान्ततोऽपि प्रतिउपन्न त्रियध्वशुद्धो । यो शुद्ध सो अनभिसंस्कृतु निष्प्रपञ्चो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.gm: Bodhisattvas do not apprehend the past limit, the future limit, And the present occurrence; the three times are pure. They are unconditioned and free from conceptual proliferation; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: पूर्वान्ततो न उपलभ्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अपरान्ततोऽपि प्रतिउपन्न त्रियध्वशुद्धो । यो शुद्ध सो अनभिसंस्कृतु निष्प्रपञ्चो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Know that all sentient beings are exactly as oneself is; Know that all phenomena are exactly as all sentient beings are; Not conceptualizing either non-arising or arising— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Knowing all sentient beings to be like oneself, Knowing all dharmas to be like all sentient beings, Not conceptualizing both non-arising and arising, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ आत्मनं तथ प्रजानति सर्वसत्त्वां यथ सर्वसत्त्व तथ प्रजानति सर्वधर्मान् । अनुपादुपादु उभये अविकल्पमानो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who practices in that way without doubt, Should be known as one endowed with wisdom, abiding in equanimity; Having fully understood that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who practices in this way without doubt, Endowed with wisdom, should be known to abide in equality; Thoroughly knowing dharmas to be without nature, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु न च काङ्क्षति बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्य यो विहर ते स उपायप्रज्ञो । प्रकृतीअसन्त परिजानयमान धर्मां एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who practices in this way without doubt, Endowed with wisdom, should be known to abide in equality; Thoroughly knowing dharmas to be without nature, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Those who think, "May I become a disciple of the Sugata," And those who desire to become Pratyekabuddhas or likewise Kings of Dharma, Cannot achieve these without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot cross from this shore to the other without seeing the ferry.
examples.gm: Whoever thinks they will become a śrāvaka of the Sugata, Or a pratyekabuddha, and likewise wishes to become a Dharma King, Cannot attain it without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot see a crossing to go from this shore to the other.
examples.sa: यो इच्छती सुगतश्रावक हं भवेयं प्रत्येकबुद्ध भवियां तथ धर्मराजो । इमु क्षान्त्यनागमि न शक्यति प्रापुणेतुं यथ आरपारगमनाय अतीतदर्शी ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: These four types of persons are not afraid of that: The Child of the Victors skilled in the truths, the irreversible one, The Arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, the one who is fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
examples.gm: These four kinds of persons are not terrified by this: The children of the Victorious One who are wise in the truth, those who are irreversible, Arhats who have cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, those perfectly embraced by spiritual friends.
examples.sa: चत्वारि पुद्गल इमे न त्रसन्ति येऽस्मिन् जिनपुत्र सत्यकुशलो अविवर्तियश्च । अर्हं विधूतमलक्लेश प्रहीणकाङ्क्षो कल्याणमित्रपरिपाचित यश्चतुर्थः ॥

examples.dm: The wise and learned Bodhisattva who practices in this way, Does not train in the stage of an Arhat, nor in the stage of a Pratyekabuddha; For the sake of omniscience, they train following the Buddha-dharma. One who does not train in the distinction between training and non-training is one who trains.
examples.gm: A wise, understanding bodhisattva who practices in this way Does not train for the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha; For the sake of omniscience itself, they train in the qualities of a buddha; Whoever does not train in training and no-more-training, that is training.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो नार्हंमि शिक्षति न प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ । सर्वज्ञताय अनुशिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे शिक्षाअशिक्ष न य शिक्षति एष शिक्षा ॥

examples.dm: It is not for the sake of the increase, decrease, or grasping of form; Nor is it for the sake of grasping the various phenomena that one trains. While training, one also grasps omniscience itself; This very transcendence is the training of those who delight in excellence.
examples.gm: It is not for the sake of the increase, complete deterioration, or complete apprehension of form; Not training for the sake of completely apprehending various dharmas, Yet training and completely apprehending omniscience itself— Whatever definite emergence this is, this is the training that rejoices in qualities.
examples.sa: न च रुपवृद्धिपरिहाणिपरिग्रहाये न च शिक्षति विविधधर्मपरिग्रहाये । सर्वज्ञतां च परिगृह्णति शिक्षमाणो निर्यायती य इय शिक्ष गुणे रतानाम् ॥

examples.dm: The Guide has proclaimed that perception is the near shore; By dismantling and abandoning perception, one goes to the far shore. Those who are free from perception have attained this subsequent state; Having crossed over, they abide by the Teacher’s command.
examples.gm: The Guide has proclaimed that perception is this shore; Destroying and abandoning perception, one goes to the other shore; Those who are free from perception, attaining this, Have reached the other shore and abide in the Teacher's word.
examples.sa: संज्ञेति नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन संज्ञां विभाविय प्रहाण व्रजन्ति पारम् । ये अत्र संज्ञविगमं अनुप्राप्नुवन्ति ते पारप्राप्त स्थित पारमिते हु भोन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many eons As there are grains of sand in the Ganges and proclaim the word "sentient being," Since they are pure from the beginning, how could a sentient being ever be born? This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many Aeons as there are grains of sand, and proclaim the word "sentient being," Since they are pure from the very beginning, how could a sentient being arise? This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि गङ्गवालुकसमानि स्थिहित्व कल्पां सत्त्वेति शब्द परिकीर्तयि नायकोऽयम् । सत्त्वस्य्’ उपादु कुतु भेष्यति आदिशुद्धो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: When I spoke in accordance with this supreme perfection, At that time, the Supreme Being of the past prophesied, Saying, "In a future time, you will become a Buddha," Thus the Conqueror spoke, saying that I had been prophesied.
examples.gm: When I, with this supreme perfection of wisdom, Spoke in conformity, at that time the supreme being of the past, Saying, "In a future time you will become a buddha"— "I was prophesied," thus the Victorious One declared.
examples.sa: एवं जिनो भणति अप्रतिकूलभाणी यद् अहं इमाय वरपारमिताय आसी । तद व्याकृतोऽहु परापुरुषोत्तमेन बुद्धो भविष्यसि अनागत-अध्वनस्मिन् ॥

examples.dm: Whoever, as a protector, practices this perfection of wisdom, And whoever holds and masters it with devotion, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water; Mara and the factions of Mara will find no opportunity to harm them.
examples.gm: The perfection of wisdom, in which the Protectors practice— Whoever respects, apprehends, and masters it, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water, And Māra and the factions of Māra will find no opportunity against them.
examples.sa: य इमां ग्रहीष्यति पर्यापुणती स नित्यं प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति नाथाः । विष वह्नि शस्त्र उदकं न क्रमाति तस्यो ओतारु मारु न च विन्दति मारपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: Suppose someone were to make offerings to the stūpas Of the Sugatas who have passed into parinirvāṇa, constructing them of the seven precious gems, And were to fill a thousand million buddha-fields With as many stūpas of the Sugatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
examples.gm: If someone, of the completely parinirvāṇized Sugata, Were to build stūpas from the seven precious things and make offerings, and with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the Ganges' Sands, were to fill thousands of millions of fields;
examples.sa: परिनिर्वृतस्य सुगतस्य करेय्य स्तूपां पूजेय सप्तरतनामयु कश्चिद् एव । तेहि प्रपूर्ण सिय क्षेत्रसहस्रकोट्यो यथ गङ्गवालिकसमैः सुगतस्य स्तूपैः ॥

examples.dm: Yet someone were to write down in a book this Mother of the Sugatas, From whom the Ten Powers of the Guides arise, And, bearing it, were to honor it with flowers and ointments, The merit of having worshiped stūpas would not approach even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding that from which the Guides of ten powers will arise, Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book, Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments, The merit of building stūpas and making offerings cannot match a fraction of that.
examples.sa: यश् चो इमां सुगतमात लिखित्व पुस्ते यत उत्पती दशबलान विनायकानाम् । धारेयि सत्करयि पुष्पविलेपनेहि कल पुण्य भोन्ति न स स्तूपि करित्व पूजाम् ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: On whichever path a universal monarch constantly travels, On that very path, the seven precious jewels and all the military hosts follow; Wherever this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors goes, From that very place, all the qualities and dharmas will follow.
examples.gm: Whichever path a Universal Monarch always travels upon, By that very path, the seven precious things and all the troops proceed. Wherever this perfection of wisdom of the Victors goes, Along that very path, all qualities and dharmas will go.
examples.sa: येनैव राज व्रजते स ह चक्रवर्ती तेनैव सप्त रतना बलकाय सर्वे । येनैव प्रज्ञ इय पारमिता जिनानां तेनैव सर्वगुणधर्म समागमन्ति ॥

examples.dm: The Victor, having been asked a question by Śakra, replied: If there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would still take this very Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Victor fully asked Śakra a question, and he replied: "Even if there were buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनेन परिपृच्छितु प्रश्नमाहु सचि गङ्गवालिकसमा सिय बुद्धक्षेत्राः । जिनधातु सर्वि परिपूरित चूडिबद्धा इमम् एव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताहु गृह्णे ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? It is not that I lack respect for the bodily relics; However, because they are completely suffused with wisdom, they are worthy of worship. For example, just as a person who relies on a king receives honor, So too the relics of the Buddha rely upon the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: "If asked why, it is not that I am disrespectful of the bodily relics; But because they are fully permeated by wisdom, they are worshipped. For example, just as a man relying on a king obtains reverence, The relics of the Buddha rely on the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: किं कारणं न मि शरीरि अगौरवत्वं अपि तू खु प्रज्ञपरिभावित पूजयन्ति । यथ राजनिश्रित नरो लभि सर्वि पूजां तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित बुद्धधातुः ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? It is not that I lack respect for the bodily relics; However, because they are completely suffused with wisdom, they are worthy of worship. For example, just as a person who relies on a king receives honor, So too the relics of the Buddha rely upon the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: "If asked why, it is not that I am disrespectful of the bodily relics; But because they are fully permeated by wisdom, they are worshipped. For example, just as a man relying on a king obtains reverence, The relics of the Buddha rely on the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: किं कारणं न मि शरीरि अगौरवत्वं अपि तू खु प्रज्ञपरिभावित पूजयन्ति । यथ राजनिश्रित नरो लभि सर्वि पूजां तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित बुद्धधातुः ॥

examples.dm: A precious jewel, endowed with all qualities and of inestimable value, Is worthy of veneration even when placed within a casket. Even after it has been removed, one still treats the casket with joy; Yet those qualities belong to the precious jewel itself.
examples.gm: "A precious jewel, endowed with all qualities, is priceless; Whichever casket it is placed in is worthy of homage; Even if it is taken out, one takes joy in the casket; Those qualities are those of that precious jewel."
examples.sa: मणिरत्न सर्वि गुणयुक्त अनर्घप्राप्तो यस्मिं करण्डकि भवे स नमस्यनीयः । तस्यापि उद्धृत स्पृहन्ति करण्डकस्मिं तस्यैव ते गुण महारतनस्य भोन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom, The Victors receive worship of their relics even after they have passed into nirvana. Therefore, those who wish to grasp the qualities of the Victors Should take up this perfection of wisdom; it is liberation.
examples.gm: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even though the Victors pass into nirvana, their relics gain worship. Therefore, whoever wishes to hold the qualities of the Victors Should take up the perfection of wisdom; this is liberation.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितागुणानि यन्निर्वृतेऽपि जिनधातु लभन्ति पूजाम् । तस्मा हु तान् जिनगुणा(न्) परिघेत्तुकामो सो प्रज्ञपारमित गृह्णतु एष मोक्षो ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, these five perfections of the Victors Also acquire the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When they are fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, known as "awakening."
examples.gm: Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also Will attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित नामतया भवन्ति । सर्वज्ञताय परिणामयमाण सर्वे षडपीह एकनयम् अर्छति बोधिनामा ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: If no sprout exists, a tree could never grow in the world; In that case, how could branches, flowers, and fruit ever appear? If the mind of enlightenment did not exist, no Victors would ever arise in the world; And if so, how could the fruits—Indra, Brahmā, and the Hearers—ever appear?
examples.gm: If the emergence of a tree in the world never happens without a sprout, How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it? If the emergence of a Victor in the world does not exist without the mind of awakening, How could the fruits of Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas emerge?
examples.sa: असतोऽङ्कुरस्य द्रुमसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शाखपत्रफलपुष्पौपादु तत्र । विन बोधिचित्त जिनसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शक्रब्रह्मफल श्रावकप्रादुभावः ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: Whatever sentient beings there are in this world that provide light, Compared to the light emitted by all of them to illuminate the world, The emergence of a single ray from the sun’s orb is far superior; The light from the host of luminaries cannot match even a fraction of it.
examples.gm: Compared to however many illuminating creatures there are in this world, All emitting their lights in order to illuminate, A single ray of light emitted by the sun's disk is far superior; All the lights of the host of illuminating creatures cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति लोकि क्वचि जोतिकप्राणभूता ओभासनार्थ प्रभ ओसरयन्ति सर्वे । वरसूर्यमण्डलविनिःसृत एकरश्मी न कला पि ज्योतिकगणे सिय सर्व-आभाः ॥

examples.dm: However much the hosts of śrāvakas generate a mass of merit Through being endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, It cannot match even a fraction of a bodhisattva’s single thought of rejoicing; The mass of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Even if however many hosts of śrāvakas generate collections of merit, Fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, Compared to a single mind of rejoicing of a bodhisattva, The heap of merit of the hosts of śrāvakas cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति श्रावकगणाः प्रसवन्ति पुण्यं दानं च शीलमपि भावनसंप्रयुक्तम् । स हि बोधिसत्त्व अनुमोदन एकचित्ते न च सर्वश्रावकगणे सिय पुण्यस्कन्धो ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Buddhas of the past, numbering tens of millions of billions, Who reside in infinitely many billions of fields, and those who have passed into parinirvāṇa, Those protectors of the world, Teach the precious Dharma for the sake of completely ending suffering.
examples.gm: Whatever tens of millions of hundreds of billions of buddhas of the past, And whoever resides in many infinite thousands of tens of millions of fields, And whatever protectors of the world who have passed into nirvāṇa, Demonstrate the precious dharma in order to exhaust suffering:
examples.sa: ये बुद्धकोटिनियुता पुरिमा व्यतीता ये वा अनन्तबहुक्षेत्रसहस्रकोटयः । तिष्ठन्ति येऽपि परिनिर्वृत लोकनाथा देशन्ति धर्मरतनं दुखसंक्षयाय ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: If one understands that these phenomena have ceased and are exhausted, And that which is dedicated is also exhausted, And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon, Then by knowing in such a way, it is a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If in this way one knows that this dharma has ceased and is exhausted, And that to which it is dedicated is also exhausted, And knows that a dharma is never dedicated to a dharma, Through knowing in that way, it is perfectly dedicated.
examples.sa: सचि एव जानति निरुध्यति क्षीणधर्मा तच्चैत क्षीण परिणामयिष्यन्ति यत्र । न च धर्म धर्मि परिणामयते कदाचित् परिणामितं भवति एव प्रजानमाने ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: If one dedicates merit to enlightenment in this way, One is "poison-free," does not forsake the Buddha, and speaks what the Victors have taught. The hero who dedicates in this way outshines All those bodhisattvas in the world who engage in conceptual apprehension.
examples.gm: If one perfectly dedicates merit to awakening in that way, It is without poison, one does not abandon the Buddha, and speaks what the Victor has spoken. Dedicating perfectly in that way, the hero outshines all Of however many bodhisattvas there are in the world who possess apprehension.
examples.sa: एवं च पुण्य परिणामयमान बोधौ न च सो हि बुद्ध क्षिपते जिन उक्तवादी । यावन्ति लोकि उपलम्भिकबोधिसत्त्वा अभिभोन्ति सर्वि परिणामयमान शूरो ॥

examples.dm: When conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, as well as white and black dharmas, Have been thoroughly deconstructed by wisdom so that not even an atom is observed, That is accounted as the perfection of wisdom in the world; It is just like space, which does not abide in anything at all.
examples.gm: When conditioned, unconditioned, and white and black dharmas Are broken down by wisdom and not even a particle is apprehended, In the world it is reckoned as the perfection of wisdom; It is like space, which does not abide anywhere at all.
examples.sa: यद धर्म संस्कृत असंस्कृत कृष्णशुक्लो अणुमात्रु नो लभति प्रज्ञ विभावमानः । यद प्रज्ञपारमित गच्छति संख्य लोके आकाश यत्र न प्रतिष्ठितु किंचि तत्र ॥

examples.dm: Even if one has honored billions of Buddhas in former lives, If one lacks faith in the Victors' perfection of wisdom, That person of small intelligence, upon hearing it, will reject it; Having rejected it, they become defenseless and go to the Unrelenting Hell.
examples.gm: Even if they honored hundreds of billions of buddhas when practicing previously, If they do not have faith in the perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Upon hearing it, those of small intelligence will abandon it; Having abandoned it, becoming without refuge, they go to the Avīci hell.
examples.sa: सत्कृत्य बुद्धनियुतां परिचारिकायां न च प्रज्ञपारमित श्रद्दधिता जिनानाम् । श्रुत्वा च सो इमु क्षिपिष्यति सोऽल्पबुद्धिः स क्षिपित्व यास्यति अवीचिम् अत्राणभूतो ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, if you wish to attain the supreme primordial wisdom of a Buddha, Have faith in this Mother of the Victors. For example, it would be unfitting to be like a merchant who, Having traveled to an island of jewels, returns home with his goods exhausted.
examples.gm: Therefore, if the supreme pristine wisdom of a buddha One wishes to touch, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! For example, having gone to the island of jewels, a merchant Returning bereft of goods—it is not fitting to become like that.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु श्रद्दधत एव जिनान मातां यदि इच्छथा स्पृशितु उत्तमबुद्धज्ञानम् । सो वाणिजो यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं मूलातु छेदन करित्व पुन आगमेया ॥

examples.dm: One should understand that the purity of form is the purity of the fruition; The purity of the fruition and the purity of form become the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruition, and the purity of form Are like the element of space—indivisible and inseparable.
examples.gm: The purity of form should be known as the purity of the fruit; The purity of the fruit and form becomes the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form Are equal to the realm of space, indivisible and unseverable.
examples.sa: रूपस्य शुद्धि फलशुद्धित वेदितव्या फलरूपशुद्धित सर्वज्ञतशुद्धिम् आहुः । सर्वज्ञताय फलशुद्धित रूपशुद्धी आकाशधातुसमताय अभिन्नछिन्नाः ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: These beings are stuck in the mire of name and form; They wander in the wheel of cyclic existence, which is like a wheel driven by wind. Knowing that deluded beings are like deer caught in a snare, Those endowed with wisdom move through the sky like birds.
examples.gm: These wandering beings are attached to the mud of name and form; They wander in the wheel of samsara like a wheel of wind. Knowing that deluded beings are like deer caught in a snare, The wise one roams like a bird in the sky.
examples.sa: नामेव रूपि जगती अयु पङ्कसक्ता संसारचक्रि भ्रमतेऽनिलचक्रतुल्ये । जानित्व भ्रान्तु जगती मृगवागुरेव आकाश पक्षिसदृशा विचरन्ति प्रज्ञाः ॥

examples.dm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva who practices in this way, Having severed attachment, moves through the world without clinging, Like the sun shining brightly when freed from the eclipse of Rāhu, Or like a fire that blazes, consuming grass, wood, and forests.
examples.gm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva practicing like that, Having cut off attachment, goes among beings without attachment, Remaining brightly like the sun freed from the eclipse of Rāhu, And like a spreading fire burning grass, trees, and forests.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो सङ्गा उछिन्नु व्रजते जगती असक्तो । सूर्यो व राहुग्रहमुक्त विरोचमानो अग्नीव युक्त तृणकाष्ठवनं दहाति ॥

examples.dm: When a bodhisattva, through the perfection of wisdom, sees That all phenomena are naturally pure and utterly pristine, They do not perceive an agent, nor do they perceive any phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: All dharmas being naturally pure and entirely pure, If the bodhisattva views the perfection of wisdom, Not apprehending an agent and not apprehending all dharmas, This is practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: प्रकृतीय शुद्ध परिशुद्धिमि सर्वधर्मां प्रज्ञाय पारमित पश्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । न च पश्यकं लभति नापि च सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The fourth chapter explains the complete realization of all aspects. Śakra, the king of the gods, asked the Victor: "How do Bodhisattvas practicing wisdom apply diligence?" "They do not apply even a particle of diligence toward the aggregates or the elements; Not applying diligence toward the aggregates is the Bodhisattva's diligence."
examples.gm: The fourth chapter: teaching the complete realization of all aspects. The king of gods, Śakra, asked the Victor: "How does a bodhisattva strive in the practice of wisdom?" "They do not strive even a speck of dust in the aggregates and elements; Not striving in the aggregates, that is the striving of a bodhisattva."
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनस्य परिपृच्छति देवराजो चरमाण प्रज्ञ कथ युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । अणुमात्र यो न खलु युज्यति स्कन्धधातौ यो एव युज्यति स युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वः ॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, having heard that these phenomena are like emanations and illusions, Is without doubt and repeatedly practices the training, Know that such a person has long since entered the Mahayana, And has performed service to many tens of billions of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whoever, having heard that these dharmas are like emanations and illusions, Without doubt, trains and continuously applies themselves, That being should be known to have entered the Great Vehicle long ago, And to have served many tens of millions of billions of Buddhas.
examples.sa: चिरयानप्रस्थितु स वेदयितव्य सत्त्वो बहुबुद्धकोटिनयुतेहि कृताधिकारो । यो श्रुत्व धर्मि इमि निर्मितमायकल्पां न च काङ्क्षते अयु प्रयुज्यति शिक्षमाणः ॥

examples.dm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the Buddha-qualities, Nor do they conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, awakening, or peace. They practice through the blessing of non-conceptuality, free from mental construction; This is the practice of the supreme Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the qualities of a Buddha; They do not conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, or peaceful enlightenment; Non-conceptualizing and free from concepts, they practice through blessing; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु यो न इह कल्पयि बुद्धधर्मां बल ऋद्धिपाद न च कल्पयि बोधि शान्ताम् । अविकल्पकल्पविगतोऽधिष्ठानचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Subhūti asked the Buddha, the Moon of Speakers: "What are the obstacles for those who delight in virtuous qualities?" The Teacher replied: "The obstacles that will arise are many; Of those, I shall briefly describe just a few."
examples.gm: Subhūti asked the Buddha, the moon among speakers: What are the obstacles for those who delight in qualities? The Teacher replied: There are many obstacles; Of those, I will fully explain just a few for now.
examples.sa: बुद्धं सुभूति परिपृच्छति वादिचन्द्रं क्यन्तन्तरायु भविष्यन्ति गुणे रतानाम् । बहु अन्तरायु भविष्यन्ति भणाति शास्त ततु अल्पमात्र परिकीर्तयिष्यामि तावत् ॥

examples.dm: When writing down this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Various and diverse kinds of flashes of inspiration will arise; Yet if, without having benefited sentient beings, they vanish as swiftly as lightning, This complete deterioration is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: When copying this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Various differing modes of confidence will arise; Yet without accomplishing the benefit of beings, swiftly like lightning, They will completely fade away; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: प्रतिभान नेक विविधानि उपपद्यिष्यन्ति लिखमान प्रज्ञ इमु पारमिता जिनानाम् । युत शीघ्र विद्युत यथा परिहायिष्यन्ति अकरित्व अर्थ जगती इमु मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: When this is explained, some will harbor doubts, thinking: "The Leader has not even mentioned my name here; He has not mentioned my family, my level, or my lineage." This is the work of Māra, causing them to reject it rather than listen.
examples.gm: When this is taught, some will harbor doubts, thinking, 'The Leader has not fully pronounced my name here, Nor fully pronounced my lineage, birthplace, or clan.' They will not listen and will abandon it; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: काङ्क्षा च केषचि भविष्यति भाषमाणे न ममात्र नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन । न च जाति भूमि परिकीर्तितु नापि गोत्रं न च सो श्रुणिष्यति क्षिपिष्यति मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Not knowing this, they abandon the root, And in their delusion, they search for the branches and leaves. It is just like finding an elephant and then searching for its tracks; Such is the case for those who have heard the Perfection of Wisdom but still search for other sūtras.
examples.gm: Not knowing thus, having discarded the root, Out of delusion they will search for branches and leaves. It is like finding an elephant but searching for the elephant's footprints; Having heard the perfection of wisdom, searching for other sūtras is just like that.
examples.sa: एवं त मूलमपहाय अजानमानो शाखापलाश परिएषयिष्यन्ति मूढाः । हस्तिं लभित्व यथ हस्तिपदं गवेषे तथ प्रज्ञपारमित श्रुत्व सूत्रान्त एषेत् ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Those who, at that time, have become longing and faithful, Having gone to listen to this sublime Dharma, Once they perceive the Dharma preacher to be preoccupied, They will depart without joy and with a troubled mind.
examples.gm: Those who at that time, having become eager and faithful, Go to listen to this holy dharma, Upon knowing that the speaker of dharma is busy with activities, Will depart, devoid of joy and unhappy.
examples.sa: ये चापि तस्मि समये इमु धर्म श्रेष्ठं श्रुणनाय छन्दिक उत्पादयिष्यन्ति श्रद्धाम् । ते धर्मभाणक विदित्वन कार्ययुक्तं प्रेमापनीत गमिष्यन्ति सुदुर्मनाश्च ॥

examples.gm: Those who at that time, having become eager and faithful, Go to listen to this holy dharma, Upon knowing that the speaker of dharma is busy with activities, Will depart, devoid of joy and unhappy.

examples.dm: At that time, these activities of Māra will occur. At that time, after many monks have been stirred to agitation, Many other various obstacles will also arise, Which prevent them from upholding this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: At that time, this work of Māra will arise: At that time, whoever disturbs many monks, They will not uphold this perfection of wisdom; And many other various obstacles will also arise.
examples.sa: इमि मारकर्म भविष्यन्ति य तस्मि काले अन्ये च नेक विविधा बहु अन्तराया । येही समाकुलिकृता बहु भिक्षु तत्र प्रज्ञाय पारमित एतु न धारयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: For those small-minded beings who have newly entered the vehicle, If they have not attained this rare and precious jewel, Mara will strive to create obstacles for them; The Buddhas of the ten directions apply themselves to protecting them.
examples.gm: Sentient beings of small intellect who have newly entered the vehicle, Who have not found this rare jewel— In order to create obstacles for them, Māra will become energetic; But the Buddhas of the ten directions will apply themselves to fully protecting them.
examples.sa: नवयानप्रस्थित स सत्त्व परीत्तबुद्धिः य इमं दुर्लाभु धर्मरतनं परापुणन्ति । मारोऽत्र उत्सुकु भविष्यति अन्तराये बुद्धा दशद्दिशि परिग्रहसंप्रयुक्ताः ॥

examples.dm: When a mother falls ill, though she has many children, They all become distressed and perform healing rites for her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions Direct their intention toward this supreme Perfection of Wisdom, who is their mother.
examples.gm: When a mother becomes sick and has many sons, They all become unhappy and attend upon her. Likewise, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions also Keep in mind this holy wisdom, which is their mother.
examples.sa: मात्राय पुत्र बहु सन्ति गिलानि काये ते सर्वि दुर्मनस तत्र प्रयुज्ययेयुः । एमेव बुद्धपिं दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात्र समन्वाहरन्ति ॥

examples.dm: When a mother falls ill, though she has many children, They all become distressed and perform healing rites for her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions Direct their intention toward this supreme Perfection of Wisdom, who is their mother.
examples.gm: When a mother becomes sick and has many sons, They all become unhappy and attend upon her. Likewise, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions also Keep in mind this holy wisdom, which is their mother.
examples.sa: मात्राय पुत्र बहु सन्ति गिलानि काये ते सर्वि दुर्मनस तत्र प्रयुज्ययेयुः । एमेव बुद्धपिं दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात्र समन्वाहरन्ति ॥

examples.dm: All those who have passed, the current Protectors of the worlds of the ten directions, And those who will arise in the future, all emerge from her. She is the Mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental activities of other sentient beings.
examples.gm: Those protectors of the world in the past and in the ten directions, And those who will appear in future times, arise from this. She is the mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental conduct of other sentient beings.
examples.sa: येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत भविष्यन्त्य् अनागताश् च । लोकस्य दर्शिक जनेत्रि जिनान माता परसत्त्वचित्तचरितान निदर्शिता(का) च ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as a lion dwelling in a mountain glen is fearless, And its roar strikes terror into many small wild animals, So too the Lion among men, by relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, Terrifies the many non-Buddhists and lets out his roar throughout the world.
examples.gm: For example, just as a fearless lion dwelling in a mountain ravine Terrifies many small wild animals and lets out a roar, The lion of men, relying on the perfection of wisdom, Terrifies many tīrthikas and also lets out a roar in the world.
examples.sa: सिंहो यथैव गिरिकन्दरि निश्रयित्वा नदते अछम्भि मृग क्षुद्रक त्रासयन्तो । तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रय नराण सिंहो नदते अछम्भि पृथुतीर्थिक त्रासयन्तो ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the rays of the sun abiding in the sky Dry up the earth and make forms clearly visible, Likewise, the Dharma King, relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, Dries up the river of craving and perfectly teaches the Dharma.
examples.gm: For example, just as the rays of the sun dwelling in the sky Dry up this earth and also clearly reveal forms, Likewise, the dharma king, relying on the perfection of wisdom, Dries up the river of craving and also clearly reveals the dharma.
examples.sa: आकाशनिश्रित यथैव हि सूर्यरश्मि तापेतिमां धरणि दर्शयते च रूपम् । तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित धर्मराजो तापेति तृष्णनदि धर्म निदर्शयाति ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.
examples.sa: रूपस्य दर्शनु अदर्शनु वेदनाये संज्ञाय दर्शनु अदर्शनु चेतनाये । विज्ञानचित्तमनुदर्शनु यत्र नास्ति अय धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्टु तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.

examples.dm: Sentient beings speak the words, "I see space," But how can space be seen? Examine the meaning of this. The Tathāgata taught that the seeing of phenomena is also like that; Such seeing cannot be described by any other analogy.
examples.gm: Sentient beings express in words, "Space is seen"; Examine this meaning: how is space seen? The Tathāgata has taught that seeing the dharma is like that; Seeing cannot be explained by any other example.
examples.sa: आकाश दृष्टु इति सत्त्व प्रव्याहरन्ति नभदर्शनं कुतु विमृष्यथ एतम् अर्थम् । तथ धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्ट तथागतेन न हि दर्शनं भणितु शक्य निदर्शनेन ॥

examples.dm: Whoever sees in that way sees all phenomena. Just as a king remains impartial while his ministers perform all the tasks, Whatever activities of the Buddhas and teachings of the Śrāvakas there may be, The Perfection of Wisdom performs them all.
examples.gm: Whoever sees in that way sees all dharmas. Just as a king sits in equanimity while his ministers do everything, Whatever deeds of the Buddhas and dharmas of the śrāvakas there are, All of them are done by the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यो एव पश्यति स पश्यति सर्वधर्मान् सर्वान् अमात्यकिरिया ति उपेक्ष्य राजा । यावन्ति बुद्धक्रिय धर्मत श्रावकाणां प्रज्ञाय पारमित सर्व करोति तानि ॥

examples.dm: Those who have firm faith in the Sugatas and bodhisattvas, And whose intentions are focused on the supreme perfection of wisdom, Having completely transcended the two levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, May they swiftly attain the unassailable awakening of the Victors.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva has firm faith in the Sugata, And applies their mind to the supreme perfection of wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, Will quickly attain the unconquerable enlightenment of the Victors.
examples.sa: यस्यामि श्रद्ध सुगते दृढ बोधिसत्त्वो वरप्रज्ञपारमित आशयसंप्रयोगो । अतिक्रम्य भूमिद्वय श्रावकप्रत्ययानां लघु प्राप्स्यते अनभिभू(तु) जिनान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those endowed with faith who have attained confidence, Do not fail to follow the Mother, the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Likewise, whoever is endowed with faith and has obtained pure trust, But does not follow the mother, the perfection of wisdom,
examples.sa: एमेव श्रद्धसंगतो य प्रसादप्राप्तो प्रज्ञाय पारमित मात्र विवर्जयन्ति । संसारसागर तदा सद संसरन्ति जातीजरामरणशोकतरंगभङ्गे ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those endowed with faith who have attained confidence, Do not fail to follow the Mother, the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Likewise, whoever is endowed with faith and has obtained pure trust, But does not follow the mother, the perfection of wisdom,
examples.sa: एमेव श्रद्धसंगतो य प्रसादप्राप्तो प्रज्ञाय पारमित मात्र विवर्जयन्ति । संसारसागर तदा सद संसरन्ति जातीजरामरणशोकतरंगभङ्गे ॥

examples.dm: For those bodhisattvas who abide on the level of a beginner, And have entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha with a resolute intention, Those excellent students who possess devotion for their gurus Should always rely upon wise masters.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva abiding on the ground of a beginner, Who has set out for the supreme enlightenment of a Buddha with a pure intention, As good disciples possessing devotion to their guru, They should always rely on wise gurus.
examples.sa: यो आदिकर्म स्थितु भूमिय बोधिसत्त्वो अध्याशयेन वर प्रस्थित बुद्धबोधिम् । तेही सुशिष्यगुरुगौरवसंप्रयुक्तो कल्याणमित्र सद सेवयितव्य विज्ञैः ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.

examples.dm: Those of great renown don the armor of difficult deeds, Which is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources. They are free from the concept of the three vehicles and have no grasping; They are irreversible, unwavering, and possess the quality of being imperturbable.
examples.gm: Those endowed with great renown don the armor that is difficult to do; It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. They are free from the perception of the three vehicles and have no grasping. They are irreversible, unwavering, and of unperturbed nature.
examples.sa: संनाहु दुष्करू महायशु संनहन्ती न च स्कन्धधातु न च आयतनैः सनद्धाः । त्रिभि यानसंज्ञविगता अपरिगृहीता अविवर्तिका अचलिताश्च अकोप्यधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Those who possess such qualities are free from conceptual elaboration; Free from doubt, hesitation, and uncertainty, they are endowed with the true meaning. Having heard the perfection of wisdom, they do not shrink back; They do not rely on others and should be known as irreversible.
examples.gm: They are endowed with such dharmas and are free from conceptual proliferation. They are free from doubt, hesitation, and wavering, and possess the ultimate meaning. Those who, having heard the perfection of wisdom, do not shrink back, Should be known as irreversible and not reliant on others.
examples.sa: ते एव धर्मसमुदागत निष्प्रपञ्चा काङ्क्षाविलेखविमतीविगतार्थयुक्ताः । प्रज्ञाय पारमित श्रुत्व न सीदयन्ति अपरप्रणेय अविवर्तिय वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: This Dharma of the Leaders is profound and difficult to see; It is not something realized by anyone, nor is it something to be attained. Therefore, the Compassionate Benefactor, having attained awakening, Felt little concern, thinking, "Who among the masses of beings will understand?"
examples.gm: This dharma of the Guides is profound and difficult to see; It is not realized by anyone, nor is it to be attained. Therefore, the Benefactor, the Compassionate One, having discovered enlightenment, Showed little inclination, thinking, "Who among the multitudes of beings will understand?"
examples.sa: गम्भीर धर्म अयु दुर्दृशु नायकानां न च केनचीदधिगतो न च प्रापुणन्ति । एतार्थु बोधिमधिगम्य हितानुकम्पी अल्पोत्सुको क इमु ज्ञास्यति सत्त्वकायो ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings delight in foundations and desire sense objects; Abiding in grasping, they are unskilled, foolish, and deluded like darkness. The phenomena to be attained are without foundation and without grasping; Therefore, conflict with the world arises.
examples.gm: Beings delight in resting places and desire sense objects; Abiding in grasping, the unwise are foolish and obscured like darkness. The dharma to be attained is without resting place and without grasping; Therefore, conflict arises with the worlds.
examples.sa: सत्त्वश् च आलयरतो विषयाभिलाषी स्थित अग्रहे अबुध यो महअन्धभूतो । धर्मो अनालयु अनाग्रहु प्रापितव्यो लोकेन सार्ध अयु विग्रहु प्रादुभूतो ॥

examples.dm: Just as a bird with a massive body of one hundred and fifty yojanas, If its wings are exhausted and it lacks strength and skill, Even if it leaps from the Abode of the Thirty-Three to this world of Jambudvīpa, It will surely meet with disaster and ruin.
examples.gm: If a bird with a large body of one hundred and fifty yojanas, Whose wings are worn out, lacks strength and skill, And jumps from the abode of the Thirty-Three to this Jambudvīpa, In jumping itself, it will come to ruin there.
examples.sa: पक्षिस्य योजनशतं महतात्मभावो पञ्चाशता पि अबलोभयक्षीणपक्षो । सो त्रायत्रिंशभवनादिषु जम्बुद्वीपे आत्मानमोसरियि तं विलयं व्रजेय्या ॥

examples.dm: Even if these five perfections of the Victors were practiced For many tens of billions of eons, And one constantly relied upon infinite and vast aspirations within the world, Without skillful means and separated from wisdom, one falls into the level of a śrāvaka.
examples.gm: Even if these five perfections of the Victors Have been accomplished for many koṭis of niyutas of eons, And one has constantly relied on the world with boundless, vast aspirations, Lacking skillful means and devoid of wisdom, one will fall into the level of a śrāvaka.
examples.sa: यद्य् आपि पञ्च इम पारमिता जिनानां बहुकल्पकोटिनियुतां समुदानयेय्या । प्रणिधीननन्तविपुलां सद सेव्य लोके अनुपाय प्रज्ञविकला परि श्रावकत्वे ॥

examples.dm: Whoever wishes to set forth in this Buddha vehicle Should train with an even mind toward all beings, the recognition of them as parents, A helpful attitude, and a loving heart, Being without harshness, remaining straightforward, and speaking gentle words.
examples.gm: Whoever desires to definitely emerge in this vehicle of the Buddha, With an even mind toward all beings, perceiving them as parents, Should act with an attitude of benefit and a mind of loving-kindness, Be free from rigidity, straightforward, and speak gentle words.
examples.sa: निर्यायनाय य इच्छति बुद्धज्ञाने समचित्त सर्वजगती पितृमातृसंज्ञा । हितचित्त मैत्रमन एव पराक्रमेय्या अखिलार्जवो मृदुगिराय पराक्रमेय्या ॥

examples.dm: Thus did the elder Subhūti request of the Protector of the World: "Please explain the signs of the ocean of qualities free from afflictions, And how those of great power do not turn back; O Victor, please grant a prophecy regarding even a mere portion of such qualities."
examples.gm: The elder Subhūti thoroughly requested the Protector of the World: "Ocean of Qualities, please teach the signs of those free from afflictions. How those of great power will not turn back again— Thus, may the Victor explain just a fraction of their qualities."
examples.sa: स्थविरो सुभूति परिपृच्छति लोकनाथं अरणाय लिङ्ग भणही गुणसागराणाम् । अविवर्तिया यथ भवन्ति महानुभावा तां व्याकुरुष्व जिनगुणान प्रदेशमात्रम् ॥

examples.dm: They are free from the perception of diversity and speak words consistent with reason; They do not rely on other śramaṇas or brahmins. These wise ones have forever abandoned the three lower realms; They are intensely devoted to the paths of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.gm: Free from differentiated perceptions and speaking rational words, Not relying on other śramaṇas and brahmins; The wise always abandon the three lower realms at all times, And vividly strive in the path of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.sa: नानात्वसंज्ञविगता गिर युक्तभाणी न च अन्य ते श्रमण ब्राह्मण आश्रयन्ति । त्रियपायवर्जित विदू सदकालि भोन्ति दशभिश् च ते कुशलकर्मपथेभि युक्ता ॥

examples.dm: They teach the Dharma to beings without any regard for material gain. They take singular delight in the Dharma and always speak with gentle words. They possess constant alertness while moving, walking, sleeping, and sitting. They walk while looking only a yoke-length ahead, keeping the mind free from delusion.
examples.gm: Without material motives, they subsequently teach the dharma to beings. Singly rejoicing in the dharma, they are always endowed with gentle words. They are fully endowed with clear comprehension when going, walking, sleeping, and sitting. Looking ahead only the distance of a yoke, they walk without a wandering mind.
examples.sa: धर्मं निरामिषु जगस्यनुशासयन्ति एकान्तधर्मनियताः सद स्निग्धवाक्याः । स्थितिचंक्रमं शयनिषद्य सुसंप्रजाना युगमात्रप्रेक्षिण व्रजन्त्य् अभ्रान्तचिन्ता ॥

examples.dm: Pure and wearing clean robes, they are pure in the three isolations; They do not desire gain, and like great bulls, they always long for the Dharma. They have transcended the realm of Māra and are not dependent on others; They meditate on the four concentrations, yet do not dwell within those concentrations.
examples.gm: Making themselves clean and wearing clean clothes, the three are isolated and pure; Without desire for gain, the supreme leaders always desire the dharma. Passed beyond the realm of Māra and not placing themselves under the control of others, Meditating on the four dhyānas, they do not abide in those dhyānas.
examples.sa: शुचिशौचअम्बरधरा त्रिविवेकशुद्धा न च लाभकाम वृषभा सद धर्मकामाः । मारस्यतीतविषया अपरप्रणेया चतुध्यानध्यायि न च निश्रित तत्र ध्याने ॥

examples.dm: They do not desire fame, and their minds are not entangled by anger. Even if they live as householders, they are always without attachment to any material things. For the sake of their livelihood, they do not seek out vast possessions. They do not practice wrathful spells of violence, nor do they practice spells for union with women.
examples.gm: Not desiring fame, their minds are not wrapped by anger. Even if they are householders, they are always unattached to all things. For the sake of livelihood, they do not seek resources through appalling means. They do not practice mantras of fierce actions, nor mantras for uniting men and women.
examples.sa: न च कीर्तिकाम न च क्रोधपरीतचित्ता गृहिभूत नित्य अनध्योषित सर्व वस्तुं । न च जीविकाविषयभोग गवेषयन्ति अभिचारमन्त्र न च इस्त्रिप्रयोगमन्त्राः ॥

For the sake of their livelihood, they do not seek out vast possessions. They do not practice wrathful spells of violence, nor do they practice spells for union with women.

For the sake of livelihood, they do not seek resources through appalling means. They do not practice mantras of fierce actions, nor mantras for uniting men and women.
